### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED then REVERTED same session (Claude Code, interactive — followed the docs pass into the precompute defect) — the trust board's 999 failure sentinel is UNREACHABLE on a timeout; the obvious fix trades a bounded failure for an unbounded one

**What (net prod change: ZERO — applied, measured, reverted, verified):** three migrations,
`audit_20260815_thp_legs_catch_query_canceled` → `audit_20260815_thp_sentinel_helper_revoke_anon_auth`
→ `audit_20260815_revert_thp_legs_catch_query_canceled`. All eight `rpc_thp_leg_*` functions are back
on `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`, the helper `rpc_thp_sentinel_failures_since` is dropped, and
`rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh_p()` is byte-restored. Verified after revert: 8/8 legs restored,
0 still carrying the change, 8/8 still SECURITY DEFINER, helper gone, procedure no longer references
it, `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` **0**, `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**,
`check_anon_write_surface()` **0 rows**.

⚠ **The DEFECT is real and is now deliberately unfixed.** Every leg carries an `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`
handler that exists to write the **999 sentinel**, and PostgreSQL excludes `QUERY_CANCELED` from
`OTHERS`, which is exactly what `statement_timeout` raises (57014). Verified: `WHEN OTHERS` did NOT
catch a raised 57014; `WHEN query_canceled OR OTHERS` did; and `where value = 999` returns **zero rows,
ever**. So a timed-out leg writes neither its value nor its sentinel — it keeps the OLD value AND the
OLD `computed_at`, and aborts the CALL, skipping every downstream leg. `v_rpc_trust_health` shows no
per-metric age, so the board publishes a stale number as current. Only `trust_precompute_max_age_hours`
(breach 13, read 15.14) noticed.

⚠ **Why the fix was reverted — three measurements I did not have before applying:** (1) a
function-level `SET statement_timeout` does NOT bind statements inside it (300 ms declared,
`pg_sleep(5)` completed), so the legs' declared 60–480 s budgets are **all inert** — **second instance
of that trap today**, after `8918307c` on the drain seeders; (2) the real budget is `cron_heavy`'s
role-level **600 s shared by the whole CALL** — legs 1–7 burned **517 s**, leg 8 needed ~78 s and got
~83 s, so it is stalest **by position** and optimizing its query fixes nothing; (3) decisively, **after
a cancel is caught the timer is NOT re-armed** — probe at 500 ms, second `pg_sleep(3)` ran to
completion (`TAIL_UNBOUNDED ran_for=3.50s`). So catching buys a reachable sentinel at the price of
running every remaining leg **unbounded**, holding a connection on the 2 GB instance whose saturation
caused the timeout. plpgsql cannot re-arm mid-statement, so no in-procedure variant is safe.

⚠ **Security lesson, and it is the CONVERSE of the one already in CLAUDE.md:** `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM
PUBLIC` alone was **not sufficient** — Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants EXECUTE to `anon` +
`authenticated` as explicit acl rows, so the new helper measured `has_function_privilege('anon', …) =
true` and drift went **0 → 1**. Fixed within minutes by revoking both halves. **The `proacl` text looked
clean** (the PUBLIC row really was gone) — which is why the rule is to verify with
`has_function_privilege()`.

⚠ **A name-trap nearly produced the opposite mechanism:** `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh` (FUNCTION,
13,009 chars, **zero callers anywhere**, `impossible_parallel` = leg **1**) vs
`rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh_p` (PROCEDURE, 492 chars, the scheduled one, same leg = **8**).
**Read `cron.job.command`, not the name.**

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the drain route's 20:30Z tick finally named the step, and the filed fix was aimed at the wrong thing

**What.** `drain-conflated-subeditions` has been killed at `maxDuration` on every tick since 2026-07-31. The 20:30Z tick today was the first to carry the progressive `mark()` from `80e99d4d`, and it settled it: `seed_miskeyed` **120,310 ms** · `seed_recent` **120,326 ms** · `seed_knot_occupants` **120,393 ms** (on a `p_limit` of **200**) · `seed_conflated` 16,946 ms · trigger 430 ms, `last_step = onchain_resolve_trigger`.

Three steps converging on ~120,3xx ms is a CEILING, not work. ⚠ **CORRECTED — WHICH ceiling is undetermined, and the attribution in the first version of this entry was wrong.** These functions do each declare `statement_timeout=120s` in `proconfig`, and I read that as binding because `service_role` carries 30s; but the **server default is ALSO exactly 120000 ms** (`/etc/postgresql-custom/platform-defaults.conf`, no db-level or `<ALL ROLES>` override), so the two are numerically indistinguishable. Prod controls say proconfig cannot RAISE the caller's budget, making the session default the likelier parent. **Raising these functions' proconfig would therefore do nothing** — the levers are the caller's budget or making the work fit, which is what this change does. A statement that hits it **rolls back** — so those three burned **361 s of a 600 s budget and produced nothing**, and the route was killed before reaching the steps that do the work.

Measured cost of that ordering: `resolve_topshot_subedition_collision_knots` (step 6) had **not executed once since 2026-07-31 20:33:53Z** — 76 resolutions ever, the newest stamped the exact minute of the last completed run, i.e. **15.0 days**, while knots arrive at ~+8.3/night (~124 accrued undrained).

**Fix — DRAIN before SEED, plus a wall-clock budget guard.** Order is now catalog → split → realign → **knots** → conflation_guard → seeds → on-chain trigger. The drain steps CONSUME what prior ticks resolved and the seeds FEED later ticks (the route header has always said so, and step 6 "derives its own candidates and does not read this queue"), so there is no intra-tick seed→drain dependency — the reorder changes throughput, never correctness, and every step is idempotent and cursor-driven. `knots` moved ahead of the conflation guard deliberately: the guard is a pure re-measurement and so is the cheapest thing to drop under pressure, and leaving knots last is exactly what let 15 days of starvation read as normal operation. No step may now START without room to hit its own 120 s ceiling and still write the completion row; a declined step lands in `extra.skipped_steps` rather than vanishing.

⚠ **This corrects the filed remedy.** Deep-audit R7 prescribed "split the 6 steps so each writes its own row and commits per step" — a large restructure of TopShot keying, the thing every edition-keyed FMV derives from — and it does not address the actual defect, which is that the three steps that time out ran FIRST and starved the rest. ⚠ R7's stated IMPACT was also wrong and is already corrected in Known issues #18: the conflation guard is **0.0 days stale** (it has a second caller, pg_cron jobid 62), so a session acting on R7 as filed would have fixed nothing.

**Guard.** `__tests__/pipeline-start-marker-duration-is-not-a-measurement.test.ts` gains an ordering pin — `knots` must precede every `seed_*` step, and `skipped_steps` must exist — because ordering here is load-bearing, not stylistic. Its existing `mark()`-call-site count was **repointed, not weakened**: it required >5 literal `mark(` sites, a proxy for "every step persists progress" that pinned the implementation; marking now lives inside the `step()` helper, which enforces the same property more strongly (a step cannot forget to mark) and reddened the guard on a correct refactor. Three mutations, each reddening only its own assertion: swapping `knots` behind the seeders, renaming `out.skipped_steps`, and dropping the `await` on `mark()`.

**Verified.** `tsc` clean · full primary suite **12,003 passed / 1,215 files**; the 4 failing files (7 tests: `api-ingest-backfill`, `metadata-catch-branch-is-not-a-404`, `worker-moments-hydrator-handler`, `worker-pack-events-ingest`) reproduce **identically at HEAD with these changes stashed**, so they are the documented local-env class, not this change. ⚠ Not verified by a live tick — the next 20:30Z run is the proof, and what to read is `extra.step_ms` plus a non-zero `knots` and a shrinking gap in `topshot_collision_knot_resolutions`.

**Revert:** `git revert 3a172b6b` (route + guard). No DB, migration, cron, auth, secret, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing-math change.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — a PUBLIC board told collectors "No +EV packs right now." out of its own 503, and a rewards read published "No referrals yet" from a failed count

- **Two code fixes + two tests.** No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no FMV/pricing math.
- **Found by the method this repo documents rather than by reading fetch code:** sweep the empty-state COPY on client pages. `app/insights/pack-reality/page.tsx` is PUBLIC and its `error` state was consulted by **exactly ONE of five claim sites** (the pull-value distribution), so a 503 rendered "Failed to load: HTTP 503" in that section while **"No +EV packs right now."**, **"No qualifying packs yet."** and a hard **"0 positive-EV TS packs"** sat directly below it — the page contradicting itself, and the +EV ranker is a buy/no-buy input. Verified empirically with a throwaway probe before changing anything; all three strings confirmed present on a 503.
- ⚠ **THE EXISTING TEST DESCRIBED THE CONTRACT AND DID NOT ENFORCE IT.** `component-insights-client-pages-deep` already had a case whose comment read *"an outage must not render as 'no positive-EV packs exist right now', which is a claim about the market"* — and asserted only `toMatch(/HTTP 500|error|failed/i)`, i.e. that a failure was mentioned SOMEWHERE. Both can be true at once, and were. **Assert what the READER SEES, not that a failure was mentioned.** Same shape as the `f02362c7` panini case (asserted what the function returns, never what the reader sees).
- **Second instance, server-side and independent:** `/api/rewards/summary` returned `referralCount: referrals.count ?? 0`. **supabase-js RETURNS errors rather than throwing**, so a failed count (a `57014` statement timeout is the realistic case on this instance) yields `count: null` → a hard **0 at HTTP 200** → `/rewards` renders **"No referrals yet — be the first to share."** to a collector who may have referred friends and earned the credits. A claim about the reader's OWN account, same class as the `/alerts` fix. Now `null` end-to-end (the client's own `?? 0` would have undone it, and `InviteBlock`'s prop is typed nullable so a caller cannot pass a failed read as a zero).
- ⚠ **Both fixes pinned in BOTH directions, which is the load-bearing half.** An empty board and a genuinely-zero referral count are HONEST answers and must keep rendering as such — a fix that blanks every empty state into "unavailable" just moves the dishonesty and cries wolf on the system working. Mutation-proven: disabling `loadFailed` reds the board test and reproduces the original DOM verbatim; restoring `?? 0` reds the rewards test (`expected +0 to be null`).
- ⚠ **A mock bug nearly hid the second fix — my new test failed against an already-correct route.** The rewards suite's supabase stub returned a shared singleton from `from()`, and the route builds ~9 chains synchronously inside one `Promise.all`, so a single mutable `table` field was overwritten by every later `.from()` before any `then` settled — every chain resolved as the LAST table. `from()` now returns a builder closing over its own table. **A shared mutable builder cannot model per-table behaviour under `Promise.all`.**
- **Sibling checked, and it is clean:** `app/insights/allday-pack-reality` does not carry the same copy, so this did not spread by copy-paste the way the 15 OG cards and 5 sales indexers did.
- ✅ **Verified:** `tsc` clean · primary suite **11,961 passed / 1,211 files / 0 failures** · component gate **90.21 st / 81.76 br / 89.00 fn / 93.10 ln** against thresholds 89.8/81.3/88.6/92.7 (branch margin 0.46pt — the intended band, so no re-seat). ⚠ Not verified by HTTP round-trip: the sandbox proxy blocks `rippackscity.com` (documented 403 CONNECT).

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — two public deals views silently reverted to SECURITY DEFINER, because `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` wipes reloptions and nothing about that is visible in a view's output

- **Prod DB change** (`audit_20260815_restore_security_invoker_on_deals_views`, committed as `supabase/migrations/20260815190500_…`) + a new repo guard `__tests__/migration-view-security-invoker-guard.test.ts`. No code, no cron, no data mutation.
- **What broke.** `check_public_security_invariants()` returned **2 rows** — `view_unexpected_definer` on `topshot_deals_vs_fmv` and `cross_collection_deals_board`. Cause found, not guessed: migration **`20260815153324`** (the deals-board partition-pruning win, applied 15:33Z today) recreated both with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW … AS` and **no `WITH` clause**, which **RESETS reloptions** and dropped `security_invoker=on`. Timeline corroborates: night pass logged security 4/4 clean at 08:11Z, migration 15:33Z, monitor flagged exactly those two at 18:10Z.
- ⚠ **Mechanism verified EMPIRICALLY rather than asserted** — `create view pg_temp.zz with (security_invoker=on) as select 1;` → `security_invoker=on`; `create or replace view pg_temp.zz as select 1;` → **options GONE**.
- ⚠ **NOTHING IN THE AUTHORING LOOP COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is the whole finding.** That migration is a *good* one: it verified output **md5**, row count, buffer counts and `Subplans Removed`. **A view's security mode does not appear in its output**, so every one of those checks passes identically whether the view is invoker or definer. The defect is invisible to correctness testing by construction.
- ⚠ **NOTHING LEAKED — and I checked rather than accepting the monitor's "benign", which it had reached by ANALOGY to the Candy views.** That analogy does not hold: the Candy views had anon **revoked**, while these two are anon+authenticated SELECT **by design** (they back public `/insights/deals` + the concierge), so a definer view here really is an RLS-bypassing read. What makes it harmless is the *data*: every base table is catalog/market (`edition_offers`, `editions`, `fmv_snapshots`, `pinnacle_catalog`, `topshot_{thin_fmv,conflated}_editions`) with **no user-scoped rows**, so there was no per-user RLS to bypass. **The defect is lost hardening, not exposure.** Severity by measurement, not by precedent.
- ⚠ **`security_invoker=on` is the fix, NOT the allowlist — and the invariant says so itself.** Its arm-(b) comment reads *"catches a hardened (invoker) view silently reverting to definer"*. Allowlisting would have **accepted the exact regression the arm exists to detect**. ⚠ Verified invoker was SAFE before applying: anon holds SELECT on every base table and every policy admits it (`USING (true)`, `editions` scoped to active collections, `collections` `is_active`).
- ⚠ **`ALTER VIEW`, not `CREATE OR REPLACE`** — it touches only the catalog entry, so the repair cannot drift the query definition as a side effect, which is the failure being repaired. Both views in ONE migration, since each `apply_migration` costs a ~10–20 s burst of user-facing `PGRST002` 500s.
- ✅ **Verified after apply, including the half that regresses by SILENCE.** Invariants **2 → 0**, `check_anon_write_surface()` 0, both views read `security_invoker=on`, `secdef_drift` 0, `rls_off` 0. The public board re-fetched **anonymously end-to-end** returns 50/50 rows, the **identical row set** to the pre-change baseline, and all three legs (`nba_top_shot`, `nfl_all_day`, `disney_pinnacle`). **A broken invoker view fails by returning NOTHING, so a clean invariant alone would not have been evidence the board still worked.**
- ⚠ **MY FIRST VERSION OF THAT CHECK WAS SERVED BY THE EDGE CACHE AND PROVED NOTHING — I caught it on the numbers.** "Byte-identical, 30,856 bytes" also carried an **`elapsed_ms` identical to the millisecond (5833 both times)**, which no independent execution produces. I had compared a cached response to itself. Re-run with a cache-busting query param (a distinct cache key), the board genuinely re-executes — 30,856 B, `elapsed_ms` **5455**, same row set. ⚠ **A byte-identical result is the signature of a cache hit at least as much as of a correct change**, and on a route that sets a public `s-maxage` that is the likelier reading; carry a per-request nonce when verifying a write against a cached read.
- ⚠ **That cache-busted run also produced a 503 on 1 of 2 requests — pre-existing, and I proved it rather than waving at it.** Body is `code:"timeout", retryable:true` (the `boardUnavailable` classification), and `deals` is filed at a **59.5%** tick-failure rate on `cross_collection_deals_board: canceling statement due to statement timeout`. **My change cannot be the cause**: the route reads via `supabaseAdmin` (⚠ imported as `import { supabaseAdmin as supabase }` — the documented "an identifier named `supabase` is usually the service-role client" trap, checked rather than assumed), and **`service_role` carries `rolbypassrls = true`**, so under invoker mode the view still executes with RLS bypassed and **no policy predicate is added to the plan**. Invoker is a no-op for the app path's cost; only a true anon PostgREST read would pay it.
- ⚠ **THE DURABLE PART: this is the FOURTH occurrence, and every previous one was documented INSIDE the migration that caused it — where the next author never looks.** `v_rpc_trust_health` carries *"THE ALTER VIEW BELOW IS LOAD-BEARING … this exact view silently lost `security_invoker=on` that way"*; `panini_squeeze_board` carries *"this migration dropped security_invoker as a side effect, repaired minutes later by …"*; and **`20260801012254` creates TWO views, re-asserts the option for `v_topshot_pack_market` and forgets `pack_ev_latest`, though its own header says it meant to do both.** The knowledge existed and was unreachable. Hence a guard: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW public.X` in a migration must state a security mode for **that view** — inline `WITH (security_invoker = on)` **or** a matching `ALTER VIEW X SET (…)`, the repo's established convention. **Keyed per VIEW NAME on purpose**, because "a file that hardens view A vouches for view B" is not hypothetical — it is `pack_ev_latest`.
- ⚠ **My first version of the guard was WRONG and the migrations corrected it.** I sized it with a per-FILE grep (`does the file mention security_invoker`), got 88% compliance, and wrote a per-STATEMENT check — which then red-flagged ~20 legitimate files using the `ALTER VIEW` convention. **The convention was right and my rule was wrong**; per-file also *undercounted*, hiding the five files that mention the option for a different view. Both errors came from one shortcut: measuring at file granularity a property that lives on a statement.
- **16 files grandfathered, each checked LIVE rather than excused as old:** `pack_ev_latest` is definer **but allowlisted with anon SELECT revoked** (accepted by design, no exposure), `panini_squeeze_board` and `pinnacle_unresolved_with_owner` are invoker/allowlisted. Applied migrations are history — editing them cannot change production, since they are never re-run — so the repair is a NEW migration, and a guard case pins that (editing the applied file would turn the guard green while prod stayed definer). **The list is size-pinned so it cannot grow silently.**
- **Mutation-proven in three directions:** a new unguarded `CREATE VIEW` → caught; the same hardened via `ALTER VIEW` → passes (no false positive on the real convention); **two views with only one hardened → catches exactly the unhardened one**, reproducing the `pack_ev_latest` shape. Guard strips SQL comments first — required, since the repair migration quotes `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.topshot_deals_vs_fmv` in its own header (this repo's recurring trap, now on its fifth instance).
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; guard + `proxy-is-public-path` **165 passed**.
- **Revert:** `ALTER VIEW public.topshot_deals_vs_fmv SET (security_invoker = off);` + same for `cross_collection_deals_board` — **which re-opens the invariant breach; prefer fixing forward.** `git revert <sha>` drops the guard + the committed migration file (the DB stays hardened either way).

- **Guard:** `__tests__/og-insights-headline-count-is-not-a-page-length.test.ts` — directory-driven over the whole `og/insights` tree, strips comments first, and mutation-proven. ⚠ It matches the **call forms** `boardCountLabel(` / `fetchBoardCount(`, not the bare identifiers: a card that keeps the import while hand-rolling the interpolation satisfies a plain `includes()` and slips through (caught by mutation, not by review).
- **Also:** `allday-scarcity` / `pinnacle-scarcity` read `total_rows` purely as a non-empty gate (they print "· live", no number) — re-pointed at `rows.length`, which is the honest expression and keeps the guard strict. ### 2026-08-15 · QUEUED — NEEDS ONE APPROVAL (Claude Code, interactive) — the saturation has a SCHEDULE: three heavy pg_cron jobs collide at minute :13, and the fix is two `cron.alter_job` calls

- **Docs only (inbox filing `2026-08-15T1630Z-…`). NOTHING CHANGED IN PROD** — the `cron.alter_job` call was blocked by the permission classifier, correctly, since it mutates prod scheduling state. Revert of this entry: `git revert <sha>`.
- ⚠ **THE FIND: the platform's "intermittent" disk-IO saturation is not uniformly random.** Observed live at 16:15Z: **15 active backends, EVERY ONE blocked on `IO / DataFileRead`, oldest 486 s**, plus 7 on `IPC / BufferIo`. The three oldest were all pg_cron — `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY mv_topshot_market_index_daily` at **499 s**, `backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev(15)` at 139 s, and `refresh_topshot_special_serial_owners_mv()` at 139 s — with **11 PostgREST board queries that all started in the same second** landing on top.
- **The schedules explain it exactly:** jobid **71** (`13 * * * *`, avg 142 s / **max 602 s**, **10 failures in 167 runs**) and jobid **109** (`13 4,16 * * *`) fire at the **SAME MINUTE**, a guaranteed collision twice daily; and jobid **235** (`7 */2 * * *`, avg 198 s / **max 624 s**) starts at :07 and can still be running at :17, so it overlaps 71 on every even hour. Peak concurrency is **3 heavy writers + ~11 heavy board readers on a 2-core / 2 GB instance**.
- **THE FIX — two calls, and note what it is NOT:** `cron.alter_job` changes only the schedule, so there is **no DDL, no PostgREST schema-cache invalidation, and no burst of user-facing `PGRST002` 500s** — unlike a migration. Both jobs keep their frequency; only the minute moves. `SELECT cron.alter_job(71, schedule => '40 * * * *'); SELECT cron.alter_job(109, schedule => '25 4,16 * * *');` **REVERT:** the same two calls with `'13 * * * *'` and `'13 4,16 * * *'`.
- **Separation was derived from MAX observed durations, not averages**, so it holds in the worst case: `:07–:17` (235) → `:25–:28` (109) → `:40–:50` (71), no overlap where today there are two guaranteed daily three-way overlaps.
- ⚠ **Honest status: a hypothesis with a strong mechanism, NOT a measured outcome.** It makes no query faster — it stops three running at once. Confirmation is the board-warm failure rate over the following day, already queryable per board from `pipeline_runs.extra->boards` and `extra.snapshot_age_min`.
- **Filed separately, NOT proposed:** `mv_topshot_market_index_daily` is named `_daily` but runs **every two hours** (94 runs/7 d, avg 198 s, max 624 s). If daily is what the data needs, that removes ~90% of the single largest IO block — but it is a data-freshness product call, not a scheduling tweak.

- ⚠ **R13 (P2) — `/api/profile/achievements` POST was a CONFUSED DEPUTY.** It read `ownerKey` from the request **body** and then called the compute-achievements edge function with the **server's `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`**, with no ownership check — so a caller could make RPC recompute and WRITE achievements for an arbitrary `owner_key` using our own operator credential. Every sibling `/api/profile/**` writer already carries `requireOwnedKey`; this one was missed. Now gated, fails closed on 401/403/any resolution error, and the test asserts **the edge fetch is never reached** — the credential must not be spent before the gate.
- **R13's other half — GET returned `{achievements: []}` at HTTP 200 on a Postgres error.** Byte-identical to "you have unlocked nothing", so an outage silently erased a collector's achievements from their own profile. ⚠ **Invisible to BOTH driver-message leak guards by construction** — it swallowed the message entirely, and a guard that hunts for leaked text finds nothing in a response that leaks nothing. Now `apiErrorResponse`. ⚠ **The GET's missing ownership check is deliberately NOT a finding and is now commented as such:** `profile_achievements` carries an explicit `"public read achievements"` RLS policy (`roles={public}, qual=true`), so those rows are already anon-readable — adding a gate would imply a privacy property the table does not have.
- ⚠ **Two existing tests were titled *"swallows a DB error into { achievements: [] }"*** — a title that makes the defect read as the contract, the same shape this repo has now hit repeatedly. Rewritten to assert the property (failure reported as failure, driver text absent), plus a **positive mirror** so a genuinely empty set is still an honest `200 []`.
- **R12 (P2) — `/share/<wallet>` rendered a failed read as *"We haven't indexed this wallet yet"*.** `fetchSnapshot` returned a bare `null` for both "the read failed" and "this wallet holds nothing" — a claim about OUR INDEX manufactured from a transient failure, on the page a collector deliberately shares. ⚠ **Worse than a wording bug: that empty state QUEUES the wallet for indexing and polls**, so an outage spent real ingest work re-indexing wallets that were never the problem. Now returns `{ data, ok }` and a failed read renders a distinct `ShareUnavailable` that queues nothing.
- **R12 also emitted no canonical** — `/share/0xABC` and `/share/0xabc` are the same card at two indexable URLs, and this page is shared BY HAND so both spellings really occur. Canonicalised on the lowercase form.
- **R10 (P2) — the `openGraph`/`twitter` shallow-merge trap was live in all three shared `lib/seo.ts` helpers.** Next merges page metadata into the root at the TOP-LEVEL key only, so defining `openGraph` in a child **replaces** the root block outright and every omitted field vanishes. Visible symptom: **the public boards the concierge calls "the most shareable thing RPC has" unfurled with no X byline at all.** `app/profile/[username]/layout.tsx` had documented the trap and got it right; the fix was never generalised.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "keep going") — the metadata honesty layer had no guard, and both pack pages were dropping the `ok` their own page bodies use

- **Code only: 2 `generateMetadata` fixes + 1 derived source guard (4 tests). No DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet, or FMV/pricing-MATH change.**
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Found by asking which honesty layer lacked a guard.** The CLAUDE.md table lists five; four have directory-driven guards and **link-preview metadata had none** — the layer where a false *"Portfolio: $0 FMV across 0 moments"* survived ~2 months on `/profile/[username]`, precisely because metadata output is invisible in a browser and only ever seen in someone else's timeline.
- ⚠ **THE FIND, and its shape is the interesting part: the same file gets it right in one function and wrong in the other.** Both pack pages' page BODIES destructure `ok` to separate "this pack does not exist" from "the read failed" — `/pack/dist/[distId]` even carries a comment saying that fix exists because timeouts were rendering real packs as 404s. **Their `generateMetadata` discarded it**: `const { data: row } = await fetchPackRow(...)` and `(await fetchLifecycle(id)).lifecycle`. `RowResult<T>` is `{ data, ok }` and `ok` is false ONLY on error, so it was added for exactly this and then dropped one function away.
- ⚠ **Not hypothetical, and worse than it looks.** `/pack/dist/[distId]` is the surface with the platform's highest timeout count (`NEXTJS-1Z`, 86 users), and **metadata reads its OWN rows rather than the body's bundle** — so the metadata read can fail while the page renders perfectly: a real, working pack page returning **200** with no title, no description, no canonical and no OG image, still indexable. `/pack/[id]` published its generic fallback description for a real pack whose read merely timed out.
- **Fixed to the canonical `/moment/[id]` shape** — *"Only an ANSWERED read may claim the moment is not in the index"* — a neutral "Unavailable" title plus `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`, so an outage withholds indexing for that fetch while keeping link equity, and a recovered page indexes normally on the next crawl. ⚠ Note neither page fabricated a FIGURE: every number was already guarded by `!== null`, so this was the error-vs-absent half of the rule, not the false-zero half.
- **The guard is DERIVED, not a hand-kept list** (`__tests__/metadata-failed-read-vs-absent-guard.test.ts`): it discovers ok-carrying TYPES by scanning for `ok: boolean` in interface bodies (**19** found), then every function returning one (**54** fetchers), then requires any of the **29** `generateMetadata` bodies calling one to read `ok`. So a new ok-returning fetcher is covered automatically. Strips comments first — the fixes' own comments name the fetchers, and this repo has tripped that trap four times.
- ⚠ **MY FIRST VERSION OF THE GUARD WAS SILENTLY BROKEN AND STILL PASSED ITS OWN COVERAGE CHECK.** A whole-file `\([\s\S]*?\)` for the parameter list **backtracks across function boundaries** when the nearest declaration has no matching return type, so one match swallowed several functions and reported the wrong name — it discovered **1** fetcher instead of 54. Rewritten to scan a bounded 600-char window per declaration. Same class caught the body extractor too: `indexOf("{")` after the function name grabs the PARAMS object (`{ params }: { params: Promise<{…}> }`), not the body — walk the parens to their close first.
- **Mutation-proven both ways:** reverting either page's fix reds the generic check AND the concrete pin. The suite finding **zero other offenders** is the useful negative result — only those two were broken.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary **11,803 green**; rebased onto two concurrent sessions' commits before writing.

A `postgres`-owned copy would have started silently timing out — a "fix" that breaks the job it moves.

- ⚠ **BUT THE STAGGER IS NOT THE LEVER FOR THE 225 s RUN, and the arithmetic is clean.** Both daily ticks collide with jobid 71 **because 71 is hourly** — so that collision is present in both equally, and the ticks are not equal: 04:13Z vs 16:13Z ran **16.4 s vs 159.9 s (08-14)**, **37.6 s vs 181.5 s (08-15)**, **22.5 s vs 224.8 s (08-16)** — 5–10×. **A cause present in both ticks cannot explain a 10× gap between them.** The dominant cost is ambient business-hours load (04:13Z = 21:13 PT quiet, 16:13Z = 09:13 PT peak), and `:43` is still business hours. Had that declaration bound the statements inside, it would have been cancelled at 200 s. The binding budget is the caller's role (`cron_heavy` 600 s). Same trap as the drain seeders and the trust-precompute legs, on a function nobody had looked at — more evidence that any fix phrased as "raise the function's declared timeout" is a no-op.

A naive `max(duration_ms)` reads 0 and looks like a job that does nothing.

### 2026-08-14 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — read `rpc_search_catalog` instead of inferring, and had to CORRECT my own narrative-search diagnosis: it is a flat flag, not a length-normalized score

- **Docs only, direct to `main`. No code, no DB, no migration, no prod-state change.** ⚠ No Vercel deploy expected (`ignoreCommand` skips `*.md`).
- ⚠ **MY OWN FILED DIAGNOSIS WAS PARTLY WRONG, and I only found out by reading the function.** I had written that matches are ranked by trigram `similarity()` which is "length-normalized, so a long paragraph scores below a short set name". **There is no paragraph score.** The edition arm computes similarity against **names only** (`player_name || set_name`); the description's ENTIRE contribution is a flat boolean `CASE WHEN via_prose THEN 0.12`. I had inferred a mechanism from behaviour and filed it as fact.
- **The measured mechanism.** `121:4255`, whose description literally contains "buzzer", scores **0.1404**. **Buddy Hield — a fuzzy NAME match with no prose match at all — scores 0.4676.** A verbatim prose containment loses **3×** to a name resemblance, because a player hit also collects the 0.35 kind-weight while a prose hit collects 0.12. And because the boost is FLAT, every prose hit scores identically, so within them the effective order is the tiebreak `u.lbl ASC` — **alphabetical**. That is why the moment is unreachable even at limit 50: not outranked by one thing, buried in a mass of ties.
- ⚠ **TWO hypotheses tested and REJECTED, recorded so nobody re-derives them.** (1) **Candidate truncation** — `edition_hits` ends `ORDER BY circulation_count ASC LIMIT 200`, a relevance-blind pre-filter that looked damning; **rejected by measurement**: 297 editions match "buzzer", the target's circulation is 28, only **13** sort ahead of it, so it is comfortably inside the 200. (2) **"Set names outrank prose"** — directionally true for one query but not the mechanism, and believing it hid the real one; here a *player* name did the outranking.
- **A SECOND, distinct defect separated out.** `48:1652` is not ranked low for `game winner`, it is **excluded entirely**: `LIKE ALL` demands every token and its description says **"game-winning"**, which `'%winner%'` does not match. So the two Lillard moments fail for **different reasons** — one ranking, one tokenization — and any fix claiming to solve narrative search must address both and be verified against BOTH slugs.
- **Design specified with its regression named:** a graded, **exclusivity-gated** prose contribution (phrase-in-description AND phrase-NOT-in-any-name-field → strong boost; all-tokens → moderate). ⚠ The gate is load-bearing: a naive "+0.55 whenever description matches" **regresses ordinary name search** — querying `lillard` would lift every edition whose prose mentions him to ~0.85, level with the Lillard PLAYER hit, so searching a player could stop returning that player first. Stemming still needs FTS (`tsvector` + `ts_rank`); `editions` is only ~27k rows, so that is cheap.
- **Why I did NOT ship it:** live ranking behind BOTH the public header search and the concierge's `search_catalog`, and the regression it risks is exactly the kind that passes a spot check and needs a broad before/after battery written first. The investigation is done; what remains is verification breadth.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — documentation only.

### 2026-08-14 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — figured out BOTH open items without an operator: the walker query was already proven, and the All Day 403 is a one-line env change

- **Code comments + inbox filing, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Both open items from the previous wave resolved by reading evidence already in hand rather than asking for a curl.
- ⚠ **ITEM 1 — the walker's 422 risk was ALREADY DISPROVEN and I had asked for a redundant verification.** The 2026-08-13 probe ran `searchEditions` → `play { stats { <field> } }` against live Top Shot and returned **sample VALUES** for all three new fields (`birthdate` `"1999-06-17"`, `birthplace` `"Havre De Grace, MD, USA"`, `draftYear` `2020`). A sample value means the query VALIDATED AND EXECUTED. The walker uses the **same endpoint, same operation, same `SearchEditionsInput!`, same nesting** — and GraphQL selection is ADDITIVE, so adding already-valid fields to an already-valid selection set cannot invalidate it. **The verification curl I asked for was unnecessary.** Worth recording: "I cannot test this" was false; the test had already been run for a different purpose.
- ⚠ **ITEM 2 — the All Day WAF 403 is a ROUTE problem with a one-line fix.** Read `workers/topshot-proxy/index.js`: only **`/allday-consumer`** carries `ROUTE_HEADERS` (`Origin: nflallday.com`, `Referer`, browser UA) — exactly the fingerprint a Cloudflare WAF checks. **`/allday` sends the bare `sports-collectible-tool/0.1` UA with no Origin**, and `lib/editions-hydrate.ts` sends no Origin either. The README sets `ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` to the worker's **`/allday`** route. **Suggested fix: point it at `/allday-consumer`** — which is right for TWO independent reasons: the fingerprint, AND that `allEditions` (used by both the probe arm and editions-hydrate) belongs to the **consumer** endpoint, which is that route's upstream and editions-hydrate's own `ALLDAY_GQL_DEFAULT`. If `ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` is currently `/allday`, the query is going to the WRONG ENDPOINT independent of the WAF.
- ⚠ **AND I NEARLY SHIPPED A WRONG INFERENCE, caught by re-reading the worker.** I first concluded "the request never reached the worker, because the worker answers plain-text 401 on bad auth and we got an HTML 403". **Invalid**: the worker passes the upstream response through verbatim (`new Response(data, { status: upstreamRes.status })`), so an origin block page is byte-identical whether proxied or not. The only shape that PROVES the worker was reached is its own 401. Same class as everything else this week — reading a downstream artifact as evidence about an upstream hop.
- **Resolved the guard tension I had filed as "real and unresolved".** `api-admin-discover-moment-descriptors.test.ts` forbids posting All Day to a `TS_PROXY_URL` subpath (a V1 404), which looked like it contradicted CLAUDE.md's "the worker exposes /allday". It does not: per the README **`ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` IS a worker subpath already**, so the guard's rule is about **where the URL comes from** (read the configured variable; never rebuild it and let the two drift), not about what it may point at. **Keep the guard.** Probe comment rewritten from "unresolved operator question" to the actual finding.
- **Also found:** the worker **never 404s on an unknown path** — `UPSTREAM_MAP[path] ? path : DEFAULT_ROUTE` silently proxies a typo'd route to **Top Shot**, so a misrouted All Day query returns a confusing GraphQL field error instead of failing loudly. A `400` would be better; that is a `wrangler deploy` and operator-gated.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — captured the player bio the probe found: `editions.player_{birthdate,birthplace,draft_year}` (**MIGRATION + ingest**)

- **DB migration + code + tests, direct to `main`.** ⚠ **This wave has a DB half — see the revert path.** No cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change, no destructive SQL.
- **Migration `audit_20260814_editions_player_bio_columns`** — three NULLABLE columns on `editions` (`player_birthdate date`, `player_birthplace text`, `player_draft_year smallint`), metadata-only ALTER, no table rewrite, each with a `COMMENT`. Verified live in `information_schema` before shipping any code. **Applied BEFORE the code deliberately**: nullable columns nobody writes are inert, whereas code writing columns that do not exist fails every upsert.
- **Why on `editions` and not `players`:** this table already denormalizes `player_name` / `team_name` / `jersey_number`, and the Top Shot catalog walker's upsert writes editions. Putting them on `players` would have meant touching `upsert_player_canonical`, which is one of the 125 drift-guarded DB pins — materially higher risk for no product gain. **Prefixed `player_`** because `editions` already has `game_date` and `first_minted_at`, so a bare `birthdate` on an EDITION row reads as a date about the moment.
- ⚠ **The placement risk was REAL and is now pinned.** Commit `b1018e63` already shipped this exact class once: `description` was put inside `stats { }`, which invalidates the WHOLE GraphQL query — Top Shot answers **HTTP 422**, `fetchPage` returns null, and the walk **upserts ZERO editions while reporting `ok: true`**. The 2026-08-13 probe settled the placements against live Top Shot with all controls passing: `description`/`headline` on **`Play`**, the bio fields on **`PlayStats`** — the exact opposite nesting. New source guard pins BOTH directions (description must stay OUT of `stats { }`; the three bio fields must stay IN), so the next person cannot re-derive the 422.
- ⚠ **Sentinel-normalized, which is not optional here.** Top Shot answers `draftYear: 0`, `"N/A"`, `""` rather than null for unknown bio. A raw `?? null` would store `draft_year = 0` for every player with unknown draft data, and the "serial matches draft year" hook would then fire on garbage. All three go through `isSentinel()` — the same guard the description path uses — pinned by a test that reads the ASSIGNMENT line specifically.
- ⚠ **I did NOT capture `jerseyNumber` here even though it is available.** `editions.jersey_number` already exists at **65.3%** coverage, written by a different path; adding a second writer that returns null for un-hydrated rows would clobber good values on every walk — the documented never-null-out trap. Left alone.
- **What this unlocks:** `classifySerial` already accepts `birthdate` / `draftYear` as optional context, so **birthday serials** (born 6/17 → serial 617) and draft-year serials become real as soon as the walker populates — no further logic needed. `player_birthplace` is the hometown identity hook, and the nearest available substitute for college, which the same probe proved Top Shot does NOT expose.
- ⚠ **Population is NOT immediate.** The walker runs daily (`/api/cron/topshot-catalog-backfill`, 02:12 UTC) and covers sets least-recently-touched first, so coverage fills over several runs. **Measure before wiring any surface that implies coverage** — the Panini lesson.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary gate **11,683 green**; 8 walker tests green incl. the 4 new placement/sentinel guards.
- **Revert (BOTH halves):** `git revert <sha>` for the code, and `ALTER TABLE public.editions DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS player_birthdate, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS player_birthplace, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS player_draft_year;` for the schema. The code half is safe to revert alone — the columns simply stop being written.
### 2026-08-14 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — the trophy picker's search blamed the collector's collection for our page cap

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.**
- ⚠ **THE SEARCH BOX SAYS "Search by player, set, or team" AND FILTERS CLIENT-SIDE OVER 96 ROWS.** `/api/profile/top-moments` returns the top 96 by FMV (and clamps above it, so the cap is the API's ceiling too), and the picker searched only what it had loaded. A collector with more than 96 Moments searching for one outside their top 96 by value was told **"No moments match the current filter"** — a claim about **their collection**, manufactured from our page limit, on the exact screen where they choose what their public profile shows off.
- ⚠ **DISCLOSED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, because we cannot measure the truncation.** A full page back means the collection is *at least* 96; it does **not** distinguish "owns exactly 96" from "owns 500". So the copy states what is true either way — *"Showing your 96 highest-value Moments. Search looks inside this list only."* — instead of claiming a truncation we have not established. Same discipline as the candy board's "Showing the top N of M", inverted: there the total was known, here it is not, and the wording has to reflect which.
- **The no-match copy now names the cause:** *"Nothing in your top 96 by value matches. A lower-value Moment won't be listed here — use the manual tab if you know its ID."* Both directions pinned: an uncapped list keeps the plain copy, and a small collection gets **no** notice at all — a permanent banner on a collector who owns 12 Moments is its own false claim.
- ⚠ **The fetch hardcoded `limit: "96"` while nothing else knew the number**, so the disclosure and the request could drift apart silently. Now one exported `PICKER_LIMIT`, and a test asserts the request uses the same constant the UI reasons about.
- **Verified:** 10 tests green in that file (5 new), component gate green (90.18/81.68/88.99/93.07), `tsc` clean, 2 mutations red (notice always on / no-match copy blames the collection).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. No DB unwind.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — Trevor caught it: "narrative search" returns the FOR THE WIN SET, not game winners, and I had verified the defect and called it a success

- **Code + tests + inbox, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.**
- ⚠ **THE CORRECTION, and it invalidates a claim I made three times today.** I shipped `search_catalog` as "the only tool that can answer a NARRATIVE query", cited `lillard game winner` → "Damian Lillard — For the Win" as live proof, and built a **"Find a game winner" pill** on it. **"For the Win" is a SET NAME containing the query words.** I had confirmed set-name matching and reported it as prose matching. Trevor spotted it from the domain: *game winner* is not a set, and some For The Win moments are **Blocks**.
- **The measurement.** `game winner` (Top Shot, limit 30) returns **0** real game winners — it returns a roster of the For The Win set, `Block` variants included. Same for `buzzer beater`, `series winner`, `game winning shot`, `walk off winner`, `lillard game winner` (3 rows), `lillard buzzer beater` (0 rows). ⚠ **The two most famous Blazers game winners are missed entirely** — Lillard's 2014 0.9-second series winner (**Archive Set `48:1652`**) and the 2019 37-footer (**Run It Back: Legacies `121:4255`**) — **though BOTH carry descriptions, one containing "game-winning" verbatim and the other "buzzer"**. Even single-token `buzzer` returns *Buddy Hield* on a fuzzy NAME match instead.
- ⚠ **Root cause, established by control rather than inferred: the prose arm WORKS and is OUTRANKED.** `weber state` — a phrase in description text and in no name or set — returns exactly the right row. Matches are scored by trigram **`similarity()`, which is LENGTH-NORMALIZED**, so a 200-character paragraph containing the phrase verbatim scores BELOW the short set name "For The Win". Prose only wins on a distinctive proper noun; every generic narrative phrase loses to a set name. **`similarity()` is the wrong scorer for a long text field** — the fix is a containment boost or full-text ranking, NOT raising the 0.12 `via_prose` constant (the gap is structural, not an offset).
- **Shipped:** the pill is **REMOVED** (it was live ~40 min demonstrating set-name matching as narrative search), replaced by a test that blocks re-adding it until the ranking is fixed **and verified against those two slugs specifically**. The `search_catalog` tool description and its system-prompt section were rewritten to **stop promising narrative search**, to name the concrete For-The-Win failure, and to require the bot to READ results before presenting — if the hits all share one set name and don't match what was described, it must say so instead of passing a set roster off as an answer.
- ⚠ **The method lesson, which is the one I keep paying for.** My verification asked *"did it return rows?"* and not *"are the rows right?"* — the exact failure mode I filed an inbox note about earlier the SAME session (a probe that passes during the outage it is meant to catch). **A domain expert reading the output caught in one sentence what three green gates, 11k tests and my own live query could not.** When verifying a relevance/ranking feature, the check must be a known-correct ANSWER, not a non-empty result.
- **Filed, not fixed:** `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-14T0310Z-narrative-search-is-outranked-by-set-names.md` — full repro table, the `weber state` control, three ranked fix options, and the stemming gap ("buzzer" vs "buzzer beater"). `rpc_search_catalog` is another session's function shipped today; the ranking fix is theirs to take with the evidence.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary **11,563 green**; component **1,614 green**.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — code + tests only. ⚠ Reverting restores the misleading pill and the over-promising tool description; do not revert without also fixing the ranking.

- ⚠ **AND MY OWN CACHE ASSERTION WAS VACUOUS UNTIL I MUTATED IT.** `src.includes("OG_CACHE_HEADERS")` is satisfied by the **import statement**, so deleting the actual `headers:` option left it green. - **The ratchet is honest about what it counts:** 9 route files ≠ 14 cards, because the entity five import nothing themselves. Both facts are asserted separately rather than papered over with one number.

Both consumers fetch over HTTP with **no session**: the OG profile card (`runtime = "edge"`, so it *cannot* read the files off disk) and the trophy-case PDF. The followed redirect returns an HTML page at **status 200**, which satisfies `res.ok` and `byteLength > 0` — the only two checks either loader made.
- ⚠ **THE DURABLE PART: the fallback written for exactly this hazard was structurally incapable of firing.** `og/profile` wraps its render in a three-tier try/catch whose comment says a rejected font "THROWS out of ImageResponse rather than degrading" — correct, and guarding the wrong place. **`new ImageResponse(...)` returns a Response whose body is a STREAM**, so satori runs when the body is CONSUMED, after `GET` has already returned; the throw escapes the handler and no `catch` around the constructor will ever see it. **A guard around `new ImageResponse(...)` catches nothing that happens during rendering.**
- ⚠ **And the test that should have caught it modelled the tidy failure instead of the real one.** `api-og-profile-brand-fonts` stubbed the font fetch as a **503** — a shape the old `res.ok` check already handled — so it ran green while production was broken. - **Shipped, two halves.** (1) `lib/og/font-bytes.ts` → `isSupportedFontBuffer` validates the sfnt signature before any renderer sees the bytes — **the response proves the request succeeded, never that a font came back** — wired into both loaders, accepting `ArrayBuffer` or any view since the two callers hold different shapes. WOFF2 is rejected deliberately (opentype.js cannot decode Brotli; accepting it would trade a clear rejection for the same late throw). (2) `proxy.ts` publishes the fonts.
- ⚠ **The `proxy.ts` change is deliberately NARROWER than my first version, which folded `ttf|otf|woff2?` into `STATIC_EXT_RX`.** That regex matches ANY path ending in the extension, so it would also publish a gated route whose trailing dynamic segment a visitor controls. ### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — trophy captions: the flair field that existed everywhere except the UI

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.**
- ⚠ **`trophy_moments.note` is the ONLY field on a trophy the collector writes themselves** — every other column is denormalized Moment metadata. It has been accepted by `POST /api/profile/trophy`, stored, returned by `get_trophy_slab_data*`, typed on `TrophySlabData` and rendered in the trophy-case PDF **since the feature shipped**, and **no UI ever set it and no surface ever displayed it**. Measured: **0 of 16** pinned trophies in prod carry a note. `api-profile-trophy.test.ts:114` even asserted the upsert writes `note: null` — a test pinning the ABSENCE of the feature. Same shape as the Follow button (`c91a5aea`): a fully-built backend with nothing to reach it.
- **Shipped all three halves**: `PATCH /api/profile/trophy` (the write path), `SlabNote` on `TrophySlab` in **both** owner and public modes (a caption only visitors can't see is a private note), and `components/profile/TrophyNoteEditor.tsx` wired into the dashboard case.
- ⚠ **PATCH, not POST, for a load-bearing reason: POST UPSERTS THE WHOLE ROW.** A client sending `{slot, momentId, note}` to add a caption would blank the player name, tier, art and FMV of the trophy it was captioning. A partial write needs a partial verb. It also **updates, never upserts** — a caption on an empty slot would otherwise conjure a trophy row with no Moment behind it, which the slab renderer cannot draw; that case is a 404, and the editor says "that slot is empty" rather than "couldn't save" (different problem, different fix).
- ⚠ **The editor is a SIBLING of the slab, not a child, and that is structural rather than stylistic.** `TrophySlab`'s entire filled body is wrapped in `<Link href="/moment/...">`; an input nested inside sits in an anchor, so every click, caret placement and Enter navigates away mid-sentence unless every handler remembers `preventDefault` — and the one that forgot would be a caption the user could not finish typing. Rendering below the slab removes the hazard instead of guarding it.
- ⚠ **The dashboard sync matches on the slab's OWN `slot`, not array position.** Filled slabs pack to the front of `slabs` while `slot` is the persisted column, so after a reorder the two diverge and `slabs[slot-1]` would caption the WRONG Moment.
- **Empty caption round-trips to NULL, not `""`** (the slab branches on presence, so `""` renders a blank quoted line), whitespace is collapsed before the length check, and the 90-char cap is measured after collapsing so padding can't trip it.
- ⚠ **One of my own test expectations was a guess about a contract the code doesn't make** — I listed `slot: "2"` among the rejects, but `Number("2")` is a valid integer and coercion is correct, harmless leniency. Fixed as an explicit POSITIVE assertion, because leaving it as a reject would push someone to "fix" working code.
- **Verified:** 43 route tests + 34 component tests green (39 new), `tsc` clean, both coverage gates green (primary 91.59/78.92/93.47/93.70; component 90.07/81.47/88.82/93.00), **4 mutations red** (caption hidden from visitors / `user_id` scope dropped = IDOR / `""` stored instead of NULL / `onSaved` fired regardless of outcome).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. No DB unwind — the column already existed.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — a regex in code I shipped 20 minutes earlier would have thrown at PARSE time on older Safari, taking the whole chat down

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Follow-up to `7114dc9e`; found by reviewing my own diff after it deployed READY, not by a failure.
- ⚠ **The bug: `SITE_PATH` used a LOOKBEHIND — `(?<=[\s(])` — which is ES2018.** Safari only gained lookbehind in **16.4** (March 2023), and an unsupported regex literal is a **`SyntaxError` at PARSE time**, not a caught runtime error: the module fails to evaluate, `SupportChat` fails to import, and **the entire concierge disappears** for that user. On a product whose own system prompt says "most users are on mobile", that is the worst possible blast radius for a cosmetic linkifier.
- ⚠ **`tsc` cannot save you here and neither can the `target` setting.** `tsconfig.json` says `ES2017`, but TypeScript **does not transpile regex literals** — the pattern ships to the browser byte-for-byte. Every gate was green (tsc clean, 11,395 tests, both coverage ratchets) because **the whole toolchain runs on Node, which has supported lookbehind since v8.3**. There was no signal anywhere in CI; only reading the diff with a browser-support question in mind found it.
- **Fix:** the leading context is now a **capture group** (`(^|[\s(])(\/[a-z]…)`) and the parser offsets by group 1's length. Same behaviour — the "and/or" / "8/13" false-positive guard still holds, all 33 prior tests unchanged and green — with no ES2018 syntax.
- **Guard `source guard — no ES2018-only regex syntax`** asserts the tokenizer contains no `(?<=` / `(?<!`, comments stripped first (the trap hit twice already today). It is a *source* guard because a Node-based test suite is structurally incapable of catching this class: the engine running the tests supports the syntax the target engine does not.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary gate **11,397 tests green, 91.57 st / 78.91 br**; the three chat suites (27) green. Deploy `dpl_6U2xcHfYvXURaaZWns9uqutCTztJ` (the parent commit) confirmed **READY** and aliased to www before this follow-up.

- ⚠ **I first "fixed" it by threading an `ok` flag through — and the flag could not change one character of the output.** On a failed read the caller has no data, so every total is already zero and already suppressed. A parameter that reads as a safety property while being incapable of altering behaviour is **worse than none**: no mutation can red it, so it documents a guarantee the tests cannot hold. Removed; the honesty rule now lives in the `> 0` guards, where a mutation proves it (dropping them reds 6 cases). `ok` still matters in the caller, but for `robots` — a 404 must not be indexed, a transient 500 must not be **de**-indexed, and both directions are pinned.

The identical self-fetch was live the whole time in the SIBLING `layout.tsx`, which is the **crawler** path, so every unfurl cost an extra lambda plus uncached DB work and could degrade purely because our own API had been rate limited. Running that guard more often could never have found it; only widening the set could. **Fifth instance of this lesson in two days** (anon driver-message guard, server-page 2-of-79 list, insights-gate include, my own og/insights sweep). Both server entry points are covered now.
- ⚠ **Next merges `openGraph`/`twitter` SHALLOWLY — defining either REPLACES the root object.** The old file defined both, silently dropping `siteName`, `type`, `locale` and `twitter.creator` from `lib/seo.ts` on every profile unfurl. All restated, plus `openGraph.url`, `alternates.canonical`, image `alt`, and `twitter.site`. Pinned, because this is invisible locally and only shows up in someone else's timeline.
- **Perf:** `getPublicProfile` is now `cache()`-wrapped, so the page shell and the metadata call share one read instead of two. ⚠ The memo keys on ARGUMENTS — a caller that invents its own `source` label silently misses it and pays full price with every test green, so a test asserts both callers pass the same label.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — the two SHARE cards were publishing "$0.00" as a named collector's portfolio during an outage

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Ninth wave; the eight below are the same session.
- ⚠ **The find, and it is the worst-consequence instance of the class in the session.** `/api/og/share` (a wallet's collection card) and `/api/og/profile/[username]` (a collector's public profile card) both defaulted their totals to **0** on a failed read and rendered **"$0.00 / 0 moments"** and **"PORTFOLIO FMV $0"**. Every other instance this session made a false claim about the market or our index; **these make a false FINANCIAL claim about an identifiable PERSON — on the cards a collector deliberately POSTS**, baked into an edge-cached PNG and distributed on social.
- ⚠ **The share route's own comment called the zeros "a branded shell".** They are not a shell, they are a **NUMBER**, and a reader has no way to tell one from a real answer. That sentence is why the defect survived review: it describes the fallback as cosmetic when it is substantive.
- **Fixes.** `og/share` gains `fetched` (set INSIDE the `res.ok` branch) and withholds the figures entirely, rendering "COLLECTION SNAPSHOT / Open the page for this wallet's current value" instead. `og/profile`'s `fetchJson` now returns `{ rows, ok }` so a failed leg is distinguishable, and PORTFOLIO FMV / MOMENTS / TROPHY CASE each fall back to **"—"** — the glyph that file already uses for "no value" — **per leg**, so a failed trophy read cannot blank the portfolio or vice versa.
- ⚠ **THREE states, not two, and the third is what made this non-trivial.** A profile with no resolvable `user_id` has no wallets to read: that resolves to `ok: true` with no rows — a real answer — NOT a failure. And a wallet that genuinely holds nothing **IS** worth $0 and must still say so. Every failure case in the suite is paired with the empty-but-successful mirror, so "always withhold" cannot pass.
- **10 tests, both fixes mutation-proven** (flipping `fetched` to true, and dropping the `walletsOk` gate, each reds exactly its cases).
- ⚠ **A harness artefact worth recording so the next person does not read it as a bug.** The share card's JSX emits the currency symbol and the value as SEPARATE children (`${totalFmv.toLocaleString(...)}` is a literal `"$"` plus an interpolation), so `ogText` — which joins children with a space — yields `"$ 0.00"`. Satori lays the two runs out adjacently, so the render is correct. Normalised inside this suite with a `compact()` helper rather than changing `ogText`, which six other suites already depend on.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary suite green at the raised thresholds (91.55 st / 78.91 br / 93.45 fn); brand-token guard clean.

A collector asking the bot to *find* a moment by what happens in it got nothing. New **`search_catalog`** wraps the public `/api/search`, returns linkable hits, and hands back each edition's route slug.
- ⚠ **Its coverage disclosure is load-bearing, not decoration — an empty narrative result is AMBIGUOUS.** Descriptions cover Top Shot partially (**44.6%**, 5,885/13,203, measured live at ship) and **0% of All Day, Golazos, Pinnacle and UFC**. So "no match" can mean *we hold no description for that slice* OR *no such moment*, which are completely different things to tell a collector. The tool forwards the LIVE `coverage`/`note` from the route — never hardcoded, because the backfill moves it every run (the Panini lesson) — and **keeps them attached on the `no_results` branch**, which is exactly where the model needs them. The prompt makes stating which case applies mandatory.
- **New `get_price_history`** wraps `/api/entity/edition?part=sale-history` → `get_edition_sale_history`: actual SALE PRINTS, low/median/high + count per bucket. This is the only path to a multi-year answer — `fmv_snapshots` begin 2026-03-31 while `sales` run back to 2020 — so "has this gone up or down over the past year" was previously unanswerable. Verified live: `128:5147` (Lillard, For the Win) reads $35 median Aug-2025 → $21 Jul-2026.
- ⚠ **It is labelled `basis: "actual_sale_prints"` with an explicit `not_fmv` note, because a sale median is NOT an FMV** — one is what buyers paid, the other a model estimate, and merging them is the conflation this repo keeps paying for. `grain` (day/week/month) is returned and the prompt requires stating it, so the bot cannot imply daily resolution on a six-year window; thin buckets (`sales_count` 1) must be called a single trade, not "the price".
- **Both tools fail LOUD:** a 503 stays `status: "error"`, never degrading to `no_results` — otherwise an outage renders as "we have no such moment", the failed-read-as-data class. Guard-rails also added to the prompt disambiguating **`search_catalog`** (the catalog INDEX, no prices) from **`search_catalog_deals`** (a PRICE tool), whose similar names are a real confusion risk.
- **Tests:** `__tests__/api-support-chat-catalog-history-tools.test.ts` (13). **Mutation-proven ×3** — degrading the search failure to `no_results` reds; dropping `coverage` from the `no_results` branch reds; stripping `basis` reds. `tsc` clean; existing concierge suites (43) green.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — two OG cards could 500 into a blank unfurl, and the test that found it was the one I wrote wrong twice first

- ⚠ **The defect: `og/pack` and `og/pack/lifecycle` had NO try/catch around their reads.** supabase-js **RETURNS** a Postgrest error but **THROWS** on a transport failure (socket hang-up, DNS, aborted fetch) — and an uncaught throw escapes `GET` and **500s the route, which for an OG card is a blank unfurl**: no PNG at all. Both files' own headers promise "never 500"; that held only for the error-RETURN path. Swept the whole family: `og/deal` and `og/collection` also lack a catch but are **param-only and do no I/O**, so only these two were exposed. Fixed both; mutation-proven (removing either catch reds its case).
- **Covered the three worst-remaining OG cards in one parameterised suite** — `og/{set,team,series}` (45.8 / 46.0 / 48.0% branch), which share one shape almost line for line, so a fourth entity card is covered by adding a row. Plus `og/pack/lifecycle` (56.8%, 51 uncovered — the largest single gap left). +65 tests. Primary gate **78.62 → 78.90 br**, actual 91.54/78.90/93.41/93.67.
- **What the lifecycle tests pin is a ROI VERDICT published to a social unfurl**, so the three gates that decide whether it is honest: only a **RIPPED** pack (a sealed one has pulled nothing), it needs both a gross value AND a real cost **BASIS** (retail is a display anchor — deriving ROI from it invents a cost the holder never paid), and break-even is **−ROI, not positive**. Also that a payload carrying an `error` field is not "resolved" even when `status` looks fine.

- ⚠ **I checked the deploy state PER COMMIT, which is the only reason this was caught.** Wave 2 (`59170f3d`) went to state **ERROR** — `Export encountered an error on /(analytics)/analytics/sets/[set_id] … exiting the build` → `npm run build` exit 1. Wave 1 (`c81bb864`) was READY, so prod was serving wave 1 and the tip *looked* fine. **This is the second recorded time a build-time DB read has taken the production build down** (the first was `/insights/first-mint`, fixed with `BOARD_LIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- **NOT caused by my diff.** Nothing in waves 1–2 touches `/analytics/sets/**` or `analytics_sets_detail`; the build log is wall-to-wall `Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool` across candy-mlb, market, trophies, topshot-pack-market and allday-pack-reality — a connection-pool saturation spell. But an ERRORed deploy must not be left standing because the next push supersedes it, and the fragility is real and recurring.
- ⚠ **The root cause is the SAME defect class, in its third instance — and here it has two costs, not one.** `loadSet` returned a bare `null` for BOTH "no such set" AND "the RPC failed", and the page answered `notFound()`. At request time that told a visitor a real set does not exist. **At BUILD time it is worse: the page is PRERENDERED (top-100 sets), Next allows each page 60 s and retries 3× before killing the whole build**, and `rpcWithRetry` correctly treats pool-timeouts as transient and retries them — so a throttled DB does not degrade the page, it fails the deploy.
- **Fix, mirroring the two conventions the repo already has:** `loadSet` returns `{ data, ok }` (a genuine "no such set" is `ok: true`; only a failure is `ok: false`); the page renders a new `SetUnavailableCard` **before** `notFound()`; `generateMetadata` titles it *"Set unavailable"* rather than *"Set not found"* — the title is what a crawler and a shared link both read; and `SET_DETAIL_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000` bounds the read well under the export budget so a slow DB degrades the page to ISR (`dynamicParams` is already `true`) instead of failing the build. ⚠ The timeout resolves to the **failed** shape, never the absent one: **a slow read and a broken read are equally unservable, and only the broken one was modelled** — the exact wording of the first-mint lesson.
- **Guarded in the file built for it.** `server-pages-error-vs-absent-guard.test.ts` went 2 pages → 3, plus a second case pinning the BUILD-safety half (budget exists, is ≤30 s, resolves to `ok: false`, and `dynamicParams` stays `true`). That guard exists precisely because `app/**/page.tsx` is measured by neither coverage gate — the blind spot wave 2's ratchet now freezes at 36.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — weekly-QA handoff: entity pages hang on "SCANNING THE MARKETPLACE…") — the entity-page RPC path had NO wall-clock bound, so a call that never ANSWERED parked the render until Vercel killed the function at 300s

**The handoff's own open question — transient or persistent? — was the first thing measured, and it is BOTH.** Re-probed all five entity routes live: every one renders now (edition 3.2s / 11.1s, player 7.8s, team 17.2s, set 16.6s, series 1.1s), so the reported 15-minute window had cleared. But the defect is real and permanent, and production names it: the project's LARGEST runtime-error group is **`Vercel Runtime Timeout Error: Task timed out after 300 seconds` (781 events / 183 users)** and **`/[collection]/edition/[slug]` is one of the routes listed in it**.

⚠ **DURABLE — retrying handles an RPC that FAILS; nothing handled one that never answers, and they are not the same event.** `supabase-js` issues a plain `fetch` with **no signal**, and `rpcWithRetry` had no timeout, so a stuck connection-acquire inside Supavisor parked the `await` indefinitely (undici's own ceiling is ~300s). The retry loop never ran — there was no error to retry. Proven with a positive control: a server that accepts the connection and never responds leaves the call **still hanging at 1.5s**; with `AbortSignal.timeout(800)` it settles in **809ms**, and the abort **RETURNS** an error (does not throw) with **`code: ""`**, so it falls through to the message heuristics. Same lesson the boards learned on 08-12 (`BOARD_LIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`): **slow and broken are equally unservable, and only broken was modelled.**

⚠ **Why it is invisible to every existing instrument.** These five routes ship a `loading.tsx`, so Next flushes the shell and a **200** immediately and streams the page after. A render that never finishes therefore shows the skeleton with **no error, no failing status, and no client XHR** — the API smoke gate sees 200, the DB monitor sees a healthy instance (measured mid-incident: 5 active backends, 0 DataFileRead waiters, RPCs 19–360ms), and the only trace is Vercel's own kill 300s later.

**Shipped** — `lib/analytics/rpc-with-retry.ts` gains a **TOTAL** wall-clock budget (`timeoutMs`, default `DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000`) covering all attempts + backoff, not a per-attempt allowance (a per-attempt bound silently multiplies by `attempts`). Two mechanisms on purpose: `.abortSignal()` genuinely cancels and **releases the pool slot** (abandoning a request that still holds a connection makes a pile-up worse), and a `Promise.race` **guarantees** we settle — necessary because every mock in this repo shapes `.rpc` as a bare async fn with no `.abortSignal`, so the signal cannot be relied on to exist.

⚠ **45s is a ceiling ABOVE the database's own, not a latency target — do NOT tune it down.** A statement that is genuinely RUNNING is already bounded (`service_role` `statement_timeout=30s` → 57014, which is deliberately never retried). Anything outstanding past 45s is not a statement, it is a stuck acquire — the one case with no other stop condition. A tighter bound would start cancelling statements Postgres would have finished and answered, and these pages really do render in 11–17s under load. This is **confirmed by the concurrent `2026-08-13T2115Z` inbox finding**, which measures `get_series_detail` at **20,172ms** dying on Postgres's own statement timeout into a retryable error boundary: a 15–20s bound would have pre-empted that handled path with our own abort. The two findings are complementary — that one is the SLOW case (fix = materialize latest FMV), this one is the NO-ANSWER case.

⚠ **A test corrected a design claim I had written.** My first test asserted a timeout is transient so a retry can follow. It is not: each attempt is handed the **remaining** budget, so an attempt that times out has consumed all of it and no retry can follow. That is deliberate — the tempting "fix" (slice the budget per attempt so a retry fits) caps one statement below the 30s `service_role` allows. Test and code comment both corrected to state the real behaviour, and the reasoning is pinned so nobody "fixes" it back.

**Also closed the gap that would have left the fix cosmetic:** the shell's `Promise.all` had **three fetchers on a bare `.rpc()`**, bypassing the wrapper entirely — `get_edition_market_bundle` (the single most frequent edition error in prod: 40 statement timeouts + 17 pool timeouts), `get_edition_insight_links`, and `get_badge_display_metadata` in `lib/badges/server-art.ts`. All three now go through `rpcWithRetry`, which returns the same `{ data, error }` shape they already destructure, so their bespoke `EMPTY_*` fallbacks are unchanged. The other four entity routes were already fully on the bounded path (swept: 0 bare `.rpc(` in each).

**Verified.** `tsc` clean. Both new behaviours **mutation-proven**: removing the bound reds 4 tests (they hang to vitest's 5s cap — the production symptom reproduced in the suite), and firing the guard at 0ms reds the slow-but-OK case, which proves that case is **not vacuous** (the documented microtask-beats-the-timer trap). New tests stress-run **10/10 stable**. Full primary coverage gate: **3 files / 7 tests failing, byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline** measured by stashing the change and re-running (the documented local-env `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN` reds, green in CI) — **0 threshold errors**. ⚠ Method note: `npm run test:coverage ... | tail` reports **`tail`'s** exit code, not vitest's — it printed a green exit over a red run and briefly hid the 8th failure; that 8th was then shown to be a flake, not my change, only by the stash-and-compare.

**Known remaining (NOT fixed, deliberately scoped):** two `.from()` TABLE reads on the edition page (`fetchPackProvenance`, `fetchOwnerUsernames`) are still unbounded. They sit BELOW the `<Suspense>` boundary, so they cannot cause the reported shell hang — they would strand a lower section, not the skeleton — and bounding PostgREST table builders needs a different helper than this RPC-shaped one.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (code-only; no DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing-MATH change).

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the Panini backup grew past Node's max string length, so the recovery tool it exists to feed could no longer read it

**Shipped** (Cowork cloud authored the patch; both its push routes were closed, so it handed off a verified diff — applied, re-verified against the REAL file, and pushed here).

`scripts/ingest-panini-runner.mjs` — `PANINI_BACKUP_FILE` (`panini-capture.jsonl`) was appended before every POST, on every batch, of every 4-hourly walk, with **no cap, no rotation, no prune-on-success**. Measured on Trevor's box: **1,268,982,254 B (1.21 GiB)**, ~26 days live ⇒ ~46 MB/day. Added `appendBackup()` with `PANINI_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` (default 100 MB) + rotate-to-`.1`. ⚠ **The bound it needed already existed 87 lines below it** — the *optional* ops-capture is correctly capped at 25 MB with one generation (19.8 MB + 26.2 MB on disk, working as designed). The always-on disaster-recovery file, written far more often, got no such treatment.

`scripts/panini-replay.mjs` — rewritten to stream via `readline` over `createReadStream`, and to replay the **rotated generation first** (`.1`, then live) in capture order.

**⚠ DURABLE — the disk was the small half. `readFileSync(FILE,"utf8")` materializes the whole file as ONE JavaScript string, and Node caps a single string at `MAX_STRING_LENGTH` = 536,870,888 B on 64-bit. At 2.36× that, the recovery tool the backup EXISTS to feed threw before POSTing a single batch — a safety net that fails only at the exact moment it is needed** (bad token, walk to recover), and fails silently until then. Verified here against the **actual 1.21 GiB file**, not a fixture: old path `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG`; new path streamed **15,279 batches in 3.7 s, 0 parse failures**.

**Verification:** `node --check` both. Rotation tested against the **verbatim shipped bytes** (extracted with `sed` from the patched file) across caps 30/100/1000 B, one fresh process per cap — pinned: total never exceeds 2× cap, newest batch always retained, fresh file never rotates. Replay tested end-to-end against a local server: ordering `old-1, old-2, new-1, new-2`, blanks skipped, CRLF handled. ⚠ My first rotation harness failed at cap=30 and **the harness was wrong, not the code** — `BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` is a module-load-time `const`, so mutating `process.env` inside a loop never took effect; re-run with a fresh process per cap, all three pass. (Cowork recorded the same class of error on its own first assertion.)

**Scope:** local-only runner scripts on the residential box. No route, DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing change. `panini-capture.jsonl` is gitignored (`.gitignore:125`, `panini*capture*.jsonl*`), so `git add -A` was never at risk.

**Space reclaimed (done, same session): 1,210 MiB.** ⚠ **The fix validated itself in production before I could act on it, and that is the transferable part.** The runner reads `scripts/` straight from the working tree, so its next 4-hourly walk picked up the patched code and the cap **fired on the real 1.21 GiB file**, rotating it to `.1` — confirmation on the actual artifact, not a fixture. It also moved the target between my measurement and the confirmation, and I truncated the **live** file (4.8 MB, mid-walk) before noticing. No loss — the backup is written BEFORE the POST and those POSTs were landing (78 rows in the following 10 min, newest 0.3 min old) — but that was luck, not design: **re-stat a destructive target after any pause, because a live writer can rename it out from under a plan that was correct when it was made.** The 1.21 GiB `.1` was then truncated on the evidence that every batch in it was already ingested (its 17:23 mtime matched the newest `panini_fmv_snapshots` row exactly). ⚠ **Cowork's stated reason for it being safe to delete — "already unrecoverable by the tool that consumes it" — was disproven by this very ship**: streaming replay reads it fine (15,279 batches). Same verdict, different reason; the honest one is "already ingested", not "unreadable". **Unrelated to the `/sessions` no-space shell outage** (Cowork VM disk, not the Windows host) — that is still "delete old Cowork sessions", ~6 nights.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the unbounded append and the slurping replay. No DB unwind. To keep the code but disable the bound, set `PANINI_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` very high.
