### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — the schema-cache 500s are SELF-INFLICTED by our own migrations, and this CORRECTS my own earlier entry

- **Docs + one in-code comment correction.** Read-only measurement; **no DB or behaviour change.**
- ⚠ **THIS CORRECTS THE ENTRY BELOW.** Earlier today I shipped `4f303102` classifying `PGRST002` as transient and described it as fixing `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-1Z` (81 users). The classification is right and should stay — but the measurement here shows it **does not, on its own, absorb the dominant cause**, and both that commit message and its ledger entry read more confidently than the evidence now supports. Recording the correction rather than letting the stronger claim stand.
- **The cause, measured.** Every schema-cache event in the trailing 24 h falls inside **one 11-second window** — 17:20:15 / :21 / :23 / :26 Z, across the pack, edition and player pages. `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` shows `audit_20260813_pack_rips_collection_block_height_index` applied at **17:20:05 Z**. **The first 500 lands 10 s after the migration, the last 21 s after it.** Applying a migration invalidates PostgREST's schema cache; every request served during the re-introspection gets `PGRST002`, which our pages surface as a 500.
- **So these errors are not saturation, not upstream, and not random — we cause them, every time we ship a migration.** That is the entire explanation for 81 users / 84 events accruing since 2026-07-18: a handful of real visitors caught per reload window, across many migrations. Three migrations landed within 11 minutes today.
- ⚠ **Why the retry is necessary but NOT sufficient, arithmetically:** `rpcWithRetry` is 3 attempts at 50 ms + 200 ms ≈ **250 ms of retrying**, against a **~10-20 second** reload window. All three attempts land inside the first quarter-second of a twenty-second outage. **Do not treat `NEXTJS-1Z` as closed by `4f303102`** — expect it on the next migration.
- **In-code comment corrected in the same push.** It previously said "if telemetry shows retries still failing, the next lever is a longer backoff — not taken on speculation." The telemetry now exists, so the comment states the measured window and explicitly says the clause must not be read as "NEXTJS-1Z is solved".
- **Options filed with the trade-off stated, none taken:** (1) lengthen the backoff for this class only (~17 s of coverage fits the 45 s budget) — ⚠ but that converts a 500 into a **~20 s render holding a lambda and pool slot**, with many concurrent requests holding at once; a product/cost call, not an obvious win. (2) Apply migrations in a low-traffic window — cheapest, no code. (3) Accept it, and stop re-investigating it as a mystery.
- ⚠ **Do NOT "fix" it by making the pages fail soft** — the throw is deliberate on all three (deep-audit D10) so a transient failure renders a retryable error boundary rather than a soft-404 that invites Google to drop a real page. That would trade a visible 20 s blip for silent SEO damage.
- **Method note worth keeping:** found by correlating two clocks nobody had put side by side — Sentry event timestamps and `schema_migrations.version` (which encodes applied time as `YYYYMMDDHH24MISS`). **When an error looks like random infrastructure noise, check whether it tracks our own migrations or deploys before blaming the platform.**
- **Filed:** [inbox 2026-08-13T2320Z](inbox/2026-08-13T2320Z-the-schema-cache-500s-are-self-inflicted-by-our-own-migrations.md).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (docs + a comment only — nothing to unwind in prod or the DB).

If the catalog genuinely holds no priced row for the characters under test, a priced deal row really IS unbacked — which is the leak this guard exists to catch. **Only a FAILED read is inconclusive.** Blanket-skipping on empty would have disarmed the guard while appearing to fix it.

Retrying.`** — `NEXTJS-1Z` (pack dist) **81 users / 84 events, first seen 2026-07-18**, plus `NEXTJS-26` (edition, 40 events) and `NEXTJS-20` (player, 12) — ~97 events in 7 days, still firing. Real traffic: a Chrome/Windows user in Singapore on `/nfl-all-day/pack/dist/6510`. **A "new issues only" filter hid the biggest one for being a month old.**
- **The defect: all three paths ALREADY went through `rpcWithRetry`** (`lib/pack-dist/fetchers.ts:246`, `lib/entity-detail-gate.ts:61`) — but `isTransient` matched none of the heuristics against this message (no "timeout", "timed out", "network", "connection pool"), and the code is `PGRST002`, not a SQLSTATE, so the code tests missed it too. **A failure PostgREST itself labels "Retrying." was never retried once, for a month.**
- ⚠ **The careful part — PostgREST has TWO lookalike "schema cache" messages meaning opposite things, and the naive fix gets it wrong.** `PGRST002` "**Could not query** the database for the schema cache" = introspection failed to reach the DB (saturation / just after DDL) → **transient, RETRY**. `PGRST205` "Could not find the table/function … **in the schema cache**" = the cache loaded fine and the object genuinely is not there, a deploy or naming bug → **NEVER retry**; retrying only burns the budget to fail identically. The exclusion is tested FIRST so the broader match cannot swallow it.
- **Mutation-proven in BOTH directions, and the second is the one that matters:** removing the PGRST002 clause reds 2 tests; replacing the precise match with a bare `"schema cache"` substring (the obvious implementation) reds the PGRST205 tests — i.e. the naive version is demonstrably wrong, not just less precise.
- **Safety checked before widening:** `rpcWithRetry` is 3 attempts with 50/200 ms backoff inside the shared 45 s budget, so this adds a bounded amount of work and cannot loop. Noted in-code that if telemetry shows retries still failing, the next lever is a longer backoff for this class specifically — not taken on speculation.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; full suite **1165 files / 11311 tests**; primary gate 91.55 st / 78.91 br / 93.41 fn / 93.67 ln (thresholds 90.4/77.0/92.2/92.6).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the un-retried behaviour. Nothing to unwind in prod or the DB.

So the common path is ~half the cost and the failure path is strictly more informative.

A count merely *below a configured floor* is reported as a threshold breach and explicitly **does not** say "ZERO" (that would be a false statement about the data) and does not pay for the second scan.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — the driver-message leak's guard was scoped to ANON-reachable, not reachable; 110 sites were leaking to signed-in collectors

- **Code + tests to `main`.** 67 route files + `lib/api-error.ts` + 2 new test files; no DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet, or FMV/pricing-MATH change.
- ⚠ **DURABLE — this is the SIXTH filing of this defect, and the first one to find it by asking what the GUARD cannot see rather than where the last person was looking.** `anon-api-no-driver-message-leak-guard` executes the real `isPublicPath` and keeps no route list — genuinely good, and it is exactly why it cannot miss an anon route. But that same design **fixes its scope**: everything behind sign-in was outside it *by construction*. Measured: **158 sites / 97 files** outside `/api/admin` + `/api/cron`, of which **120 across 64 files were user-facing** (the rest are operator-secret-gated, the same rationale that excuses admin/cron).
- ⚠ **One was rendered STRAIGHT INTO A TOAST.** `app/dashboard/page.tsx` throws `data.error` from `/api/profile/trophy/reorder` and shows it — so a statement timeout was displayed to a collector as the reason their trophy case did not save. That route also **branches on the message** to pick 409-vs-500; reading it server-side to classify is fine, publishing it was not, so the 409 now carries its own actionable copy.
- **Applied by a codemod on exact `(file, line)` matches, never a broad regex** — this repo has a documented incident where one hit 351 files instead of 18. It **deferred 13 sites** whose body carried contract keys (`ok:false`, `matched:true`, `code`, `stats`, `rows`, `results`) and those were done by hand. `matched: true` was preserved deliberately: "your listing DID match and only the recording failed" is a different thing to tell a user than "no match".
- ⚠ **The codemod introduced two regressions and BOTH were caught by existing tests, which is the argument for running the full suite rather than the touched files.** (1) It flattened a **502 → 500** in `breaks/{draft,lock}` — the Flow access node is a third-party upstream and that distinction is what tells an operator whether WE broke; 502 + `Retry-After` restored. (2) Its ternary pattern was too permissive and silently dropped `rows: []` / `results: []` from two bodies. That drop turned out to be *correct* (empty data beside a 500 lets a caller who skips `res.ok` render "no market data" from an internal error, same call as `pack-pulls`) — but it is now **deliberate and commented**, not accidental.
- ⚠ **`safeApiError` only knows Postgres, so blanket-applying it DESTROYS an actionable caller error.** Four routes throw their own `"Could not resolve …"` for a bad username; classifying that as `internal` replaced the one thing the user needed to be told with "Something went wrong." and returned **500 for what is a 400**. New `isUnresolvedIdentifierError()` / `unresolvedIdentifierResponse()` in `lib/api-error.ts` — classify on the message server-side, publish **fixed copy**, 400 + `code: "not_found"`.
- **59 existing tests asserted the leak**, two titled *"500s and **surfaces the message**"* — a title that makes the defect read as the contract. Rewritten to `not.toContain(<driver text>)` and retitled.
- **The durable half: `__tests__/helpers/driver-message-leak.ts` is now the ONE source of the five spellings**, imported by both guards. This directly answers the recorded failure where the anon guard shipped with four spellings against its predecessor's five and 12 sites kept leaking — a new spelling now widens both guards at once. New `authed-api-no-driver-message-leak-guard` covers the signed-in surface, **asserts its own operator-exclusions really carry a secret gate**, and asserts the anon guard's set is a **subset** of its own so no route falls between them. Mutation-proven (re-introducing the leak in `/api/portfolio` reds it).
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; full suite **1153 files / 11000 tests**; primary gate 91.17 st / 77.99 br / 92.88 fn / 93.34 ln (thresholds 90.4/77.0/92.2/92.6); component gate 89.97/81.34/88.74/92.89 (88.5/79.4/88.2/91.6). Re-swept: user-facing leak sites **120 → 0**; 32 operator files / 37 sites remain deliberately.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED — CODE ONLY, DEPLOY DELIBERATELY WITHHELD (Claude Code, interactive) — `compute-pinnacle-pack-ev` duplicate-conflict-key upsert

- **The defect.** `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` may not touch one target row twice, so a single duplicated `dist_id` in the batch aborts the WHOLE statement with `21000 ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time` and discards every other row in the chunk. The throw also skips Phase 3b, so **no `pack_ev_history` row was written either**. Live: 100% failing, identical error on every tick since the last successful write at **2026-08-11 06:17Z**; `pack_distributions` for Pinnacle is 143 rows all stamped that instant. Bounded to Pinnacle pack-EV staleness — no corruption, and unlike the catalog-walker bug this one **logged its error honestly**, which is why it was caught in 2 days rather than by accident.
- **The fix.** New `supabase/functions/_shared/upsert-dedupe.ts` → `dedupeByConflictKey(rows, key)`, wired into Phase 3a. **Last occurrence wins**, so the batched form matches what a sequential per-row upsert would have left. `collection_id` is constant for this function, so `dist_id` alone is the key — the helper's contract requires the key fn use the same columns as the `onConflict` string.
- **⚠ The dedupe is COUNTED, not silent.** `dist_dupe_count` + a 5-key `dist_dupe_sample` now ride both `pipeline_runs.extra` payloads. Quietly collapsing the rows would trade a loud deterministic failure for an invisible one — the exact class fixed on the Top Shot catalog walker the same day. **If `dist_dupe_count` stays non-zero, the studio-platform walk is emitting two nodes under one `dist_id` and THAT is the thing to investigate; this fix stops the crash, it does not explain the duplicate.**
- **Scope checked, not assumed:** the three sibling pack-EV functions (`compute-allday`/`golazos`/`topshot-pack-ev`) carry **no** `onConflict` upsert, so this shape is unique to Pinnacle. `evRows` is deliberately NOT deduped — `pack_ev_history` is append-only history and two listing uuids under one dist is a real upstream state, not a conflict.
- **⚠ NOT DEPLOYED, and the reason is a hard coupling — do not deploy this file alone.** `compute-pinnacle-pack-ev` is **jobid 42, one of D2b's five un-rotated functions**: the repo copy reads `PINNACLE_PACK_EV_GATE_KEY`, that secret is **not set**, and the gate fails CLOSED. Deploying now would turn a deterministic SQL failure into a **403 on every tick** — strictly worse. The deploy must ride the rotation window (set the secret → deploy → repoint the pg_cron `?key=`), or at minimum the operator sets `PINNACLE_PACK_EV_GATE_KEY` to the currently-deployed literal first. Until then Pinnacle pack EV stays frozen at 08-11 06:17Z and the alert stays honestly red.
- **Tests.** `__tests__/edge-upsert-dedupe.test.ts` (8 cases) pins upsert-safety, last-wins, the collision count, the sample cap, first-seen key order, and that `7` and `"7"` collapse to one key (the fn builds `dist_id` with `String(node.id)`, so type-split keys would still be one target row in Postgres). Required anyway by the `edge-shared-test-completeness` rot-guard, which reds CI on any untested `_shared` module.
- **Verified.** `tsc --noEmit` clean; dedupe + rot-guard tests 12/12. ⚠ `deno check` NOT run locally (deno is not installed on this box and `jsr.io` is proxy-blocked) — the blocking `edge-deno` CI job is the check. The new module has zero imports, so the risk is confined to the one added import line.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — removes the dedupe + counters and deletes the `_shared` module and its test. No DB, cron or deploy change to unwind (nothing was deployed).

### 2026-08-13 · reconcile-saved-wallet-stats soft deadline 100s → 50s (fixes intermittent 120s hard-abort)

`rpc-reconcile-saved-wallet-stats` (pg_cron jobid 259, runs as `postgres`) was flapping to cron
status `failed` on saturated days (2026-08-09 and 2026-08-12, both **exactly 120.0s** = the global
`statement_timeout`; postgres has no role-level override, and `cron_heavy`'s 600s is unreachable
because the proc is invoker-rights, directly writes RLS-protected `saved_wallets`, and `cron_heavy`
is not BYPASSRLS). Root cause: per-wallet `aggregate_saved_wallet_stats` costs **16–55s** under IO
saturation (EXPLAIN: the top-tier correlated subquery does a Bitmap Heap Scan + Sort per collection,
~70% of the plan; the 43k-moment whale wallet `0xf77bf547fccf6656` is the worst case), while the
soft deadline (100s) is only checked BETWEEN wallets — so a single expensive wallet entered near the
100s mark pushed cumulative time past the 120s hard cap and aborted the whole CALL.

Fix: lowered `p_max_seconds` default **100 → 50** in `reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats` — leaves ~70s
of headroom below the 120s cap for the in-flight wallet, converting the straddle-abort into a clean
`succeeded` truncation (partial progress already commits per-wallet; stalest-first resumes next run).
Body byte-identical otherwise: invoker-rights (COMMIT requires it), no SET clause, same signature →
grants preserved (`postgres` + `service_role` only, verified; not anon/authenticated). Structural
fixes were re-checked and remain correctly declined: array_agg fold (−21%, loses index-only outer
scan — `tier` not in `idx_wmc_cohort_cover`), tier covering index (HOT write amplification on 2.2M-row
wmc), cron_heavy (RLS/BYPASSRLS), schedule move (13:33Z not structurally congested).

Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260813150925_audit_20260813_reconcile_saved_wallet_stats_lower_soft_deadline.sql`
(applied to prod as version `20260813150925`; committed file matches by name — commit it to close the
`migration-parity` window).

Residual (NOT fixed, monitored): a single wallet whose aggregate alone exceeds ~70s under extreme
saturation could still abort — unavoidable without the declined structural work; Check 7 (daily
onboarding watch) surfaces a recurrence. Behavioral proof is the next scheduled run (06:33 PT
2026-08-14) reading `succeeded`; the deployment (new default, invoker, no-SET, grants) is verified.

**Revert (NOT `git revert` — the migration file is not yet committed):**
```
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE public.reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats(
  IN p_max_seconds integer DEFAULT 100, IN p_max_wallets integer DEFAULT 500, IN p_min_age_minutes integer DEFAULT 360)
-- ...restore the identical body with DEFAULT 100...
```
i.e. re-apply the prior definition with `p_max_seconds DEFAULT 100`, and delete the migration file.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the catalog walker can no longer report a total upstream refusal as a clean run

- **What.** `app/api/admin/backfill-topshot-catalog/route.ts`: `fetchEditionsPage` returned `… | null`, collapsing "this set has no editions" and "we could not ask" into one value. `walkSet` broke on it, the loop counted the set processed, and the run logged `ok:true`. That is why the 2026-08-11 malformed-query bug (`description` selected on `PlayStats`, which 422s the whole query) produced two live runs reading `sets_processed=257 / gql_calls=257 / editions_upserted=0 / errors_count=0` and looked clean. - **Change.** `fetchEditionsPage` now returns a discriminated `PageFetch` carrying a `fault` string (HTTP status + body, or the GQL error message — for a malformed query the upstream body NAMES the offending field and was being thrown away). `walkSet` propagates `fault` alongside `editions`, so a genuinely empty set (`editions: []`, `fault: null`) is distinguishable from a refused one. New `sets_faulted` counter in both the `pipeline_runs.extra` and the HTTP payload.
- **`ok` deliberately does NOT redden on a single fault.** Top Shot GQL is intermittently flaky and a chronically-red pipeline trains the operator to skim past it — the lesson already paid for with `ufc_fmv_stale_hours`. It reddens on an upsert error, or on **every walked set faulting**, which cannot be upstream noise and is exactly the 08-11 shape. Partial faults stay visible in `errors_count` / `errors_sample` / `sets_faulted` without flipping the flag.
- **Tests (the gap that let this ship).** `b1018e63` fixed the query but touched no route test, so nothing pinned the field's DEPTH. Both new guards mutation-tested (revert either and the suite reds).

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED — **the PRIMITIVE, not a third instance** (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 23) · `summarizeDegraded` silently dropped any status that said "I succeeded, and I know I was cut short"

CLAUDE.md's board-status bullet now records the `ok` = USABLE rule, that `partial` is honoured regardless of `ok`, that a filled `.limit()` is a truncated ranking, and that **candy's caps are not all the 600 default** (serials 607/**800**, holders 395/**800**).

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — **HONESTY FIX + coverage** (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 21) · the same moment could show a DIFFERENT P&L on a phone than on a desktop — and the test covering it ran on an impossible fixture

- **⚠ Found by writing the test.** `components/collection/CollectionMomentTable.tsx` derived the mobile card's P&L basis as `const basis = label === "Loan" ? cb.buyPrice : cb.buyPrice` — **a ternary whose two branches are identical**, i.e. `cb.buyPrice` unconditionally. The DESKTOP P&L column derives the same number through the shared, named **`resolveMomentPnlBasis()`**, whose rule is deliberately narrower: only a `"Bought"`/`"Loan"` cost-basis amount is trusted as a purchase price, otherwise fall back to `lastPurchasePrice`. The helper was written for the desktop column and **never applied to the mobile tree**.
- **The divergence is reachable and common.** The component's own `cb` fallback builds `{ buyPrice: row.costBasis, costBasisLabel: row.costBasisLabel ?? null }`, and `ACQUISITION_METHOD_LABEL` maps `unknown → null`. So an **unlabelled cost-basis amount** is a real shape — and on it, mobile computed a P&L off `buyPrice` while desktop ignored that amount and used `lastPurchasePrice`. **Two different profit figures for the same moment, decided by screen width.** Same family as the mobile empty state fixed earlier today: this file renders two separate trees and the second one drifts because it is maintained by hand.
- **⚠ My first fix was too blunt and a sibling test caught it.** Swapping in the helper also removed the **cost figure**, because desktop splits these across TWO columns (a Cost cell showing any positive `buyPrice`, and a separate P&L cell) while the mobile card renders both in one block. Deriving one from the other is exactly what caused the original divergence. Now split: `pnlBasis` gates the P&L line, `cb.buyPrice > 0` still renders the amount — **omitting a real number is not the way to avoid a fabricated one.**
- **⚠ DURABLE — the sibling test passed on a label that DOES NOT EXIST.** `component-CollectionMomentTable-mobile-expanded` paired `acquisitionMethod: "pack_pull"` with `costBasisLabel: **"Pack pull"**`. The real vocabulary is exactly `Bought | Pack | Loan | Gift | Reward | Airdrop | null` (`ACQUISITION_METHOD_LABEL`, `lib/analytics/shape.ts` — `pack_pull → "Pack"`). "Pack pull" matched no chip branch and fell through to the generic cost path, so the test asserted a code path **real data never reaches** — the same passing-test-on-an-impossible-fixture shape **deep-audit D9** recorded, found independently. Repointed to `"Bought"`, which genuinely shows a cost figure, so the assertion keeps its meaning. **A green test proves nothing if its fixture is unreachable — check a label against the map that produces it.**
- **Also pinned:** the four acquisition chips (PACK / GIFT / REWARD / AIRDROP) return BEFORE any P&L is computed, which is correct — a pulled, gifted or airdropped moment has no purchase price, and "+$200" against a $0 basis would be a fabricated gain on **every pack pull a collector owns**. Plus no-FMV → no P&L (unknown, not a loss) and no NaN/Infinity from a zero basis.
- **Mutation-proven:** restoring the no-op ternary reds exactly the two parity tests (unlabelled-basis, and the `lastPurchasePrice` fallback).
- **Coverage:** CollectionMomentTable branches **83.9% → 85.0%**; component gate **81.29 → 81.34**, 1,550 → 1,560 tests.
- **Verified.** `tsc` clean · primary gate **1150 files / 10,966 tests, exit 0** · component gate **185 files / 1,560 tests, exit 0**. No DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet, or FMV/pricing-MATH change.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the no-op ternary and the single-block cost/P&L render. No DB unwind.

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — **HONESTY FIX + coverage** (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 20) · the Candy board's row cap truncated a RANKING with no signal — a margin that had been re-raised twice instead of fixed

- **`app/insights/candy-mlb/CandyBoardClient.tsx`'s `DataTable` applies `r.slice(0, cap)` AFTER sorting**, so an overflow is **invisible by construction**: every row on screen is still correct, the board just stops. This repo already names the class — *"truncating a ranked board silently is worse than blanking it, because every number on screen still looks right."*
- **⚠ The file's own comments are the evidence it kept recurring.** Two call sites carry notes reading *"DataTable slices silently (`r.slice(0, cap)`) with no 'showing N of M' indicator"* — and the response both times was to **raise that one cap** (550→800, 250→800). That is a **data-dependent margin, not a guarantee**, and it only holds until the data grows: the **scarcity tab sits at cap 130 against 125 editions**, and CLAUDE.md records Candy as expecting further drops. Meanwhile the Market tab in the SAME file already renders "Showing N of M matching editions" — the honest pattern existed and simply had not been pushed down into the shared component.
- **Fixed structurally, once, in `DataTable`:** when `rows.length > cap` it renders "Showing the top N of M rows for this sort — this list is **capped, not complete**" (`role="status"`). A future overflow now announces itself instead of quietly shortening a ranking, and no future editor has to remember to re-raise a number. **Deliberately silent at `rows.length === cap`** — that board IS complete, and a permanent "capped" note would be its own false claim that trains the reader to ignore it.
- **Also pinned (behaviour that was already correct, and is easy to "simplify" into wrongness):** `DataTable` sorts NULLs to the **bottom in BOTH directions** via `x == null ? (asc ? Infinity : -Infinity)`. A naive `null → 0` floats unpriced rows to the top of an **ascending price sort**, presenting *"we have no price for this"* as *"this is the cheapest"* on a deals-oriented board — mutation-proven, that exact change reds the ascending test only. Plus `usd()` rendering an em-dash for null / NaN / **non-positive** (a `$0` is the absence of a market price, not a price) and its cents-below-$100 threshold.
- **⚠ A repo guard caught my copy before CI did.** `component-CandyBoardClient.test.tsx` carries a JSX-whitespace assertion: a text run that starts after `}` and wraps onto another line loses its space. My first draft of the notice did exactly that. Restructured rather than suppressed — the guard is right.
- **⚠ Method failure, mine, twice in one file: I inferred a prop shape instead of reading it.** Mounted with an `initial={{...}}` envelope; the component takes **flat props** (`initialRows`, `fetchedAt`, nine optional row arrays). All 9 tests failed at once, which is the tell. Same class as the ProfileClient sort-order guess an hour earlier — **read the signature.** Also: `echo "TSC=$?"` after a pipe into `head` reports HEAD's exit, not tsc's, and printed a green `0` over a real `TS2698`. The explicit `TSC=$?; [ "$TSC" -ne 0 ] && exit 1` guard is the only form that works.

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — **HONESTY FIX + coverage** (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 19) · a public profile could report **"↑ 50000.0% / 30D"** — `|| 1` as a divide-by-zero guard

- **⚠ Found by writing the test for it.** `app/profile/[username]/ProfileClient.tsx` computed its 30-day portfolio change as `((last - first) / (first || 1)) * 100`. **A ZERO baseline silently became a $1 baseline**, so a collector whose first snapshot was `$0` — a newly saved wallet, or one snapshotted before the FMV populate ran — had a rise to $500 rendered as **"↑ 50000.0% / 30D"** on a page they SHARE. A percentage change from zero is **undefined, not enormous**, and `|| 1` is precisely the shape that converts "undefined" into a confident number.
- **The fix omits the percentage and KEEPS the sparkline**, because the *shape* is real even when the ratio is not. ⚠ **That forced a second, easy-to-miss half:** the sparkline colour read `sparkChange != null && sparkChange >= 0`, so a null change fell through to RED — painting a genuine $0→$500 gain as a loss. Direction is knowable even when the ratio is not, so it now derives from the series (`last >= first`). Both halves are separately mutation-proven; restoring either reds its own test.
- **⚠ Deliberately NOT collapsed with the flat case.** `[300, 300]` still reports **"↑ 0.0%"** — that change really IS zero and saying so is information. Only the *uncomputable* case is suppressed. A fix that hid both would have passed the regression test while deleting the feature, which is why every case here has a positive mirror.
- **Coverage (the reason I was in this file):** `ProfileClient` was the largest remaining component-gate gap on a user-facing page — **68.4% → 79.9% branches, 55 → 36 uncovered**. Also pinned: wallet-list ordering (registry LABEL then FMV desc), unknown-collection → "Multi" rather than leaking a raw uuid, the positional "Wallet N" fallback, the RPC-score colour bands at their **inclusive 800/500 boundaries**, score ABSENT (not 0) when no wallet carries one, and own-profile gating of the private Cost-Basis card — **case-insensitively**, since session-username casing must not decide whether spend and P/L are exposed.
- **⚠ Method note: I guessed a sort order instead of reading it, and the test caught me.** I asserted All Day sorts before Top Shot; the key is the registry **label**, so `"NBA Top Shot" < "NFL All Day"` and Top Shot comes first. Same class as the fixture-shape errors earlier in this session — **read the source of the ordering, do not infer it from the slug.**
- **Coordination:** deliberately worked the component layer because a concurrent session is active in `lib/insights/**`, the API routes, the concierge and the DB — that area cost me one full duplication and three rebase conflicts earlier today.
- **Verified.** `tsc` clean · primary gate **1148 files / 10,941 tests, exit 0** · component gate **183 files / 1,541 tests, exit 0** (branches 81.04 → **81.24**). No DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet, or FMV/pricing-MATH change.

- **⚠ DURABLE — `warmBoard` carried an error ONLY when the live closure THREW, and these fetchers never throw.** They reduce a PostgrestError to `ok: !error` and drop it (`if (!res.ok) return { key, ok: false, rowCount }`). So the `ok:false` path — the overwhelmingly common one — was structurally incapable of reporting a cause. **The same class this session has been sweeping, pointed at the instrument instead of the user:** a failure recorded as a bare fact with the reason discarded.
- **Sharpened:** the two worst boards were the only two with **no error instrumentation at all**. Candy and Panini `console.error` each view (that is why their timeouts show up in Sentry); `boards.ts` (deals / rookies / first-mint) logged nothing and propagated nothing. We had no information about why the two worst-performing public boards fail.
- **Shipped:** `BoardLiveResult.error?` + `describeBoardFailures()` in [lib/insights/board-cache.ts](lib/insights/board-cache.ts); `warmBoard` propagates it on the `ok:false` path; all five fetchers populate it, **naming WHICH backing query failed** (these boards run 2–10 sub-queries, so "which one" is the whole diagnostic value). Panini additionally distinguishes its two different declines — view **errored** vs. **partial ranking hit the page cap** — which were previously indistinguishable and imply different fixes.
- **⚠ Deliberate: the driver message DOES belong here.** It lands in `pipeline_runs.error`, a service-role-only table — the LOG side of the same rule `lib/api-error.ts` enforces on the response side (classify what you publish, keep the detail where an operator can read it). `readBoardOrLive` ignores the field so no consumer can publish it. Recorded in the type's doc comment so a future reader does not "fix" it as a leak.
- **Verified.** 7 new tests, **all mutation-proven** (dropped the propagation / made `describeBoardFailures` blame every part / removed deals' field → each reds; restore → green). `tsc` clean; primary gate **1147 files, exit 0**; component gate 182 files / 1526 tests.
- **NOT shipped, deliberately — a tidy story that the data refused.** The obvious hypothesis was that `*/5` warming of 5 heavy boards is wasteful and self-inflicting under an IO-starved instance (runs average **~32s**, max 65.6s, i.e. a ~11% permanent duty cycle). But the pages are ISR `revalidate = 300` with `s-maxage=300` on the routes — **the cadence exactly matches what a consumer can observe**, so there is no waste to reclaim, and a cadence change would have been a plausible-sounding regression. Serializing the `Promise.all` was likewise left alone: contention is a *hypothesis*, and at 32s parallel a serial run would blow the 60s `maxDuration`. **The reason instrumentation shipped here is precisely what makes that question answerable next time.**
- **Code + tests only — no DB, cron, auth, or prod-state change. Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

- **What.** Every client dashboard under `/analytics` fetched with a variant of `fetch(url).then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : null).catch(() => {})`, which collapses a network failure, a 5xx, an unparseable body and a genuinely empty result into one indistinguishable value — and each then rendered a **sentence** off it. - **⚠ Why the earlier sweeps missed this whole surface.** It is the SAME class the `/insights` work closed server-side (`lib/insights/board-status.ts`), but the client failure path is a `.catch` inside a `useEffect`, not an `if (error)` in a server page — so **the grep that found every server instance finds none of these**. Same defect, different spelling, different directory.

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — test coverage (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 9) · the concierge's constant-time header checks + bot-DM identity bridge — and TWO vacuous-pass traps caught in my own test

**What it covers.** `isTrustedBotRequest` is the sharp edge of the concierge: when it validates **AND** `pageContext === "bot_dm"`, the route **TRUSTS `body.ownerId` / `body.ownerKey` as the caller's identity**. The Telegram/Discord bridge has no auth cookie, so `deriveIdentity()` can never see the linked user — that header is the only thing standing between "bridge-resolved owner" and "client-supplied owner". If it returned true for a wrong or absent secret, **any anonymous caller could assert an arbitrary owner and reach that user's owner-scoped tools**. Same shape for `isSmokeTestRequest`, where mis-flagging real traffic as synthetic silently drops it from the support corpus and the quota accounting.

So the assertions are deliberately **mostly NEGATIVE** — wrong secret, absent header, empty header, length-mismatched secret, BOTH server secrets unset, and valid-secret-but-`pageContext:"web"` must each fail to confer identity. **A positive-only test would pass just as happily against `return true`.**

⚠ **TWO vacuous-pass traps, found in my own test and worth keeping:**
1. **`persistConversation` runs inside `after()`**, and the conventional `after: () => {}` stub means **nothing is ever persisted** — so every "must NOT confer identity" assertion passed *because no row existed at all*. The mock now EXECUTES the callback and its promises are drained before asserting.
2. **`body.ownerId` and `body.ownerKey` are DIFFERENT fields landing in different places** (`userId` vs the persisted `owner_key` column). Asserting `owner_key` while sending only `ownerId` yields null either way — the negatives passed for the wrong reason a second time.

⚠ **The tell in both cases: the POSITIVES failed while the NEGATIVES stayed green.** That asymmetry is the signature of a test asserting against nothing. If a suite's "must not" cases pass on the first run and its "must" cases don't, suspect the fixture before the code.

**Mutation-tested:** forcing `isTrustedBotRequest` to `return true` fails the refusal cases; inverting the length check in `isSmokeTestRequest` fails the mis-flag case. Route restored byte-clean (`git diff --stat` empty).

⚠ **Method note:** `tsc` failed on the first commit attempt (a heterogeneous header-array literal) and the run STOPPED before committing — the `[ "$TSC" -ne 0 ] && exit 1` guard added after the cont. 7 mistake did its job.

**Verification:** primary gate **exit 0**, **1,135 files / 10,810 tests**, buffers +0.69…+0.85; `tsc` clean. support-chat branches 68.7% → **70.2%**. No app code changed.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — test-only.

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — test coverage (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 8) · the Trophy-Case PDF art pipeline · branches 48.4% → 73.3%

`fetchMomentArt` was the densest uncovered cluster left in the primary gate (**143 uncovered branches**) and it is the art path of a **Pro deliverable** — the exportable Trophy Case. It is module-private, so it is driven through `GET` with REAL PNG/JPEG bytes (pngjs, the same encoder the route uses) and a **recording** fetch stub.

**The assertions that carry weight are about WHICH network calls happen**, because the two rules here are network rules:
1. ⚠ **A Pinnacle render must NEVER be fetched directly.** The asset CDN 403s all datacenter egress, so the only server-usable source is the browser-harvested `pinnacle_render_cache`; a direct attempt burns the **6s timeout budget per slab** on a response that cannot succeed. Asserted on both a cache HIT and a cache **MISS** — the miss is the one that matters, because "fall through to a direct fetch" is the tempting wrong fix and it would look like a robustness improvement.
2. **Non-Pinnacle art IS fetched, with a browser `User-Agent`.** Some Dapper CDNs bot-block a UA-less request, and the failure mode is a **silently art-less export**, not an error.

Plus the degradation ladder — 404 / empty body / non-image bytes / thrown socket / **corrupt cache row** / >10MB — each of which must still emit a valid `%PDF`, because a missing thumbnail can never cost the user their whole export.

**Result: 48.4% → 73.3% branches** (143 → 74 uncovered), statements → 87.6%, functions → 82.3%.

⚠ **Method note (the second instance of this class today):** Node accepts a `Buffer` as a `Response` body at RUNTIME but the DOM `BodyInit` type does not — the tests all passed while `tsc` failed with TS2345. Every image body is now wrapped in a `Uint8Array` view. **A green test run is not a green typecheck**, and this time I checked the exit code BEFORE committing rather than after (see the cont. 7 entry for what happens otherwise).

### 2026-08-11 · SHIPPED — code (Claude Code, interactive) · the D3 driver-message leak was SURFACE-WIDE on `/api/public/insights/**` (29 routes, THREE shapes) — closed + source-guarded; plus 5 smaller corrections and an unbreak of `main`'s CI

**The leak was ~5× bigger than filed.** The follow-up I filed earlier today scoped it to the six single-view boards. Sweeping the directory found it in **all 29 public insights routes**, in **three shapes** — which is why a grep for the obvious one found less than half:
1. `{ error: error.message }` (14 sites)
2. `const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` → `{ error: msg }` (10 sites)
3. `{ error }` **shorthand where `error` is already a bare string** — `lib/supabase-paginate` returns `error: string` (4 sites: market, topshot-pack-market, allday-pack-market, allday-pack-reality)
Plus `pack-reality`, which published a per-source `errors[]` of driver messages into `meta.errors` on its **200** response. All 29 now route through one new helper.

**New: `lib/insights/board-error.ts` → `boardUnavailable(err, board, fallback?)`.** New/edited public-insights failure paths MUST use it. Two things it adds over a bare `safeApiError()` call, both load-bearing:
- ⚠ **`Cache-Control: no-store`.** Every one of these routes sets a PUBLIC edge cache (`s-maxage` 300..3600) on success. Without an explicit no-store on the failure, a transient 503 risks being held at the CDN and served to everyone for the rest of the TTL — **pinning a momentary blip into a sustained outage.**
- ⚠ **String normalization.** `safeApiError`'s message reader only understands `Error` and objects with `.message`; a **bare string** (shape 3) fell through to `internal`, so a statement timeout was reported as a hard 500 instead of a retryable 503. Pinned by a test that fails without it.

**Blast radius of the old behavior:** these are anon-readable routes AND the concierge's `fetchPublicInsight` forwards `json.error` straight into the model's tool result — so Postgres's own "canceling statement due to statement timeout" reached both visitors and the assistant.

**Guarded, not just fixed:** `__tests__/public-insights-no-driver-message-leak-guard.test.ts` walks the directory and fails on any of the four leak spellings. ⚠ A source test because **no type forbids this** — `error` is a string and putting a string in a response body type-checks perfectly, so `tsc` can never catch a regression, and a behavioural fixture would need writing per route (29 of them). It asserts `files.length > 20` first so it can't pass vacuously. Both new tests are mutation-proven.

**Also corrected (each verified, not assumed):**
- ⚠ **`main`'s CI was RED on the blocking `unit-tests` job** — `edge-fn-no-hardcoded-gate-keys.test.ts` failed on clean HEAD (`caf9da34`), proven by stashing my diff. All 8 pack edge fns are genuinely fail-closed (`!!k && ((GATE !== "" && k === GATE) || …)`); the TEST only knew the `!GATE ||` / `!!GATE &&` spellings and reported 8 SAFE functions as offenders. I widened the accepted idioms, then **a concurrent session landed a strictly better fix and I took theirs instead**: it EXECUTES the real `gateKeyOk` helper under set/unset secrets rather than pattern-matching, and pins `executed === 8` so the extraction cannot silently stop covering anything. Their reasoning is the right one — a syntactic proxy breaks on a refactor AND would pass a rewrite that kept the spelling while breaking the logic. My edit to that file was dropped in the rebase.
- ⚠ **`app/api/topshot-listing-cache/route.ts`: a pre-authorized deletion whose PREMISE IS FALSE.** Its note said the wallet-verification matcher "is effectively a no-op — cached_listings is frozen (Flowty shut 2026-05-13)" and was "safe to delete". Deleting would have dropped a **working backstop**. It has never fired, but for a different reason: all 9 `wallet_verification_challenges` resolved `expired` (8) or `gql_on_demand` (1) because the on-demand GQL route gets there first. ### 2026-08-11 · SHIPPED — test coverage (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 4) · guards for the two CI-gating SCRIPTS that had none (`check-brand-tokens`, `check-migration-parity`)

**The class: a guard that quietly stops guarding does not fail.** Both scripts run in CI (brand-tokens in the **BLOCKING** `typecheck` job; migration-parity daily), both are pure regex/parsing, and neither had a test. When such a script's pattern stops matching it prints "N surface(s) clean" / "0 drift" and exits 0 — a weakened guard and a genuinely clean repo are **byte-identical to CI**. Same failure shape as the pin-staleness parser blind spot that silently dropped 2 pins from the live-drift check.

**Technique (both):** read the script's ACTUAL regexes/functions out of its source and exercise them, rather than restating them in the test — a restated copy drifts and then asserts nothing, which is the very defect being guarded against. Precedent: `db-pin-staleness-parser-coverage.test.ts`.

- **`check-brand-tokens-detection.test.ts` (18 cases).** Covers all five patterns — LITERAL, FALLBACK, VAR_FALLBACK (incl. the nested-`rgba()` paren case, where a naive `/var\([^)]*\)/` would stop at rgba's first `)` and false-positive on correct code), NEUTRAL (incl. the **deliberate** `rgba(0,0,0,*)` allowance for scrims/shadows, pinned so a future "tighten this" pass sees it is a decision), TAILWIND_NEUTRAL (incl. the raw zinc scale, and that semantic classes are NOT flagged — a guard that flags the correct answer trains people to add exceptions) — plus the 3-line `brand-exception` window **including the 4-lines-above negative case**, and both PROTECTED lists against stale entries. Mutation-tested: dropping a font from LITERAL, and widening the exception window, each caught.
- **`check-migration-parity-logic.test.ts` (11 cases).** Pins the TWO defects the script's own header records, both of which kept it passing while blind: (1) it used to match on **VERSION** — `apply_migration` stamps its own version, so a committed file's timestamp legitimately differs and a version match reports real files missing forever; (2) it used to read `readdirSync`, so a file on disk but never `git add`ed satisfied it — **exactly the state the job exists to catch** (observed 2026-08-10: two candy pack-EV migrations untracked while the 3-day window reported 0). Also pins: a git failure is UNKNOWN/null and **never** parity, UNTRACKED stays distinct from MISSING (different operator actions — `git add` vs recover-SQL-from-prod), the window stays bounded (unbounded it reports ~2,000 findings and becomes noise), `process.exitCode` not `process.exit()` (the documented Windows libuv footgun), and `KNOWN_FILELESS` entries carry a reason. Mutation-tested: reverting to `readdirSync`, and matching on version, each caught.

⚠ **Method note worth keeping:** my first exitCode assertion FAILED because the script *documents* the `process.exit()` footgun in prose and the regex matched the comment. Strip comments before asserting on source, or the test asserts the opposite of what it means.

**Verification:** both suites green; `tsc` clean. **No script was changed** — both restored byte-clean after mutation testing (`git diff --stat scripts/` empty).

### 2026-08-11 · SHIPPED — test coverage (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 3) · the sitemap route handlers were outside `app/api`, so BOTH gates missed them — SEO surface, silent failure mode

**A route handler is a FILE convention, not a directory one.** `app/sitemap.xml/route.ts` (the `<sitemapindex>` at the **GSC-registered URL**) and `app/sitemap/[id]/route.ts` (its five segment children) live outside `app/api`, so the gate's `app/api/**/route.ts` glob never matched them and neither had a test. It also pins the index against the child route's `SITEMAP_SEGMENT_IDS` — the two are declared in **different files**, and drift is invisible until Search Console reports missing pages.

Recorded as ACTUAL behaviour rather than asserted as a contract — nothing links it (the index emits only 0–4), so no crawler reaches it, and tightening the regex would be a change to live SEO routing for a URL that is never requested. Deliberately not "fixed" on my own initiative.

### 2026-08-11 · NO-OP / SUPERSEDED (Claude Code, interactive) · diagnosed the red `main` gate-key arm as a FALSE POSITIVE; a concurrent session shipped a better fix, so mine was dropped

Recording this because the DIAGNOSIS is worth keeping even though the fix was not mine.

`main` was RED on the blocking `unit-tests` job (7 of 8 CI jobs green; 1 failing test of 10,645): `every gate comparison fails CLOSED when the secret is unset` reported all 8 pack-pipeline edge fns as unguarded. **Not caused by the test-coverage pass in the entries above** — the identical failure is present on `b7ec294d`, which predates that work, and none of its commits touch any `supabase/functions/**/index.ts`.

**The arm was wrong; the code was right.** The check accepted only `!GATE ||` or `!!GATE &&`. The dual-accept rotation refactor moved the identical guard inline and per-key — `!!k && ((GATE !== "" && k === GATE) || (GATE_OLD !== "" && k === GATE_OLD))` — which is **stricter** than the early-return it replaced (it guards the OUTGOING key too). So CI reddened on a change that had *improved* the security posture. Verified by reading all 8: each rejects both an empty caller key and an unset secret.

**My fix (a third accepted pattern, `<CONST> !== ""`) was DROPPED in favour of the concurrent session's `e30bc73d`, which is better:** it EXECUTES the extracted guard under set/unset secret combinations instead of pattern-matching the spelling. That is the right call for the reason their commit states — a syntactic guard breaks on a refactor *and* would PASS a rewrite that kept the spelling while breaking the logic. Taking theirs and discarding mine avoids two sessions layering competing fixes on one security arm. Their version verified green locally (7/7).

⚠ Durable, regardless of whose fix landed: **a permanently-red security arm is not harmless** — it trains readers to wave it through, which is exactly how a real unset gate would later slip past. Same class as the `ufc_fmv_stale_hours` permanent-red retirement.

**Revert:** nothing to revert — no code shipped from this session for this item.
### 2026-08-11 · QUEUED (decision) — STALE FMV label is dropped at the wmc denorm boundary; $167k of Golazos value renders unlabeled on a public surface

Filed `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-12T0358Z-stale-label-lost-in-wmc-denorm.md`. Read-only investigation — no code/DB/prod change, so no revert path.

**CONFIRMED:** `wallet_moments_cache` has no confidence column and `populate_wmc_fmv_from_snapshots` never references one (`SET fmv_usd = lf.fmv_usd`), so `fmv_current.confidence` is structurally unavailable at the point portfolios are summed — **platform-wide by construction, not Golazos-specific**. `get_wallet_collection_snapshot`, the RPC behind anon-public `/share/[wallet]`, emits per-collection `fmv` with no confidence field at all; 9 of 10 portfolio-summing RPCs never mention confidence; **34 fns** sum `wmc.fmv_usd`. Golazos exposure: 177 copies / 10 wallets / 28 editions / **$167,420.50**, reaching **80%** of one wallet's entire displayed Golazos total.

**CORRECTED vs the original cloud filing (acting on it would have destroyed real data):** (1) the writer did NOT stall — `drain_fmv_cold_tail` (7-day eligibility) and `apply_fmv_thin_sales_guard` **oscillate every ~7 days at byte-identical values**, and the guard's `stale_30d_no_ask` branch does `v_cap := rec.fmv_usd` — value UNCHANGED, confidence already STALE from cold-tail — so the guard is a **pure no-op duplicate** and is not the author of these numbers; (2) the "$1,015 vs $0.85, ~1,200× the market" claim pairs LEGENDARY at median circ **35** against COMMON at median circ **10,000**, and there were **0 LEGENDARY Golazos sales in 90 days**; (3) the values are genuine historical medians sitting **below their own last prints** (Benzema LEGENDARY /45 → $4,500 vs a real $6,500 print in 2023). **The price is not the defect; the missing label is. Do not re-price or null them.**

**Decision owed (Trevor):** A = carry `confidence` onto wmc (correct, but INCLUDE/predicate cols block HOT on a hot 2.2M-row table — size first) · B = null the STALE denorm (destroys last-known-value, understates real holdings) · C = disclose at the surface (cheapest honest option, Panini "floor, not a census" precedent). Recommend **A then C**. ⚠ The larger sibling must be decided in the same pass: `ask_only_v2` carries **$135,271 across 2,964 copies** in Golazos alone, equally unlabeled, plus a `NO_DATA` cohort showing up to $449/copy.

### 2026-08-11 · SHIPPED — descriptor probe v3 (Claude Code, interactive) · v2's controls worked; its captured error BODIES named both real causes

v2 came back **INCONCLUSIVE on both arms instead of lying** — the control mechanism did exactly its job — and the error bodies it captured (the whole reason v2 captures them) identified both failures precisely. **(a) Top Shot 422 body:** `Field "SearchEditionsInput.filters" of required type "EditionFilterInput!" was not provided.` So `input: { first: 1 }` was never a valid `SearchEditionsInput` — and the flat `searchEditions { data { play } }` response shape v1/v2 used **does not exist in the schema either**. v3 uses the EXACT shape the live `backfill-topshot-catalog` route uses: a `$input: SearchEditionsInput!` variable carrying `filters.bySetIDs` (**UUID-format set ids only**) + `searchInput.pagination`, and reads the **double-`data` inline-fragment** path `searchSummary.data.data[]` (`... on Editions { data { ... on Edition } }` — required by the schema, not a typo). Default set uuid is a real Base Set row from our own catalog so the probe needs no arguments; a non-UUID `?setID=` is ignored rather than passed through to be rejected. **(b) AllDay 403** with an HTML `<title>block</title>` page — a **WAF bot-block, not a schema answer**. v3 sends headers identical to the production `editions-hydrate` path (same `User-Agent`), so if the block persists it is a real finding about that ingest rather than an artifact of the probe. ⚠ **Related, unexplained, worth watching:** `editions.last_updated_at` is **NULL on all 6,190 `nfl_all_day` rows** (Top Shot: newest 2026-08-11, 21 updated in 7d) — consistent with the AllDay hydrate path not currently writing, though that column may simply never be set by it; do not conclude either way without checking. 15 tests, incl. new ones pinning that `filters.bySetIDs` is always supplied, that the double-`data` pluck is used (a flat pluck would silently fail the controls), and that the production User-Agent is sent. Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 15/15 green. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`; no DB change. Target metric: a conclusive arm — i.e. controls returning `yes` — before ANY field is called absent.
### 2026-08-11 · SHIPPED — test coverage (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) · 5 unpinned edge-fn inline copies added to the drift guard

The first live run of `/api/admin/discover-moment-descriptors` returned `exists:false` for **every field on both leagues** — which its own output disproves: it marked `classification`, `gameDate`, `homeTeamName` and `dateOfMoment` non-existent, and **all four are in our LIVE production ingest queries and work every day**. Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 13/13 green. **The earlier claim "AllDay description does not exist" is RETRACTED — it was never measured.** **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`; no DB change. Target metric: a probe result that is trustworthy enough to act on.

**What.** `lib/insights/board-status.ts` was built 2026-08-09 for one named failure — a backing view times out (57014), the page's fail-soft `if (error) return []` swallows it, and the board renders EMPTY at HTTP 200, byte-identical to "nothing matched". ### 2026-08-10 · SHIPPED — candy pack-EV FMV fetch-path scoped to collection (Claude Code, interactive) — cleared the one live `public_board_slow_count` breach

- **What:** `candy_pack_ev_model` joined the shared `fmv_current` on `edition_id` ALONE, so the planner materialized latest-FMV for ALL 26,888 editions (Merge Append of 1,069,488 `fmv_snapshots` rows) before hash-joining down to Candy's 125 — 1,007,009 of 1,023,629 buffers, 98% of all traffic. Scoped the lookup to the Candy `collection_id` so it rides `fmv_snapshots_<year>_collection_id_edition_id_computed_at_idx`. Same remedy as the 08-10 `allday_scarcity_board` fix.
- **Measured (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, TIMING OFF):** `candy_pack_ev_model` 3,006 → **52.6 ms** (~57×; buffers 1,014,801 → 703). `candy_pack_market` 5,969 → **1,830 ms**, now under its 3,000 ms cap — it was the ONE board making `public_board_slow_count` = 1.
- **Fetch-path only — no pricing math touched.** Proven output-identical BEFORE applying: `fmv_current` is a plain `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ORDER BY computed_at DESC` with no other filter; all 2,098 Candy snapshot rows carry the Candy `collection_id` (0 wrong/null, 125/125 editions covered); 0 editions tie at `max(computed_at)`; `EXCEPT ALL` = 0 rows in BOTH directions. Post-apply the view returns the identical row (actual_ev 57.94 / typical_pull 24.45 / commons 100/100 / rainbow 25/25).
- **⚠ DURABLE — `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` does NOT preserve reloptions, it RESETS them.** The first migration silently dropped `security_invoker=on` from `candy_pack_ev_model` (→ NULL = DEFINER semantics, in scope for `view_unexpected_definer`). Caught by checking `pg_class.reloptions` post-apply and fixed in a second migration. **Grants were unaffected (anon/authenticated SELECT stayed revoked), so there was no exposure window — and that is exactly why grants alone will not reveal this.** Any `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` on a security_invoker view MUST re-`SET (security_invoker = on)` in the same migration. `check_public_security_invariants()` = 0 after.
- **⚠ METHOD — `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING)` overstated this plan 4×:** 24,692 ms vs **5,969 ms** with `TIMING OFF`, because per-node instrumentation on 1.07M rows added ~18.7 s. Reporting the timed number would have been the same class of error as the migration deleted below. Use `TIMING OFF` on wide-row plans.
- **Also — deleted an untracked, never-applied migration** (`20260802145156_..._board_liveness_probe_bound_and_recalibrate_v2.sql`): stale on BOTH halves after the 08-10 probe decoupling. Its part 1 targets `count(*)` code the probe no longer contains (the probe is now a pure reader of `public_board_liveness_state`; `public_board_liveness_sweep` does the work and DELIBERATELY leaves each view unbounded to preserve honest `elapsed_ms` — bounding it would degrade the new history store). Its part 2 cited `candy_holder_board` at 6,169 ms vs a 4,000 ms cap; live is **15 ms vs a 3,000 ms cap**, so it would have written a false audit note and left ~1000× headroom. Nothing was applied; nothing to unwind.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the files. DB unwind: replace the `fc` CTE in `candy_pack_ev_model` with `LEFT JOIN fmv_current fc ON fc.edition_id = e.id`, then re-run `ALTER VIEW public.candy_pack_ev_model SET (security_invoker = on);`. No data change to unwind.

### 2026-08-10 · SHIPPED — DB (Cowork cloud; verified + ledgered by Claude Code) · the board-liveness sweep had no persistence store, so its own "trust only persistent breaches" rule was unactionable

Migration `20260811003456` (`audit_20260810_board_liveness_history_decoupled_capture`) + pg_cron **jobid 290 `rpc-capture-board-liveness-history`** (`51 */6 * * *`). Parity file committed.

**Why.** The entry directly below closes with the right conclusion — on this instance a single honest timing is a SAMPLE, so the only actionable signal is a board that breaches PERSISTENTLY across sweeps. Verified live: there was nowhere to read that from. `public_board_liveness_state` holds **45 rows / 45 distinct `view_name` / exactly ONE distinct `checked_at`** — one row per board, upserted, no history; each sweep overwrites the last. The sweep writes no `pipeline_runs` row either (checked `prosrc` on all three functions). So the rule was correct and unactionable.

**What.** `public_board_liveness_history`, created `LIKE public_board_liveness_state` (so column types cannot drift from the source) plus `captured_at`, PK `(view_name, checked_at)`, index on `checked_at DESC`. `capture_board_liveness_history()` appends the current state `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and prunes >90 days. pg_cron at **`51 */6`** — the sweep starts `:28` and takes ~202 s (done ~:32), leaving ~20 min of margin; `:51` is a free minute (the `*/2` job occupies even minutes only).

**Deliberately DECOUPLED — ZERO edits** to `public_board_liveness_sweep()` / `public_board_liveness_probe()` / `rpc_thp_leg_board_liveness()`, all shipped ~1 h earlier by a concurrent session. Nothing here can regress them.

**Idempotent, and honest about absence.** Keyed on `(view_name, checked_at)`, so a re-run appends nothing (2nd call `inserted: 0`) and **a failed or skipped sweep appends no row at all** — missing history is then evidence the sweep did not run, rather than a silently duplicated row.

**✅ VERIFIED live post-apply:** table present, **45 rows / 1 distinct `checked_at`**, PK `(view_name, checked_at)`, RLS **on**, anon + authenticated SELECT **false**, `service_role` EXECUTE true / `anon` EXECUTE **false**, cron `51 */6` **active (jobid 290)**, **83 active jobs** (81 + sweep 288 + this), `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**, `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` **empty**, migration recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. ⚠ **The drift fn returns ONE row containing an EMPTY array, so `count(*)` on it is always 1 and reads as a finding** — use `jsonb_array_length`, per the standing mixed-return-shape footgun; I tripped it here and it briefly looked like this migration had opened SECDEF drift. It had not: `capture_board_liveness_history()` is **invoker-rights, not SECDEF** (pg_cron runs it as `postgres`; the only other grantee is `service_role`), so it is correctly absent from that surface.

**What it unlocks — the triage query the sweep's own caveat asks for:**

```sql
SELECT h.view_name,
       count(*)                                        AS sweeps,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.elapsed_ms > w.max_ms) AS breaches,
       round(avg(h.elapsed_ms))                        AS avg_ms,
       max(w.max_ms)                                   AS budget
  FROM public.public_board_liveness_history h
  JOIN public.public_board_liveness_watchlist w USING (view_name)
 WHERE w.is_active AND h.checked_at > now() - interval '7 days'
 GROUP BY h.view_name
HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.elapsed_ms > w.max_ms) >= 3   -- persistent, not a cache miss
 ORDER BY breaches DESC, avg_ms DESC;
```

⚠ **It says nothing until several sweeps have landed** — 4/day at `28 */6`, so ~2 days before the `>= 3` threshold is usable. Until then the 13 currently-over-budget boards remain a snapshot, not a ranking.

**Target metric:** the 13 breaching boards become separable into persistent vs cache-miss.

### 2026-08-10 · SHIPPED — DB (Claude Code, interactive) · public-board liveness probe made HONEST + decoupled from the precompute transaction + slow-vs-empty split

Migration `20260810233442` (`audit_20260810_board_liveness_honest_sweep_decoupled`) + pg_cron **jobid 288 `rpc-public-board-liveness-sweep`** (`28 */6 * * *`, command carries a `SET statement_timeout='900s';` prefix). Parity file committed. Drains inbox `…T1900Z-*` §1 and `…T1930Z-*`.

**What:** three defects in one instrument. (1) The probe timed `SELECT count(*) FROM <view>`, which the planner PRUNES — measured on `allday_scarcity_board`, pruned plan cost 3,873 vs honest 42,826, so the arm read green for a board the page pays 15,172 ms to render. ⚠ **The filed candidate fix does NOT work:** `SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM v) t` measured **3,873.09 — byte-identical to the bare count** (PG flattens it), and an `OFFSET 0` fence (3,873.98) also fails (the fence stops flattening, but PG still strips subquery outputs the outer aggregate never references). The form that works is a whole-row reference: `SELECT count(*), count(t.*)` → 42,827.12. `count(*)` keeps the row count exact (`count(t.*)` alone would undercount an all-NULL row, since `ROW(NULL,NULL) IS NULL` is TRUE); `count(t.*)` exists only to keep the joins in the plan. (2) ⚠ **The per-board `statement_timeout` guard was INERT** — `candy_pack_ev_model` ran **94,508 ms under a 5,000 ms cap**, because the timer is armed at top-level-statement start and a runtime SET inside a function cannot re-arm it; and had it fired, the cancel poisons the surrounding transaction, so the sweep dies rather than degrading. The inert call and its false "fails its own probe" comment are removed; the real bound is the between-boards soft deadline, which cannot preempt a single long board — now documented rather than pretended. (3) A timed-out probe was counted as EMPTY, not SLOW, so a board that renders fine but slowly was reported as "renders a blank board"; now split by SQLSTATE (57014 → slow, any other error → empty).

**Why two functions.** The sweep's only caller was `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh` Leg 8 — the last and most expensive leg of a single 600 s transaction already killed at 600.0 s on 08-09 and 08-10 12:58Z (rolling back all 18 metrics). The honest sweep is far more expensive, so shipping it into Leg 8 would have made that kill routine — strictly worse than the blindness it fixes. New `public_board_liveness_sweep()` does the honest sweep on its own job/transaction; `public_board_liveness_probe()` keeps its **exact signature** (so grants don't reset and the no-arg Leg 8 call stays unambiguous) but is now a cheap READ of `public_board_liveness_state` — **Leg 8 goes ~86 s → ~0 ms with zero edits to the 18-metric function**, which also cuts the 12:58Z kill risk. Bonus: the reader returns `budget_exhausted=true` when the newest sweep is >8 h old or partial, which Leg 8 already maps to 999 → BREACH — that is the separately-queued "cheap honesty guard" for a stale snapshot served as current, delivered free (staleness was previously invisible until the generic 24 h mapping).

**⚠ The filed planner-cost ranking does not predict runtime — do not use it to order this work.** Measured honest vs pruned (ms): the two largest filed ratios are runtime non-events (`panini_sale_feed_status` 441,780× → **97 ms**; `cross_collection_cohort_stats` 355× → **33 ms**, actually *faster* than its pruned 72 ms), while a mid-table 1,134× is the worst board on the estate. Boards that will newly BREACH: `candy_pack_ev_model` 94,508 (budget 3,000, **31×**), `candy_pack_market` 19,297 (**6.4×**), `allday_scarcity_board` ~15,172 (budget 8,300), `topshot_2025_rookie_cohort_stats` 7,283 (**2.4×**), `candy_secondary_board` 6,549 (**2.2×**), `panini_squeeze_board` >60,000 (exceeded a 60 s probe). Expect `public_board_slow_count` **5 → ~11** on the first honest sweep. All true positives; per the standing directive do NOT remedy by raising `max_ms`.

**✅ VERIFIED — first honest sweep ran the exact cron command (23:38Z, one-off): `succeeded` in 202.1 s, 45/45 probed, `budget_exhausted` false, `empty_or_error` 0.** `public_board_slow_count` **5 → 13** (I predicted ~11). Worst is `topshot_first_mint_trophies` **36,975 ms / 6,200 (6.0×)** — a board the earlier passes never individually re-measured — then `cross_collection_deals_board` 30,300 (2.0×), `topshot_first_mint_trophy_stats` 15,913 (2.9×), `allday_scarcity_board` 12,111 (1.5×), and 6 candy boards 5.6–11.2 s against 3,000 ms. ⚠ **No collision with the precompute split shipped 27 min earlier** (`20260810230704`): its new `rpc_thp_leg_board_liveness` calls `public_board_liveness_probe()`, which is now the cheap reader, so that leg drops to ~0 ms too — the two changes compose.

**⚠ COUNTER-EVIDENCE TO MY OWN NUMBERS ABOVE — a single honest measurement is a SAMPLE, not a constant.** The sweep's per-board times differ wildly from the ad-hoc ones taken 20 min earlier on the same boards: `candy_pack_ev_model` measured **94,508 ms** ad-hoc but came in **under its 3,000 ms budget** in the sweep (absent from the breach list entirely); `panini_squeeze_board` **>60,000 ms** ad-hoc vs **4,284 ms**; `panini_sale_feed_status` **97 ms** ad-hoc vs **5,456 ms**. On a disk-IO-budget instance the dominant term is cache residency and neighbour contention, not the query. So: the filed planner-cost ranking is wrong (established), **and measured ms from one run is not much better** — rank this work by REPEATED observation across sweeps, which is exactly what the state table now accumulates. Do not act on any single row of it.

**Target metric:** `public_board_slow_count` / `public_board_empty_count` stop under-reporting; `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh` sheds ~86 s.

**Migrations:** `audit_20260810_reconcile_saved_wallet_stats_resumable_procedure` (FUNCTION → PROCEDURE with per-wallet `COMMIT`, stalest-first, soft deadline, `pipeline_runs` telemetry) then `audit_20260810_reconcile_saved_wallet_stats_pass2_first_and_freshness_skip` (pass 2 first + ungated, freshness skip, holdings-aware ordering). Job 259's command is now the single statement `CALL public.reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats();` — the `SET statement_timeout = '300s';` prefix is REMOVED.

**Measured on this instance (throwaway one-minute pg_cron probes, 15:49–16:08Z) — three claims that would otherwise have been shipped wrong:**
- A procedure doing transaction control can be **NEITHER `SECURITY DEFINER` NOR carry a `SET` clause** — both fail `2D000 invalid transaction termination`. Probes: SECDEF-no-SET **FAILED**, invoker+`SET search_path` **FAILED**, plain invoker **SUCCEEDED**. The inbox doc explicitly prescribed keeping both ("grants reset — re-REVOKE/GRANT in the same migration"), which would have produced a job that 2D000s every tick — strictly worse than the timeout it replaces. The procedure is therefore INVOKER-rights with no `SET` clause and schema-qualifies every reference.
- **`statement_timeout` does NOT re-arm per `COMMIT`.** The doc's stated mechanism ("the timer re-arms after each COMMIT, so it effectively gets the budget per wallet") is false: a probe set the session GUC to 2500ms and then ran three 3.0s legs, all of which survived, each reporting `statement_timeout = 2500ms` at its own commit boundary. One budget for the whole CALL. The COMMIT buys **durable partial progress**, not a per-wallet budget — the soft deadline is what bounds the run.
- The cron command **must be a single statement**: `SET ...; CALL ...` is an implicit transaction block and the COMMIT fails 2D000.

**⚠ DURABLE — `saved_wallets.cache_updated_at` is a LAST-CHANGED stamp, not a last-verified stamp, and every staleness figure filed against this job so far has been measuring the guard.** Live after the first run: 21 of 99 rows read older than 12h, and **all 21 are (wallet, collection) pairs holding nothing whose three `cached_*` columns are already correctly `(0, NULL, NULL)` — 0 rows wrong on screen.** Pass 2 skips a row that already holds the right values, so its stamp can never advance. The inbox doc's "p50 age 9.4h / max 33.5h / 21 rows past 12h" is that artifact, not user-visible staleness — do not re-file it as a data-quality defect.

**⚠ The first run's own new telemetry caught a defect I had just introduced.** It committed **4 of 21 wallets / 13 rows in 106.5s** — the first progress this job has ever made (2 of 2 prior attempts committed nothing) — and reported `truncated: true`. That exposed (a) stalest-first was ordering on those perpetually-old zero-holding rows, so it burned its whole budget on wallets chosen by a timestamp that can never move and would pick the same ones every run — a livelock dressed as a priority queue; and (b) `IF NOT v_truncated` gated the cheap, always-correct pass 2 behind completion of the expensive pass 1, so the ONE genuinely-wrong-on-screen case (a wallet that sold out of a collection keeps showing its old count) was skipped in exactly the saturated conditions that cause it. Second migration puts pass 2 first and ungated, restricts pass 1's list and ordering to pairs that actually hold moments, and adds a 6h freshness skip.

**Also measured:** the soft deadline is checked BETWEEN wallets only and **cannot preempt a single long wallet** — one wallet exceeded 100s under the 16:00Z saturation window. A kill then costs only that wallet. And `cron.unschedule` **cancels a running job** (killed one mid-run at 29.0s).

**NOT done, deliberately:** no third budget raise (refuted twice); no schedule move off 13:33Z (the slot is not structurally congested); no `tier` covering index on `wallet_moments_cache` (INCLUDE columns block HOT on a 2.2M-row table written constantly by the wallet walks — not worth it for display-only data); no change to `aggregate_saved_wallet_stats`, still the single definition of these three columns and shared with the route; the array_agg fold declined (the doc measured it at only −21%).

**Revert:**
- Code/docs: `git revert <sha>`.
- DB: `DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS public.reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats(integer, integer, integer);` then re-apply the function body from `supabase/migrations/20260809050000_audit_20260809_reconcile_saved_wallet_cached_stats.sql`, and `SELECT cron.alter_job(259, command => $$SET statement_timeout = '300s'; SELECT public.reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats()$$);`

**Target metric:** `pipeline_runs` rows for `reconcile-saved-wallet-stats` — `truncated=false` on a quiet-window run, and `wallets_done > 0` on every run (previously: no telemetry at all, and 0 rows written across 2 of 2 scheduled attempts).

### 2026-08-09 · MEASURED + DECLINED (Claude Code, interactive) · `statement_timeout` OVERSHOOTS by up to 458 s on this instance — and jobid 78's "cleanest budget fix" is a fully-drained job

Drained items 2 and 3 of `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-10T0555Z-cron-budget-headroom-audit.md` (resolution appended in-file). Item 1 was already closed by the entry below; item 4 (jobid 235) untouched, as filed. **Read-only — no prod change, nothing to revert but the docs commit.**

⚠ **DURABLE — the audit's instrument framing was backwards. `cron.job_run_details` duration is accurate; `statement_timeout` itself is imprecise here.** The inbox doc looked only at over-budget *successes* and concluded the duration overstates. The failures settle it: all statement-timeout kills over 14 d, by binding budget — **120 s: 5 kills, 0 overshoot, max 120.6 s · 300 s: 2 kills, 0 overshoot, max 300.1 s · 600 s: 129 kills, 12 overshoot (9.3%), max 1058.0 s (+458.0 s)**. A 1058.0 s `canceling statement due to statement timeout` under a 600 s cap **cannot** be pg_cron bookkeeping lag — pg_cron logged the error the backend returned, so the backend genuinely ran 1058 s and was genuinely cancelled. **Mechanism: cancel latency.** SIGALRM only sets `QueryCancelPending`; the cancel is serviced at the next `CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS`, and on this disk-IO-budget-throttled box a heavy statement can go minutes between checks. The kill therefore lands at the first interrupt check *after* the budget expires — **and a statement that finishes inside that gap commits successfully despite blowing its budget** (5 such successes in 14 d: 215 938.7 s · 218 762.0 s · 210 701.8 s · 62 701.0 s · 261 299.9 s). Ruled out with data: not role (both `postgres` and `cron_heavy` overshoot), not command form (218 has **zero** semicolons and still hit 762.0 s — so the doc's "two statements, each gets its own 600 s" explanation for 215/62 is also wrong), not `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`, not startup lag (trivial jobs in the *same minute* as 218's 942.3 s run finished in 0.3 s).

🔓 **This UNBLOCKS the headroom table instead of invalidating it:** overshoot is exclusively a 600 s-cohort phenomenon, so the 120 s cohort's `% of budget` figures are sound and the doc's reason #3 for withholding no longer applies. ⚠ What IS newly soft is the other direction — "nine `cron_heavy` jobs at 95–100% of 600 s" overstates the *scheduled* work they need, since part of that tail is latency the budget never granted. Slot-squat is real either way.

⛔ **jobid 78 `rpc-backfill-pinnacle-acquisitions` DECLINED — right instinct, wrong reason. It is fully drained.** Measured: **candidate pool 4,256 = rows already written 4,256, exactly equal**; **37 rows inserted across ~40 runs in 10 days**, ~27 of them inserting nothing. It has no cursor and no anti-join, so every run re-derives all 4,256 and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`s them — the `[[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]]` shape. Cost is fixed at **35,301** because an unordered `LIMIT` over a hash join can't push down, so the 47 k-row Pinnacle wmc index scan (**25,462**, the dominant node) always runs in full. Raising 120 s → 300 s would only make the waste reliable, four times a day, on the one resource this instance is short of. ⚠ `LIMIT 50000` is inert (pool is 4,256) — not a defect, don't "fix" it.

**Real fix, measured but NOT shipped:** narrow on **ingest** time (`ps.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'`; 187,156/187,156 non-null) — planner cost **35,301.68 → 10,489.34 (−70%)**, with the 25,462 wmc scan replaced by per-candidate `Index Only Scan` probes. ⚠ **Do NOT ship that narrowing alone — it has a hole the full rescan silently covers:** `wallet_moments_cache` is written by wallet walks, so a buyer's wmc row can land *days after* the sale is ingested, and a `ps.created_at`-only key never revisits that pair. Needs **incremental + periodic full sweep** (`p_since_days int DEFAULT 7`, `NULL` = full) — the same shape this doc prescribes for jobid 235. Not pinned in `db-invariants-drift-guard` (checked), so no test copy to update. ⚠ jobid 218 is the same family (hourly, 50000 cap, 7 failures, produced the 942.3 s kill) — re-measure its drain state first.

### 2026-08-09 · SHIPPED — DB (Claude Code, interactive) · deep-audit D3b: 6 wallet-read fns seq-scanned the 2.2M-row wmc because `lower(wmc.wallet_address)` is non-sargable — same class as the D3 Set-Tracker kill

Migration `20260810062131_audit_20260810_sargable_wmc_wallet_predicates_d3b`. Rewrote the 6 prod functions that genuinely seq-scan `wallet_moments_cache` on a single-wallet predicate: `get_wallet_portfolio` (4 preds — incl. the un-aliased `lower(wallet_address)` the register's aliased-regex never counted), `get_active_challenges`, `get_challenge_plan`, `mcp_find_set_completion` (2), `pick_verification_target`, `update_fully_enriched_flags`. Wrapping the COLUMN in `lower()` defeats every `wallet_address` index → parallel Seq Scan of 2.2M rows; **live-measured a normal wallet TIMED OUT (>60s) pre-fix and returns instantly post-fix** (planner cost 41,253 → 1,662, ~25×; Index Cond, not a Filter).

**Candy-safe by construction.** The naive `lower(col)=lower(p)` → `col=lower(p)` rewrite would zero out all 25,375 case-sensitive Candy (Solana base58) wmc rows. Used two equivalence-preserving forms: cross-collection/user-facing reads → `col IN (raw, lower(raw))` (keeps Flow case-insensitivity AND matches the exact Candy base58); Flow-only-scoped preds → bare wmc column with lowered RHS (`col = v_wallet`); seeded-wallets JOIN → `wmc.wallet_address = LOWER(sw.wallet_address)`. **Equivalence proven live: 0 colliding lowercase groups across all 2,211,030 wmc rows** → identical row set for any correctly-cased input. Verified `get_wallet_portfolio(0xbd94…)` returns the exact same **19,260 moments / $79,746.91**; `pick_verification_target` 5 rows in [0,1); `mcp_find_set_completion` supported / missing-19 / owned-1; both challenge fns return valid JSON.
