### 2026-08-07 · QUEUED — deliberately NOT shipped (Claude Code) · `public_board_liveness_probe` measures a PRUNED query (confirmed) — re-baseline must wait for load to normalise

Independently reproduced the Cowork finding: Postgres prunes LEFT JOINs whose columns nothing selects, so the probe's
`SELECT count(*) FROM <board>` skips exactly where board cost lives. Measured live on `candy_secondary_board`, same 125
rows both ways: **`count(*)` 27ms vs `count(t.*)` 11,383ms — a 421× understatement**, and 3.8× over that board's own
3,000ms `max_ms`. So the arm is real and the boards it calls healthy are not necessarily healthy.
**Not shipped, on purpose.** The one-word fix (`count(*)`→`count(t.*)`) must NOT land alone: the probe arms
`statement_timeout` at `greatest(5000, least(30000, max_ms*1.5))` = 5,000ms for a 3,000ms board, so an honest 11.4s board
would exceed its own probe timeout, throw, and be reported as `empty_or_error` — i.e. **misreported as a DARK board when it
is merely slow**, which is a worse wrong answer than under-reporting. It therefore requires re-baselining every active
`max_ms` from honest warm timings first, in the same migration.
⚠ **That re-baseline must NOT be taken now.** The instance is currently under the crawler load this session's proxy change
addresses, and CLAUDE.md's own rule from the 2026-08-03 candy board work applies: wall-clock here swings ~500× with I/O
contention, so budgets derived under load would be miscalibrated garbage baked into monitoring. Re-measure after the page
rate limiter has been live long enough for load to normalise; prefer **buffer accesses** (load-independent) over wall-clock
where possible. Also note `candy_holder_board` is unaffected (it is an MV, nothing to prune) — the scope is plain views
with prunable joins, so do not over-generalise. `public_board_empty_count` is sound (pruning does not change row counts).
`public_board_liveness_probe` is NOT in the drift-guard `PINS` array.
**No revert needed — nothing shipped.**

### 2026-08-07 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, crawler-load handoff) · proxy — rate limiter extended to expensive PAGE routes (was `/api/`-only)

`proxy.ts`'s limiter guarded only `pathname.startsWith("/api/")`, so every server-rendered, DB-backed PAGE route was
completely unmetered. Measured 2026-08-06: ~78k page requests /12h from the post-2026-08-01 AI-crawler unblock, none of it
rate limited, against a Micro instance — the proximate cause of the pooler exhaustion, 128×504 across the scheduled layer,
and the statement-timeout 500s on `/[collection]/pack/dist/[distId]` (85 of 88 total 500s). The limiter was spending its
whole budget on `/api/public/profile/[username]`, which 404s cheaply (it keys on username, so a `0x…` never matches) while
the heavy routes absorbed the crawl untouched. Added a SECOND counter map + ceiling (`PAGE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=120`,
vs 60 for APIs — Next.js prefetch fires an RSC request per hovered link, so 60 would 429 real humans). Scope is deliberately
narrow: GET/HEAD only, anonymous only (`hasAuthCookie` exempts signed-in readers), and an ALLOWLIST of DB-backed surfaces
(`/<collection>/{collection,edition,player,team,set,series,pack,moment}`, `/profile/*`, `/moment/*`,
`/special-serial-owners`) — `/`, `/login`, `/pricing`, `/share/*` stay unmetered so the funnel is never throttled. 429s are
`Cache-Control: no-store` so the CDN can never store one and replay it as the page.
⚠ **Did NOT re-add the blanket AI-crawler block to `app/robots.ts`** — removing it was a deliberate 2026-08-01 traffic
decision (Trevor); re-adding is a traffic call, not cleanup. Noted in-code.
⚠ **Honest limitation, documented in-code:** the counter Maps are module-scope = PER-LAMBDA on serverless, so the effective
global ceiling is (120 × warm instances). This is a burst cap on a single hot IP, NOT a global limit; a real one needs
shared state (KV/Redis/Upstash). Do not read 120 as a guarantee.
New `__tests__/proxy-page-rate-limit.test.ts` (33 assertions) pins the metered/unmetered table + the signed-in exemption;
mutation-proven (removing `pack` from the set and flipping the `/profile/` arm reds exactly the 3 intended rows).
`tsc` clean (source); full suite 9035 passed / 7 pre-existing env-timeout failures also red on a clean `origin/main` tree.
**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (no DB unwind — restores the `/api/`-only limiter).

### 2026-08-07 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, crawler-load handoff) · candy-offers — synchronous heartbeat so a dark run is diagnosable

`candy-offers-indexer` has been fully dark since 2026-08-05 00:50Z (62h at time of writing; `max(candy_offers.last_seen_at)`
unchanged, 39 rows still flagged `is_active` on a sweep a day older than that and itself degraded). The cause could NOT be
determined from any available signal, because the route logged ONLY from inside `after()` — so "cron never fired",
"`after()` dropped", and "killed at the 300s `maxDuration`" are all indistinguishable silence. Vercel runtime logs do not
settle it either: `/api/ingest/candy-offers` shows no line at its 12:50Z tick, but neither does the KNOWN-GOOD sibling
`candy-listings-indexer` that ran 4× the same day — so log-absence proves nothing here (no valid positive control).
Added a synchronous invocation marker written BEFORE `after()` is scheduled, mirroring the `pinnacle-sync` 2026-08-03 fix.
⚠ **Written under a SEPARATE pipeline name (`candy-offers-indexer-heartbeat`), NOT as an extra `candy-offers-indexer` row —
this is load-bearing.** That pipeline is on `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` (`max_silent_minutes` 800), so a marker under its
own name would refresh `last_run` every tick and silence `detect_stalled_pipelines()` even while the real work never
completed — masking the exact outage the marker exists to expose. Under a distinct name the stall detector still fires on
the real pipeline while the heartbeat says how far the invocation got. Mirrors the existing `fmv-recalc-heartbeat`
precedent, and avoids a 46KB `v_rpc_trust_health` rewrite (which carries the twice-bitten `security_invoker` reloptions-wipe
risk) that a data-freshness arm would have required. Terminal logs now carry `phase:"complete"`; heartbeat is `ok:true` so
it cannot inflate `v_pipeline_failure_rates`, and its write is try/caught so a diagnostic can never break the sweep.
States now separate: heartbeat+complete = ran; heartbeat only = `after()` dropped/killed; neither = route never reached.
**Still open (not fixed by this — it is instrumentation):** the outage itself. `detect_stalled_pipelines()` IS flagging it
(3,730 min silent vs 800) but at `severity='info'`, whose recorded rationale — *"candy_mlb is unpublished (no route dirs)
so a stall is not user-facing"* — went STALE at the 2026-07-31 Candy go-live. Raising it is a small follow-up.
**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (no DB unwind; the heartbeat rows are inert history).

### 2026-08-07 · DECIDED — DO NOT SHIP (Claude Code) · `topshot-pack-opens-history-backfill` wedge is an UPSTREAM SPORK OUTAGE, not a range defect

Drained `docs/handoff-2026-08-07-pack-opens-history-backfill-wedge.md`, which proposed two fixes (A: adaptive sub-chunking;
B: bounded permanent-skip) plus manual-unwedge SQL, and could not test its own premise ("spork egress is proxy-blocked
here"). Ran that test from Trevor's Windows box, which DOES have `SPORK_PROXY_*`. **Both options are refuted and the
unwedge SQL would have caused data loss for no benefit — neither was shipped.**
Measured: every historical spork band **≤ 65,264,618 returns Cloudflare 522** (origin connection timeout, ~19.6s); every
band **above returns 200** (124–350ms). A clean cut. The wedged range (61,808,596–61,808,845) sits inside the dead band.
Option A refuted directly: 250/125/50/25/**10**-block windows on the exact range ALL fail identically (`status 0`, ~46s) —
window size is irrelevant against an origin that never answers. Option B / the SQL is actively harmful: the handoff's own
caveat ("only durable if the failure is range-specific … if the whole spork is down it will re-wedge one chunk lower
within ~15 min") now has a MEASURED-FALSE precondition, so skipping would permanently lose ~250 blocks of real 2022-era
pack-open provenance AND re-wedge on the next tick.
⚠ **Positive control is why this is trustworthy** (an all-fail probe proves nothing): same box, same moment —
`google/generate_204`→204, `spork-proxy` worker root→`{"ok":true}` in 72ms, `rest-mainnet.onflow.org`→200, and the 4
newest spork bands→200. Box, network and worker are all healthy; only the old spork ORIGINS time out.
**The cursor hold is CORRECT — there is no code bug.** Refusing to advance past unscanned blocks while upstream is down is
the 2026-08-01 design working as intended. Blast radius is exactly one pipeline (68 runs / 0 ok / 24h); no other pipeline
shows spork-class errors (the concurrent `topshot-badge-catalog` 429 is an unrelated TS-GraphQL rate limit).
Shipped instead: `scripts/probe-spork-bands.mjs` (read-only; refuses to report "sporks down" unless the worker root
answers first) + a ⛔ correction block at the top of the handoff so nobody re-derives this or ships the harmful fix.
**⚠ OPERATOR DECISION (Trevor) — the real question is whether the pre-65M spork nodes are ever coming back.** Historical
spork access nodes do get decommissioned. If permanently gone, the sub-65M leg is unreachable by construction and the
pipeline should be floored at 65,264,619 or retired rather than retrying every 15 min forever. If transient, correct
action is to do NOTHING — the hold already protects the data. Until known, held-and-noisy is strictly safer than skipping.
**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (docs + new script only; no code, DB, or prod-state change).

### 2026-08-05 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, drained the 2026-08-06 Cowork handoff) · series 0-vs-1 convention collision — the bare "1" AND a silent filter that dropped 385,734 rows

Trevor reported two Damian Lillard "Cosmic" moments of the SAME edition (`8:145`) rendering different series:
serial 38 "Series 1 · 2019-20", serial 12 a bare "1". Root cause in `get_wallet_moments_with_fmv`:
`COALESCE(wmc.series_number, e.series)` unions TWO INCOMPATIBLE ENCODINGS — `wmc.series_number` is
ON-CHAIN (Top Shot's Series 1 is **0**; there is no on-chain 1) and `editions.series` is DISPLAY (1 = Series 1).
385,734 TS wmc rows have a NULL series_number and fall through to the editions arm.

⚠ THE WORSE HALF, silent: the same column backs `AND (p_series IS NULL OR series_number = p_series)` and the
client sends the ON-CHAIN number, so filtering "Series 1" sends `p_series=0` and DROPPED every one of those
rows — an incomplete collection with NO error. Measured on Trevor's wallet: 532 → 545 (13 recovered).

⚠ THE TRAP — the fix MUST be Top-Shot-scoped. Measured live against `collection_series`: nba_top_shot has NO
series 1 (0='Series 1'), but nfl_all_day / laliga_golazos / disney_pinnacle use 1 legitimately and **ufc_strike
has BOTH 0 and 1**. A blanket `1 -> 0` remap would corrupt FOUR collections.

Shipped: migration `audit_20260806_get_wallet_moments_series_topshot_convention` — the editions FALLBACK arm
normalises 1 -> 0 only when `p_collection_id` is the Top Shot uuid. `wmc.series_number`, when present, still wins.
VERIFIED on prod: both Lillard moments now emit 0; TS `p_series=0` → 545, `p_series=1` → 0 (correct, no such
series); **All Day `p_series=1` still → 559 and is NOT rewritten**. Also collapses a duplicated "Series 1" / "1"
pair in the client-side label filter (`lib/collection/filter-sort.ts` matches on LABEL).
DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: `lib/collection/helpers.ts:48` `return seriesRaw` — the fall-through is asserted by
`__tests__/collection-filter-options.test.ts:57`, and the DB fix removes the bad input, so touching it would
break a pinned contract for no remaining benefit.
Pin maintained: `PINS` entry re-pointed to the new migration + the verbatim DDL and assertions updated in
`supabase/tests/get_wallet_moments_with_fmv.sql` (+7 assertions incl. an All-Day scope guard that reds any
unscoped remap). Drift guard 122/122 green.
**Revert:** restore `COALESCE(wmc.series_number, e.series) AS series_number,` in `base_other` via
`CREATE OR REPLACE` (full prior body in `supabase/migrations/20260726016000_audit_20260726_serial_fmv_consumers_pooled_edition_id.sql`),
and re-point the `PINS` entry + verbatim test copy back to that migration.

### 2026-08-05 · SHIPPED (Claude Code) · rollup_pipeline_runs made shape-defensive — ONE malformed row was destroying the only indefinite pipeline history

Found via the 01:45Z daytime-monitor HIGH. `rollup_pipeline_runs()` built `extra_key_counts` with
`jsonb_object_keys(COALESCE(e,'{}'::jsonb))`, which guards NULL but NOT a non-OBJECT jsonb —
`jsonb_object_keys` hard-errors on a JSON array, and since the rollup is a single INSERT ... SELECT that one
row aborted the aggregate for EVERY pipeline on EVERY day in the window.

Measured live: of 42,010 `pipeline_runs` rows the `extra` shape is **object 42,003 | NULL 6 | array 1** — the
single array row is `pipeline='diag-step6-cohort'` (a 2026-08-05 16:40Z one-shot diagnostic). pg_cron jobid 233
(`11 */6 * * *`) had failed 2 consecutive ticks and `pipeline_runs_daily` held **0 rows for 2026-08-06**.

⚠ Why it mattered more than it looked: `pipeline_runs` retains only ~73h, so `pipeline_runs_daily` is the ONLY
durable record and cannot be backfilled. Every failed tick permanently lost history from the exact archive
sessions rely on for >73h defect archaeology. It would have PARTLY self-healed when the row aged out (~08-08),
but the days lost were unrecoverable and the defect RECURS on any future non-object `extra`.

Shipped: migration `audit_20260806_rollup_pipeline_runs_shape_defensive_extra` — non-object `extra` is treated
as no-keys instead of aborting. VERIFIED: ran `rollup_pipeline_runs(4)` → upserted 424; **2026-08-06 went
0 → 108 pipelines**, and the malformed row's day now records `extra_key_counts` NULL for that one pipeline
(133 of 134) rather than killing the statement.
**Revert:** `CREATE OR REPLACE` restoring `jsonb_object_keys(COALESCE(e, '{}'::jsonb))` in the
`extra_key_counts` subquery (full prior body in
`supabase/migrations/20260801210100_audit_20260801_rollup_pipeline_runs_fix_generated_duration.sql`).

### 2026-08-05 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, Trevor-directed "do what else makes sense") · 🔧 made the SessionStart mirror-lineage self-heal purge-proof (the old gate was defeated by the 08-03 filter-repo root re-hash)

`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`'s realign fallback keyed on `merge-base == origin's root commit`. The 2026-08-03 `git filter-repo` purge silently defeated it: the purge re-hashed origin's root, so a frozen pre-purge mirror now shares only a deeper NON-root ancestor with origin/main — the gate stopped firing and stranded local `main` days behind (observed this session: `merge-base 90c508a4 ≠ origin root 55f5fe4f`, so the hook nagged "left as-is" instead of healing). Replaced the fragile root-equality gate with a purge-proof `is_mirror_lineage()`: realign when local `main` carries no commit unique by patch-id (`git cherry origin/main main` prints no `+` — provably lossless) OR is ≥100 commits ahead (mirror-shaped magnitude — genuine unpushed work on a commit-directly-to-`main` repo is never hundreds; catches the case where the purge leaves a few orphaned `+` patches so the lossless signal alone misses). Every prior guard kept: ff-only merge is still tried FIRST, a clean tree is still required before any `reset --hard`, and a genuine small branch-off satisfies neither signal so it is left untouched. Validated before commit: `bash -n` clean; the REAL July-29 mirror `d7fda5a0` (ahead 4023, 1 purge-orphan `+`) → DETECTED (realign); a synthetic 3-commit branch-off (ahead 3, 3 unique) → left alone. Root cause is upstream provisioning seeding a stale re-hashed mirror (handed to Cowork separately); this hook change makes it self-heal every session in the meantime. Hook-only; no product/DB/prod change. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the `merge-base == root` gate.

### 2026-08-05 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, Trevor-directed, incident response) · 🛡️ capped 3 edition-page read RPCs at statement_timeout=8s (were inheriting the 30s service_role default) — closes a pooler-hold gap during scraper bursts

Prod DB migration `audit_20260805_cap_edition_read_fn_statement_timeout` (repo `supabase/migrations/20260806013319_*.sql`, applied via MCP + committed). Context: a Vercel "Edge Requests 18×" alert (Aug 06 00:30 UTC) traced to a full-catalog **scraper** flooding public pages (all `cache=MISS`/200), intermittently exhausting the Supabase **pooler** → cascading "connection pool" + "statement timeout" errors (the "external API failures"). NOT caused by any recent deploy; DB was calm between bursts (4 active/90). The entity pages query under **service_role (30s timeout)**, and the team had already deliberately capped most entity read RPCs per-function at 8s — but `get_edition_market_bundle`, `get_edition_insight_links`, `get_edition_special_serials` inherited the 30s default, so on the edition page they could hold a pooler connection 30s while their same-page siblings freed at 8s. Measured warm (2026-08-05): 132ms / 41ms / sub-second → ~60× headroom, so the 8s cap NEVER fires in normal operation; it only fail-fasts (freeing the connection) under genuine saturation, matching the deliberate sibling pattern. Config-only `ALTER FUNCTION SET` (bodies + search_path preserved), verified live. **This is a blast-radius reducer, not the fix** — the definitive mitigation is edge rate-limiting the scraper (Vercel Firewall, operator) + pooler headroom; the read path is otherwise already 8s-protected, so the exhaustion is volume-driven. **Revert:** `alter function public.get_edition_market_bundle(uuid,text) reset statement_timeout;` (+ `_insight_links(uuid,text)`, `_special_serials(uuid)`) — or `git revert` the migration and re-apply the RESET.

### 2026-08-05 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, Trevor-approved) · 🔧 fixed the SessionStart hook so a re-hashed mirror lineage of `main` self-heals (kills the recurring "N unpushed commits" nag)

`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` assumed local `main` is only ever *behind* origin (it used `git merge --ff-only`, which correctly refuses to clobber real work). But web sessions here are seeded with a **re-hashed MIRROR lineage** of `main` that shares only the ROOT commit with `origin/main` (merge-base == root, thousands of commits each side) — so the ff-only merge fails and the hook treated the redundant mirror as precious unpushed work, leaving it and making the Stop hook nag "4023 unpushed commits" every turn. Added a realign arm to BOTH the on-main (3a, `git reset --hard origin/main`) and not-on-main (3b, `git branch -f`) branches, fenced by three guards so it fires ONLY for the artifact and never on real work: non-fast-forwardable **AND** `merge-base == root` **AND** (3a) a clean working tree. A genuine branch-off of recent origin/main history (recent merge-base) or any uncommitted edits fall through to the unchanged "left as-is" NOTE. `bash -n` clean; verified dormant on the current healthy repo (merge-base ≠ root → realign path not reached). Root cause is upstream (the environment seeds the mirror lineage at provisioning); this is the in-repo self-heal. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

`lib/moment-detail-format.ts::fmtRelDate` (relative age on public moment/edition pages) had a dead zone: for `days ∈ [360,364]`, `months = floor(days/30) = 12` fails the `months < 12` months-branch, then `years = floor(days/365) = 0` → it rendered **"0y ago"**. ### 2026-08-04 · DECIDED — do NOT broaden Golazos discovery (Claude Code, measured) · ⚠ **CORRECTS MY OWN "14.5% buyer coverage" FIGURE FROM EARLIER TODAY — the denominator is not the market, and "100% coverage" is a FAKE FINISH LINE.**

Followed up my own flagged Golazos wmc sampling-bias finding by asking what it would take to close. The measurement moved the answer twice, and the conclusion is **ship nothing**.

- **⚠ THE CORRECTION — 98.7% of Golazos sales carry NO BUYER AT ALL.** Of **78,524** Golazos sales, **77,496 have `buyer_address IS NULL`**; only **1,028** name a buyer, and those yield the **173 distinct buyers** I quoted earlier. So my "129 wmc wallets vs 173 known buyers = 14.5%" is arithmetically right but **its denominator is a 1.3% sample of sales, not the market**. Driving that ratio to 100% would produce a metric reading "fully covered" over a 1.3% sample — strictly worse epistemically than the honest 14.5%, because it would look finished. **Do not target this ratio.** (Cause is known and already documented: `sales-counterparty-backfill` excludes Golazos — no transfer to decode.)
- **THE GOOD NEWS, also measured: buyer capture is 100% for EVERY month since 2025-12** (Aug 25/25, Jul 153/153, Jun 170/170, May 6/6, Apr 24/24, Mar 21/21, Feb 10/10, Jan 108/108, Dec 2/2). The NULL mass is entirely the **historical 2022→2025 tail**, not a live defect. So the 173 are the **currently-active trader set** and it is being captured correctly going forward — the live pipeline is healthy and needs no change.
- **Then: would scanning the ~148 known-but-unscanned buyers buy anything? Measured — NO, on both axes.** (1) **Sales resolution is already terminal:** `unmapped_sales` open for Golazos is **6**, and all 6 are the Flowty escrow address the discovery route deliberately excludes — there is no unresolved-sale backlog left for more scanning to drain. (2) **There is no consumer:** as established earlier today, the only cross-wallet holder/scarcity boards over wmc are Candy's; **no Golazos holder board exists**, and per-wallet surfaces populate on demand when someone actually visits the wallet. So broadening `golazos-discover-buyers` from `unmapped_sales` (unresolved) to `sales` (all buyers) would spend ~148 Cadence wallet walks to improve a dataset **with no current reader and no pending backlog**.
- **Decision: leave `app/api/cron/golazos-discover-buyers/route.ts` exactly as built.** Its narrow `unmapped_sales` scope is CORRECT for what it exists to do, it is self-draining and idempotent, and it has already reached terminal state. Broadening it would be work manufactured to move a number that does not mean what it appears to mean — and it cuts against the standing "no infra spend pre-revenue" line. **The standing warning is unchanged and now sharper: do not build a Golazos holder / scarcity / "N collectors own this" board over `wmc`** — not because coverage is 14.5%, but because **the true Golazos holder universe is UNKNOWN and cannot be derived from `sales`**, since 98.7% of them name nobody. A board there would need an on-chain holder enumeration, not more buyer scanning.
- No code, no DB, no migration. Recorded so the next session does not re-derive this or "fix" the ratio.

`RPC Ops Monitor` was red on **6 of its last 8 runs**, across shas going back to this morning. It is not a flaky monitor and it is not a deploy artefact: the job exhausts **all 3 retries** against `/api/cron/stale-fmv-monitor`, each returning **504 `FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT`** at the 30s lambda wall. So the FMV-staleness alarm — the thing that pages when `fmv-recalc` dies — has itself been down, and a real FMV stall today would have gone unannounced.

- **Root-caused by measurement, one leg at a time — it was NOT the leg the route's own comments blame.** The file carries a 2026-06-26 note about an unfiltered `count(*)` over `fmv_snapshots` that was removed then, and `maxDuration` had already been raised 10s→30s once. Measured live, the current cost is entirely elsewhere:

  | leg | measured | why |
  |---|---|---|
  | `sales` latest `sold_at` | **17,067 ms** / 336,469 buffers | ⛔ the whole problem |
  | `fmv_snapshots` latest `computed_at` | 2.07 ms | has `idx_fmv_snapshots_2026_computed_at_desc` |
  | `count(*) editions` (×3) | ~25 ms each | index-only scan, fine |

- **THE DURABLE CAUSE — `sales` is year-partitioned and NOT ONE partition has a `sold_at`-LEADING index.** Every index leads with `edition_id` or `collection_id` (`sales_2026_edition_id_sold_at_idx`, `sales_2021_collection_id_sold_at_idx`, …). - **Fix: bound the window** (`sold_at >= now() - 2d`), which makes the partition key prunable — verified `Subplans Removed: 6`, leaving only `sales_2026` + the empty `sales_2027` — **17,067 ms → 1,993 ms**. The three counts are untouched.

Pass/fail is unaffected — the GHA only reads HTTP 200 + `status`, which the FMV-staleness check alone determines.

So **LOW** — which is sale-derived, just off few/wide sales — published **"Floor/Ask price"**, asserting an ask basis that never existed; and **ASK_ONLY**, the one tier that is literally `0.90 × a single seller's ask`, fell through to **"—"** and disclosed nothing at all. That is the exact inversion `lib/fmv-basis.ts` exists to prevent, on the surface where the owner is valuing their own portfolio. Re-keyed off derivation: `HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|SALES_ONLY → band`, `ASK_ONLY → best-offer-only`, `STALE|NO_DATA|null → none` (absent, never wrong). Uses only existing enum values + the existing renderer — no type or UI change.

### 2026-08-04 · SHIPPED (Claude Code) · 🩹 Golazos had **NO organic wallet discovery at all** — the scanned universe was the curated seed list. New buyer-derived discovery closes it.

Gate 1 residual left by today's shell drain, and a different mechanism from it. Measured: every wallet ever scanned for Golazos came from `seeded_wallets` (268 distinct, all collection-agnostic); `wallet_backfill_state` for Golazos held 269. Nothing ever discovered a wallet from a SALE. So the Golazos holdings view was a curated panel, not the market — and 47 unresolved priced sales across 17 buyers (`onchain_dapper_v2`, newest 2026-08-01, 17 inside 30d) sat permanently unresolvable because `promote_unmapped_sales` Path 4 maps via `wmc.edition_key` and the holder had never been scanned in ANY collection.

- **NEW `/api/cron/golazos-discover-buyers`** (Vercel cron `18 8 * * *`, daily) — selects buyers of unresolved priced Golazos sales that have no Golazos `wallet_backfill_state` row and **dispatches a real `/api/wallet-backfill-golazos` scan** (`skip_cached:false` — a never-scanned wallet has no cache to diff).
- **⚠ IT DISPATCHES; IT DOES NOT WRITE A QUEUE — both obvious tables are traps.** `wallet_backfill_state` is a record of scans ALREADY PERFORMED (`last_scanned_at` DEFAULT `now()`, `scan_count` DEFAULT 1), so inserting there marks a wallet scanned and can SUPPRESS the scan you want. `seeded_wallets` is a human-curated outreach list (username/notes/tags/priority/is_pro_user), not a queue. Letting the scan write its own state row makes the whole thing self-draining and idempotent — once scanned, a candidate is never re-selected, **including when the wallet is legitimately empty.**
- **⚠ THE HANDOFF'S PROPOSED AGGREGATOR HEURISTIC IS CIRCULAR — did not use it.** It prescribed excluding "high purchase count with zero wmc rows". But wmc rows are populated BY scanning, so **every never-scanned candidate has zero by construction**; the test would exclude everything, or collapse to an arbitrary unvalidated cut on purchase count. Used the repo's canonical curated `EXCLUDED_ADDRESSES` (`lib/chains/flow/allday-edition-onchain.ts`) instead — which already contains **both** addresses the heuristic was reaching for: the Flowty storefront escrow `0x3cdbb3d569211ff3` and the AllDay contract account `0xe4cf4bdc1751c65d`.
- **POSITIVE CONTROL before shipping (ran the check against a case it must catch):** the raw live candidate set is **18**, not the handoff's 17 — the extra is `0x3cdbb3d569211ff3`, the Flowty fee router, carrying 40 unresolved sales on a lane dead since 2026-04-16. The exclusion list takes 18 → **17**, removing exactly that address and independently reproducing the 17 real collectors found by hand, with **0** known contract addresses left uncovered (checked against all 9 non-excluded contracts in CLAUDE.md's address table).
- **Bounded 3 ways + nothing silent:** `buyer_address IS NULL` skipped (no wallet path can ever resolve those); envelope addresses excluded; `MAX_DISPATCH=25`/tick with the remainder reported as `deferred_over_cap`. The 1000-row PostgREST cap is reported as `candidate_rows_capped` rather than being read as "saw the whole backlog". Deliberately NOT filtered by `source` — the dead flowty lane's only buyer is the escrow, already excluded, so a source filter buys nothing and would blind discovery to a future lane.
- **Auth accepts INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN *or* CRON_SECRET** — Vercel Cron sends only the latter, which is what made `/api/cron/pinnacle-sync` 401 on every tick for months. Pinned by a test.
- **19 tests, mutation-proven to bite:** disabling the exclusion reds exactly the 3 envelope tests; disabling the already-scanned filter reds exactly 1; widening the cap reds exactly 1. Also pins address normalisation (an unpadded/upper-case escrow address must still be excluded — a raw compare misses it), dedup, full-suite `ok:false` honesty on both fetch-error paths and on a rejected dispatch, and that work is deferred into `after()`.
- **Verification:** `tsc` 0 non-`.next` errors; full suite **8991 passed**. The 7 reds are in `api-ingest-backfill` + 2 `worker-*` files and were **proven pre-existing by re-running them with this work fully stashed — identical 7 failures** (the documented Windows-only 5000ms-timeout/401 class). Discovery's own 19 all green.

### 2026-08-04 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, self-correction) · 🩹 the AllDay resolver window's **arm A was still full-scanning — my own two-arm fix was only half a fix.** 10,483ms → 16ms once the ORDER BY steers the planner.

Follow-up to the two-arm split shipped hours earlier. **Post-ship verification caught that the timeout was NOT gone**: the 17:56Z run still logged `load_open:canceling statement due to statement timeout`, and it carried the `window_*` telemetry, proving it was the NEW code. Measured instead of assumed, and instead of waiting on a 3-run sample (1 of 3 failed — far too small to conclude anything either way against the old code's 12/178).

- **Arm B was already perfect** — 14ms / 6 buffers, `idx_unmapped_sales_tail_resolver_targets`, terminating at the first entry past the cutoff exactly as designed.
- **Arm A was the whole residual cost: 10,483 ms / 37,411 buffers.** By ordering it `sold_at DESC` alone I let the planner choose `unmapped_sales_unresolved_idx (collection_id, sold_at DESC)`, which **cannot satisfy `last_onchain_attempt_at IS NULL` from the index at all** — so it walked the collection in sold_at order and reported `Rows Removed by Filter: 75,820` to return 37 rows.
- **⚠ THE DURABLE LESSON: a sort key that cannot change the result order can still be load-bearing, because it steers the PLANNER.** Every row in arm A has `last_onchain_attempt_at` NULL, so naming it as the leading sort key is a semantic no-op — but it makes the ORDER BY match the column order of `(collection_id, last_onchain_attempt_at NULLS FIRST, sold_at DESC)`, so the planner picks that index and probes the NULL block directly (`Index Cond: collection_id = X AND last_onchain_attempt_at IS NULL`). **Same 37 rows, same order: 16 ms / 17 buffers — ~655× faster, ~2,200× fewer buffers.** Dropping that key is invisible in the output and silently reintroduces the timeout, so the test now pins it explicitly with the measurement in the comment.
- **⚠ AND THE META-LESSON: "split the OR into two bounded arms" was the right SHAPE but did not by itself make either arm bounded.** I verified the mechanism (arm B stops early) and shipped without EXPLAINing arm A, because it looked obviously index-served. It was not. Explain BOTH arms of a split, not just the one the analysis was about.
- Tests 7/7, tsc clean. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores the `sold_at`-only ordering on arm A — which is correct output but slow).

### 2026-08-04 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, handoff drain) · 🩹 **Gate 1 item 3 CLOSED — Golazos shells 3,822 → 0** · root cause was NEITHER hypothesis in the handoff · + fixed the AllDay tail-resolver timeout it was queued behind

**§1b — Golazos shell drain. The handoff offered two branches; the truth was a third, and acting on either branch would have been wrong.**

- The control wallet `0x4ba45c2312086820` reported `on_chain_count: 0` on **7 consecutive scans Aug 1 → Aug 4**, all `ok:true`, while holding 1,832 wmc rows. Branch (a) said the Cadence scan is broken; branch (b) said the shells are stale ownership and should be deleted.

Positive control `skip_cached:true` @17:01Z → **`on_chain 1832`, 2,849ms**.
- **⚠ So `skip_cached` is EXONERATED — the handoff was right to say so, and the 08-03 roadmap is wrong to blame it.** `skipCached` is applied *after* the `fcl.query` in `runAllDayDetailsBackfill`, so it cannot change what the scan returns. The real variable is the **Cadence scan itself intermittently resolving to `[]` on large wallets**, and the **elapsed time is the tell**: a healthy scan of this wallet is ~2.8s, the failing ones burn ~31s and return empty. A degraded read, not an empty wallet.
- **⚠ The shells were REAL HOLDINGS.** Branch (b) — mass-delete — would have destroyed 1,712 rows of genuine inventory across 39 wallets. The handoff's ⚠ against deleting first was correct and load-bearing.

It was unexercised until now.

- **Revert:** none, and none wanted — this is repaired data, not a change. wmc rows are idempotently rewritten by the normal pipeline.

**§1c — the AllDay tail resolver's `load_open` statement timeout. The handoff called for a "UNION split"; the diagnosis underneath it was wrong, and the correct fix is the same shape for a different reason.**

- **⚠ "The OR is non-sargable" is NOT the mechanism here.** The supporting index already matches the query exactly — both the partial predicate and the sort: `idx_unmapped_sales_tail_resolver_targets (collection_id, last_onchain_attempt_at NULLS FIRST, sold_at DESC) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL AND price_usd > 0`.
- **The real mechanism is that the second OR arm matches NOTHING, and the planner cannot know that in advance.** Measured live: never-attempted rows = **36** (vs `CANDIDATE_LIMIT` 600), attempted = **32,850**, oldest attempt stamp **2026-07-27**, reattempt cutoff (−14d) **2026-07-21**. The oldest stamp is *newer* than the cutoff, so `< cutoff` is empty **by construction**. The single query therefore returns its 36 NULL rows from the index head instantly, finds itself 564 short of the LIMIT, and **keeps walking all 32,850 remaining index entries applying a filter that can never match again** — a guaranteed full partial-index scan every tick, to return nothing. That is the timeout.
- **⚠ It is SELF-PERPETUATING:** every successful run stamps `last_onchain_attempt_at` on the rows it probes, which keeps arm A tiny, which guarantees the next run scans the whole tail again.
- **Fix: `lib/unmapped-rotating-window.ts`**, shared by BOTH resolvers (the live `allday-resolve-unmapped` carried the identical `.or()` at line 200 with no `sold_at` bound at all, so it scanned an even larger set). Arm A `IS NULL` = the contiguous NULL group at the index head; arm B `< cutoff` = a range scan that **stops at the first entry ≥ cutoff**, i.e. immediately, precisely in the case that was previously the most expensive. Arm B is skipped entirely when arm A fills the window, and capped at the remainder otherwise. Adds `window_never_attempted` / `window_reattempt` telemetry to `pipeline_runs`.
- **Ordering is preserved exactly** — the original sort is `attempt ASC NULLS FIRST, sold_at DESC`, so every NULL row sorts ahead of every non-NULL row; arm A is precisely the head of that ordering and arm B its continuation. `.lt()` excludes NULLs on its own, so the arms are disjoint and no row can appear twice.
- **Tests:** `__tests__/unmapped-rotating-window.test.ts` (7 tests) pins the STRUCTURAL properties — two separately-bounded arms, never a combined `.or()`, arm B capped at the remainder, arm B skipped when arm A fills, exact per-arm ordering, error propagation without partial data, and no unbounded read on a non-positive/NaN limit. **Mutation-tested:** restoring the single `.or()` form reds exactly the intended assertion. tsc clean; 13/13 green with the tail route's existing suite.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores the `.or()` form in both routes; no DB unwind — the indexes are untouched and already existed).

### 2026-08-04 · SHIPPED (Claude Code) · fixed the Golazos wallet-scan silent-failure that stalled the shell drain — root-caused to a nil Cadence borrow, not an empty wallet

The 08-04 handoff's shell drain stopped dead at 3,822 shells because `wallet-backfill-golazos` reported `on_chain_count: 0 / no_more_moments / ok:true` for wallets holding real moments. Root-caused from telemetry + code (Flow REST is 403 from the sandbox, so no on-chain re-scan possible here): the details scan runs `fcl.query`, which RESOLVES with a real `[]` on the failing wallets (never throws — 7d of golazos runs show ONLY `no_more_moments` + `pagination_failed`, never `error`/`timeout`), so the empty is a genuine Cadence return from a **nil capability borrow**. The details script (added 07-31) borrowed the NARROW `&{NonFungibleToken.Collection}`; the sibling ID-only `CADENCE_GOLAZOS` — which resolves for these same wallets — borrows the BROAD `&{NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic}`. Proof it's the borrow type: `0x4ba45c2312086820` holds **1,480 enriched + 352 shell** wmc rows (all written in one 07-25 18:16 bulk pass) yet `max_onchain_ever = 0` across every route scan since — the live route has NEVER successfully read it. 23 wallets in this failure bucket (4,408 enriched + 3,406 shells); the 3,822 shells are 0/3,822 resolvable DB-side (no `sales`/wmc-twin source), so enrichment strictly needs a working on-chain scan.

Two-part fix (code + tests only; **no migration, no prod-DB change**), based on origin/main (local main was a stale divergent line; prod deploys origin/main):
- **Enrichment fix — `GET_GOLAZOS_MOMENT_DETAILS` borrow `&{NonFungibleToken.Collection}` → `&{NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic}`** (both public-path attempts). Verified against onflow/flow-nft `NonFungibleToken.cdc`: `CollectionPublic` declares BOTH `getIDs()` and `borrowNFT()`, and `Collection` inherits it, so CollectionPublic is strictly broader — resolves for the currently-working wallets PLUS the failing ones. Self-verifying post-deploy: the 23 failure wallets should start returning >0. Worst case if the interface differs on-chain: script fails → visible `ok:false`, never silent, never corrupting.
- **Honesty guards in `runAllDayDetailsBackfill` (the shared details runner)** so `on_chain_count: 0` can never again silently mean "the scan failed": (a) a non-array `fcl.query` resolve → `ok:false terminated_reason=non_array_scan_result` (universal, defensive); (b) an empty scan for a wallet that STILL has cached wmc rows → `ok:false terminated_reason=empty_scan_but_cached_holdings` (+ `cached_row_count`), gated by new config flag `flagEmptyWithCachedHoldings` set ONLY on the Golazos route, so AllDay's verified-healthy empty behavior is untouched. Both skip the clean-refresh stamp so the wallet stays stale and is re-attempted. NOT deletion — handoff step 3 (delete stale shells) stays operator-gated pending on-chain confirmation.
- **Files:** `lib/chains/flow/wallet-backfill-helpers.ts` (script borrow + `BackfillCollectionConfig.flagEmptyWithCachedHoldings` + `countCachedRows` helper + guards), `app/api/wallet-backfill-golazos/route.ts` (flag on), `__tests__/wallet-backfill-helpers.test.ts` (+6 tests: borrow-type pin, non-array, empty-but-cached, genuine-empty, guard-off-AllDay). tsc clean; helper+route+multicollection suites green (82 tests).
- **Verify after deploy:** `SELECT extra->>'terminated_reason', count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE (extra->>'on_chain_count')::int>0) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline='wallet-backfill-golazos' AND started_at>now()-interval '6h' GROUP BY 1;` — expect the 23 failure wallets to move to `on_chain_count>0`; any residue surfaces as `empty_scan_but_cached_holdings`, not silent success.
- **Revert:** `git revert <this code sha>` (restores the narrow borrow + removes the guards; the flag field is inert without the guards). No DB unwind.

### 2026-08-04 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, PROD EDGE DEPLOY) · deployed the 2 Deno edge fns left undeployed by the 08-04 bug-sweep — and closed the repo↔deployed import divergence in the process

`9a38010d` fixed `flowty-proxy` + `special-serial-delta` in the repo but edge fns don't ship from a git push, so both had been running the pre-fix code since. No Supabase CLI on Trevor's box → deployed via Supabase MCP `deploy_edge_function`. **flowty-proxy v23 → v24; special-serial-delta v4 → v5.** Both `verify_jwt:false` preserved.

- **⚠ THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THIS — the repo↔deployed divergence runs the OPPOSITE way from the one CLAUDE.md documents.** The old note says *deployed* carries inline `esm.sh`/`jsr:` URLs and repo carries bare specifiers, so "deploy a MINIMAL DIFF keeping the inline import". Measured here: deployed v23/v4 **did** inline `jsr:` while the repo imports `@supabase/supabase-js` by BARE specifier via `supabase/functions/deno.json`. So shipping repo source **without** the import map would have left `createClient` unresolvable and boot-failed `special-serial-delta` (a live 30-min cron that writes `special_serial_holders`). Fix: pass `deno.json` in `files` **and** set `import_map_path: "deno.json"` — the MCP tool supports exactly what `supabase functions deploy` does. Deployed responses now report `import_map: true`. **This CLOSES the divergence rather than perpetuating it** — deployed body is now byte-identical to the repo source (verified by re-fetching and diffing, em-dashes and all).
- **Sequenced safest-first + verified behaviourally, not just by deploy status.** flowty-proxy went first (its only import is the type-only `edge-runtime.d.ts`, erased at runtime) to prove the import-map channel before risking the fn with a real runtime import. Its fix was **proven by black-box probe**: an unauthorized POST returned `Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8` on a JSON body BEFORE (the actual defect) and `application/json` AFTER, status/body unchanged. `special-serial-delta` returns a clean 401 rather than a 500 BOOT_ERROR, which is the proof its module-level `createClient` constructed — i.e. the bare-specifier import resolved through the map.
- **Live-ingest regression watch — PASS.** `flowty-proxy` backs the 4 listing-cache pipelines (Flowty blocks Vercel IPs). Baseline 3h before deploy: ~100–105 rows/tick, all ok. First post-deploy tick `golazos-listing-cache` 14:26:13Z **ok=true, 100 found / 100 written** — identical. Success path healthy through v24.
- **Note on scope:** `special-serial-delta`'s fix (`sales_2026` → parent `sales`) is on the FALLBACK path only, and `get_recently_traded_special_serials(p_hours integer)` **exists** in prod — so the fallback is dead code today and the fix is defensive (it arms the 2027 year-boundary case if that RPC is ever dropped). Deployed anyway to close the divergence; no behavioural change expected today.
- **Revert:** `git revert 9a38010d` then redeploy both fns from the reverted source the same way (`files` = index.ts + deno.json, `import_map_path: "deno.json"`, `verify_jwt: false`). No DB unwind — neither fn's schema or data contract changed.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code+test) · smoke-test `smokeFetchRetry` re-used a one-shot AbortSignal on its retry — the timeout-retry was a silent no-op; converted the resolve-and-associate probe onto it

Interactive issue sweep. Sentry `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-K` ("smoke test failed: /api/profile/resolve-and-associate responds (200 or 401)", detail `"The operation was aborted due to timeout"`) has flapped **43× over 3 months** (regressed substatus). Root cause is a latent bug in the shared `smokeFetchRetry` helper (`app/api/smoke-test/route.ts:63`): callers pass their per-attempt budget as `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(N)` in `init`, and the helper reused the **same `init`** on its retry. `AbortSignal.timeout` is one-shot — once it fires on attempt 1 it stays aborted — so the retry `fetch` aborted **instantly**, making the retry a no-op **on the exact timeout class the helper exists to tolerate** (`isTimeoutOrTransient` catches the abort, the retry re-aborts on the dead signal). The existing unit tests passed only because they mock `fetch` with no real signal. This weakened EVERY `smokeFetchRetry` caller (sniper-feed, og, wallet-search, public-profile), and the two `resolve-and-associate` probes had never even been migrated onto it (still bare `smokeFetch` = zero retry). **Fixes:** (1) `smokeFetchRetry` now builds a **fresh** `AbortSignal.timeout(SMOKE_RETRY_TIMEOUT_MS=15000)` on the retry when the caller's signal has already aborted (reuses it otherwise, so a non-timeout transient keeps its live budget); (2) converted the flapping Phase-4.1 `resolve-and-associate` correctness probe from `smokeFetch`→`smokeFetchRetry` (left the Phase-4.2 latency probe on bare `smokeFetch` — a retry would muddy its <3s latency assertion and it wasn't flapping). Test-only + smoke-route-only; **no product runtime, FMV/pricing/ingest, or DB touched.** Added 2 regression tests in `__tests__/api-smoke-test-html-contains.test.ts` (fresh-signal-on-aborted-retry + reuse-live-signal); the first was **proven to fail against the pre-fix helper** and pass after. `tsc --noEmit` clean; 21/21 smoke-route tests green; full local suite was 8923/8923 pre-change. Also resolved 4 stale Sentry issues (`NEXTJS-1Z/1Y/23/24`, entity-detail statement-timeouts) as confirmed collateral of the fmv-recalc sweep-cursor stall fixed by `484d08d7` (warm `get_pack_detail_bundle`=16.8ms; all events predate the 20:42Z fix). **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(smoke): give smokeFetchRetry a fresh signal on retry + use it for resolve-and-associate">` (Sentry resolutions auto-reopen on recurrence — nothing to revert there). **Verified post-ship:** commit `c741e338`, deploy `dpl_FPMh627sXvaJz83zPnjRBP437cK9` READY (live on www.rippackscity.com), `ci.yml` green 8/8; `NEXTJS-K` resolved in Sentry now the fix is live. Memory wrap-up added to CLAUDE.md Recent-sessions in the same docs commit.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, DB-only) · `allday-unmapped-resolver-tail` was scanning 73,736 rows to return 36 — and the monitor's prescribed fix did not apply

Drained item 1 of `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-04T0010Z-daytime-monitor.md` (37.5% fail on `load_open: canceling statement due to statement timeout`, confirmed live). ⚠ **THE MONITOR'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG.** It read this as "an unbounded scan of partitioned `sales`" and prescribed today's classify-acquisitions remedy (`sold_at >= COALESCE(p_since,'-infinity')`). But the query reads **`unmapped_sales`, a PLAIN table** — `relispartition=false`, 0 partitions, 132 MB, ~112k rows. There are no partitions to prune and no time bound to add (it already has `sold_at < now() - 7 days`). Applying the prescribed fix would have been a no-op at best.

**What is actually slow** (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, live): `Rows Removed by Filter: 73,736` **to return 36 rows**, `Buffers: hit=27,280 read=7,366`, 2,655 ms. Two things compound: `price_usd > 0` sits in no index predicate so it is filtered over every unresolved AllDay row; and because the ORDER BY is `last_onchain_attempt_at ASC NULLS FIRST` the ~36 eligible rows sort FIRST, so `LIMIT 600` can never be satisfied and the scan walks the whole remaining range hunting matches that do not exist. The tail is essentially drained — nearly all of that work is waste, and on Micro the 7,366 uncached page reads are what blow the statement timeout under load.

**Fix — DB-only, no resolver logic touched:** `audit_20260804_unmapped_sales_tail_resolver_partial_index` adds `price_usd > 0` to the partial-index predicate (1,600 kB, 35,942 rows vs 77,500 unresolved). Planner picks it. ⚠ **Quote buffers, not wall clock** (the 08-03 candy-board lesson — wall clock here swings with contention): **disk reads 7,366 → 177, −98%**; total buffers 34,646 → 23,146, −33%. Wall clock 2,655 → 41 ms, but that number is load-dependent.

⚠ **RESIDUAL, DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN — 32,206 rows are still removed by filter.** The `(x IS NULL OR x < cutoff)` OR-form cannot become an index condition, so the scan still cannot stop early. Making it sargable means splitting into two arms (the UNION pattern used on `candy_special_serials_board` the same day) — a CODE change to an ingest-adjacent resolver, off-limits for autonomous shipping and not proportionate here: the monitor itself classes this efficiency-only (main resolver healthy at ~2.2k resolved/24h, backlog unaffected), and the index removes the disk I/O that was causing the timeouts. ⚠ **The failure-rate improvement is NOT yet verified** — this arm runs once per 3h and the index landed ~01:50Z, so the next few ticks are the real test. Revisit the UNION split only if the rate does not fall. Pre-existing `idx_unmapped_sales_onchain_attempt_cursor` KEPT (superset predicate, other callers may use it). **Revert:** `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_unmapped_sales_tail_resolver_targets;`

### 2026-08-03 · MEASURED / NO ACTION (Claude Code) · `wallet-username-resolver`'s 35% failure rate was collateral damage from the fmv-recalc stall, and it is already gone

Item 2 of the same inbox tick, which suggested bounding/throttling its scan window but sensibly said "investigate before touching". **Investigated — do NOT touch it.** The 35.2% figure is a retention-window average that hides the shape: failures run **07:00Z–20:00Z on 08-03 (1–2 per hour, every hour) and then stop dead at 21:00Z**, with 10 consecutive clean runs since and `rows_found=0` (backlog drained, ~6s per run).

**The cause is measured, not inferred.** `fmv-recalc` over the same boundary: 17:00–19:00Z = **0 runs advancing the cursor**, avg **212–298s** per run; from 21:00Z = **every run advancing**, avg **116–124s**. The cursor-stall fix (`484d08d7`, deployed 20:55:16Z) roughly **halved the DB time fmv-recalc consumed per run**, and the username resolver's timeouts vanish at exactly that boundary. It was contention collateral, not a defect in the resolver — so bounding its scan window would be optimising a problem that no longer exists.

⚠ **DURABLE — this is direct evidence for the deferral recorded against candy Item 2 above** (`paginateGroup`, whose 2.8× slowdown spans the same 08-01→08-03 window). Same mechanism, same timeline, same instruction: **measure the post-fix tick before optimising.** More generally: a `pipeline_runs` failure-RATE aggregated over the retention window can be entirely an artifact of a since-fixed contention source — always bucket by hour before treating a rate as a property of the pipeline. No code, no DB, no config change.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code+test, Trevor "make your own judgements and execute") · extended the cursor-safety fix to all 4 sales indexers (FMV-critical)

Completed the queued sales-indexer rollout, judged worth doing (silent sale-loss on FMV-feeding paths, and FMV accuracy is the roadmap gate). Read each file individually — they split into three structural variants, each handled correctly: (1) **`allday-sales-indexer` + `golazos-sales-indexer`** — same block-chunk + cursor-to-`targetHeight`-after-loop shape as the listings, so the identical `firstFailedChunkStart` cap-on-throw pattern applies (idempotent re-scan — `sales` dedup on `transaction_hash`). (2) **`ufc-sales-indexer` — DIFFERENT: it advances the cursor PER-CHUNK inside the loop**, so a mid-range chunk throw would let a later successful chunk move the cursor PAST the failed one (a leapfrog skip). (3) **`sales-indexer` (topshot) — DIFFERENT: `fcl.send` THROWS on a failed request** (vs the REST helpers returning `[]`) into TWO separate per-fetch catches, with TWO cursor-write sites (no-events + has-events); tracked `firstFailedChunkStart` across both catches and capped both sites via a shared `cursorTarget`. All surface `extra.partial_scan`/`first_failed_chunk`. tsc clean; all sales-indexer suites green (68) + the new ufc regression test bites. **Scope note:** as with listings, the intentional HTTP-500→`[]` degrade in the REST fetch helpers is untouched — only the genuine THROW path (network/timeout/parse; and fcl's throw-on-failure) is fixed. **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(sales-indexers): cap cursor on chunk fetch throw">`.

### 2026-08-03 · DECIDED / DECLINED (Claude Code, own judgement) · do NOT change the live-leg HTTP-500 cursor tolerance in the event indexers

The second half of the queued cursor item asked whether a LIVE event leg returning an HTTP 500 (which `fetchEventRange` deliberately degrades to `[]`, letting the cursor advance past those blocks) should also hold the cursor. **Declining, with reasoning:** (1) the degrade-to-`[]` on `!res.ok` is INTENTIONAL and tested — the dormant Flowty-fork legs 500 by design, and the "survives a 500" tests encode it; (2) making a live-leg 500 hold the cursor would change the OUTAGE behavior of every FMV-feeding indexer at once — during a broad Flow-REST 500 storm they would all wedge (cursor stops, work piles up), a real operational risk on the platform's most critical pipelines; (3) distinguishing "live leg" from "dormant Flowty leg" per-fetch across 8 files is fiddly and error-prone; (4) the safer alternative (bounded retry on 5xx/429) risks pushing these runs past `maxDuration` and changes run timing — it needs PROD METRICS (how often do live legs 500? current duration headroom?) I don't have from the sandbox. The already-shipped THROW-path cap covers the connection-failure/timeout class, which is the more common broad-outage manifestation. **This is a measure-first decision, not a defect to fix blind** — revisit only with live 500-rate + run-duration data. No code change.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code+test, Trevor-authorized "proceed with all") · listing indexers cap the cursor to the last good chunk on a fetch THROW (was silently skipping blocks)

The queued "[RISKY, systemic] indexer cursor advances past a failed chunk" item, scoped precisely after reading the code. ⚠ **The sub-agent's framing was too broad:** the fetch helper `fetchEventRange` DEGRADES an HTTP error (500/429) to `[]` **on purpose** (the dormant Flowty-fork legs 500 by design; the "survives a 500" test encodes it), so that path is NOT a bug and was left untouched. It only THROWS on network/timeout/parse errors — and there the chunk `catch` logged + continued while the cursor still jumped to `targetHeight`, permanently skipping those blocks' listing/sale events. Fix (identical 3-line pattern in all 4 direct-Flow-REST listing indexers — `allday`/`topshot`/`golazos`/`ufc-listings-indexer`): track `firstFailedChunkStart`, cap the cursor write to `firstFailedChunkStart - 1`, and surface `extra.partial_scan`/`first_failed_chunk`/`cursor_held_from`. A transient throw now self-heals next tick (re-scan is safe — all writes are idempotent upserts); a persistent one visibly stops the cursor (a real signal) instead of eating data. +1 regression test on the exemplar (a chunk leg throws → cursor held at lastBlock, partial_scan surfaced), proven to bite (pre-fix the cursor jumps to targetHeight). tsc clean; all 69 listings-indexer tests green. **NOT touched (documented, needs its own careful pass):** the `*-sales-indexer` family is structurally different (multiple fetch helpers, different cursor shape) and is the most FMV-critical — it warrants individual per-file analysis, not this blind pattern; and the intentional HTTP-500→`[]` degrade on LIVE legs (vs dormant Flowty) is a separate tolerance-vs-completeness design question for Trevor. **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(indexers): cap cursor on chunk fetch throw">`.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code, Trevor-authorized "proceed with all") · candy-sales-indexer parks non-duplicate insert failures instead of dropping them

The queued "[RISKY] candy-sales-indexer row-by-row fallback drops non-23505 rows" item. In `insertSales`'s per-row retry, a row failing for a non-duplicate reason was `if (!se) written++` → silently dropped, uncounted, while the cursor (`cursorAfter`) had already advanced past it = permanent loss. Conservative fix (can only PRESERVE data, never corrupt): on `se.code !== "23505"`, `park()` the row with reason `insert_failed:<code>` — reconstructing the park args from the built row — so the existing dead-letter drain retries it on a later tick, exactly as the drain loop already does for its own inserts. A genuine 23505 duplicate still skips silently (correct). tsc clean; 15/15 candy-sales-indexer tests green. **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(candy-sales): park non-dup insert failures instead of dropping">`.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, DB-only) · anon could EXECUTE a SECDEF **writer** — opened by today's own classify-acquisitions fix

Drained the HIGH finding from the daytime monitor's 21:15Z inbox tick (same day, not the night
pass). `public.backfill_acquisitions_for_collection(uuid, integer, timestamptz)` is
SECURITY DEFINER and WRITES `moment_acquisitions`, but
`has_function_privilege('anon', …, 'EXECUTE')` was **true**.

CAUSE — a signature change, not a grant mistake: `audit_20260803_backfill_acquisitions_bounded_window`
(today's `c571e9f3` / `8e62cf26` bounded-window fix) added `p_since timestamptz`, which DROPs
the `(uuid,integer)` overload and CREATEs a NEW function object. A new function gets the
default PUBLIC EXECUTE grant, and Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` additionally grants
EXECUTE to `anon` + `authenticated`.
**⚠ DURABLE: changing a SECDEF function's SIGNATURE silently re-opens its exec surface even
when the previous signature had been revoked. Any migration that adds or changes a parameter
on a SECDEF function must re-apply the revokes in the same migration.**

⚠ **The monitor's prescribed fix (`REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`) was INCOMPLETE and would have left
the hole open.** The live ACL carried BOTH forms —
`{=X/postgres, postgres=X, anon=X, authenticated=X, service_role=X}` — so revoking only PUBLIC
leaves `has_function_privilege('anon', …)` true via the explicit grant, and revoking only
anon/authenticated leaves it true via PUBLIC. **Both revokes applied.** This is the exact
two-sided version of the trap CLAUDE.md documents from one side only.

REVOKE (not allowlist) justified by auditing callers BOTH ways, per CLAUDE.md:
- **Direct:** sole caller is `app/api/cron/classify-acquisitions-multicollection`, using
  `supabaseAdmin` — a genuine service-role import, not an aliased name (the `supabase`-name
  trap) — behind Bearer `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`.
- **Invoker-mode:** **zero** — no function body, view definition (`security_invoker` or not),
  or `cron.job` command references it, so no anon-reachable SECURITY INVOKER path made the
  grant load-bearing.

Verified after: ACL `{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}`; anon/authenticated EXECUTE
**false**; service_role + owner **true**; `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` → `[]`;
`check_public_security_invariants()` 0; `check_anon_write_surface()` 0. Clears the
`secdef-anon-exec-drift` pipeline alert. Inbox tick archived with the drain note.

✅ **CONFIRMED BY A REAL RUN, not just the privilege bit:** the next
`classify-acquisitions-multicollection` tick after the revoke (**22:06:17Z**) came back
`ok=true` and **wrote 80 rows** — the SECDEF writer still executes as service_role and is doing
real work. No caller was broken by the revoke.

REVERT (restores the hole — only if a genuine anon caller is ever found):
`GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.backfill_acquisitions_for_collection(uuid, integer, timestamptz) TO anon, authenticated;`

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, DB-only) · candy_special_serials_board 7.4s → 58ms (public board, was 2.73× over its warn budget)

Identified the boards behind the carried `public_board_slow_count = 3` BREACH. ⚠ They are
**NOT** the two the arm's own `catches` text names (`topshot_perfect_mint_premiums_board`,
`topshot_pack_reality_dist` — both since re-budgeted and now inside their caps). The live
three are `candy_special_serials_board` (11,193ms vs 4,100ms budget, **2.73×**),
`topshot_first_mint_trophy_stats` (1.04×) and `topshot_first_mint_trophies` (1.02×). The
latter two are threshold-flapping noise; only the first was a real defect. **The roadmap
amendment's assumption about which boards these were is wrong — corrected here.**

ROOT CAUSE (profiled, not guessed): the special-serial predicate was one OR —
`serial=1 OR serial=circulation_count OR serial<=3 OR serial=jersey_number` — which Postgres
cannot satisfy from an index, so for each of 125 editions it scanned EVERY serial
(~203 rows) and filtered 198 away: **25,375 index entries, 6,623 heap fetches, to return 607
rows**. Because that wmc leg was correlated, the latest-FMV-per-edition Unique/Merge Append
also re-ran once per output row — **607 loops, 327,554 buffer hits**.

FIX (`audit_20260803_candy_special_serials_board_union_arms`): split the OR into three UNION
arms inside a LATERAL, each an index point/range probe. Removing the correlation also let the
planner collapse the FMV join to a single Hash Right Join (**1,101 buffers, from 327,554**).

⚠ **CORRECTION to my own first claim — I initially wrote "7,388ms → 58ms (~126×)" and that
number is NOT defensible.** Re-measuring the SAME fixed view under load returned **28,174 ms**.
The plan was identical and the buffer counts were identical; only wall-clock moved. This Micro
instance's wall-clock swings ~500× with I/O contention, so a quiet "after" against a contended
"before" measures the load, not the fix. **The load-independent metric is buffer touches:
~397,000 → ~42,000–45,000, a ~9× reduction, consistent across BOTH post-fix measurements
(quiet and contended).** Like-for-like under heavy load it is 82,137 ms → 28,174 ms (~2.9×).
**Quote the ~9× buffer reduction, not the 126×.**

⚠ **REMAINING, NOT ADDRESSED:** the `candy_treasury_wallet` InitPlan (a GroupAggregate over all
25,375 candy wmc rows to pick the single top holder) is untouched by this fix and was **12,618
ms of the contended 28,174 ms (~45%)** — 27 ms when quiet. It is the next lever on this board
if it needs one; materialising or caching the treasury wallet would remove it entirely.
- `UNION` not `UNION ALL` is load-bearing — a serial can satisfy two arms (circulation_count=1,
  or jersey_number≤3) and UNION ALL would duplicate rows the single-scan OR emitted once.
- `serial_number <= 3` kept verbatim rather than tightened to `BETWEEN 1 AND 3`.

EQUIVALENCE PROVEN BEFORE APPLYING, not assumed: old and new both return **607** rows and
**both directions of `EXCEPT ALL` return 0**. `EXCEPT ALL` preserves multiplicity, so a
duplicate-count change would have surfaced.

⚠ NOT bloat/VACUUM — that hypothesis was tested and rejected: wmc is **98.4% all-visible**,
4.5% dead, autovacuum 40 min prior. The heap fetches are concentrated in the candy rows
because they are the most recently rewritten, but the fix is the query shape, not a VACUUM
(which would have decayed within hours on a table this hot).

⚠ **`public_board_slow_count` will NOT clear immediately, and that is not a failed fix.** The
arm reads `public_board_liveness_state`, refreshed only by `public_board_liveness_probe()`
called inside `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh()` — pg_cron jobid **222**,
schedule **`58 */6 * * *`** (00:58 / 06:58 / 12:58 / 18:58 UTC). The 11,193 ms sample that put
this board in breach is the **18:58Z** tick, taken hours BEFORE the fix; the next probe is
**00:58Z**. A board can therefore read "slow" for up to 6h after it has actually been fixed —
**re-measure the view directly before concluding a board is still slow, and do not re-fix one
on the strength of a stale probe.** (The daytime monitor independently re-measured this board
live at **3,883 ms**, inside its 4,100 ms budget, after the fix.) The arm will still read
BREACH at 2 afterwards because it breaches at 1 and the two threshold-flapping trophies boards
remain — deliberately not "fixed" by raising their budgets, per the standing guardrail.

Verified after: `reloptions={security_invoker=on}`, anon/authenticated SELECT **false**,
service_role **true**, 607 rows, `check_public_security_invariants()`=0,
`check_anon_write_surface()`=0.

REVERT: restore the previous definition (single OR in the WHERE clause) and re-apply
`ALTER VIEW public.candy_special_serials_board SET (security_invoker = on);`. View definition
only — no data change.

⚠ The `ALTER VIEW … SET (security_invoker = on)` is MANDATORY and shipped in the same
migration: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` silently drops `reloptions`, which cost
`v_rpc_trust_health` its `security_invoker` twice in three days (08-01 and 08-03).

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code) · fmv-recalc swept the same ~1,000 editions every run — 74% of the traded catalogue was never repriced

`/api/fmv-recalc` paginates with a cursor in `pipeline_runs.cursor_after`. It asked
`fmv_recalc_edition_page` for a 2,500-edition page over PostgREST, which clamps RPC
results to `db-max-rows`=1000 and returned 1,000. `hasMore = pageEditionIds.length === limit`
(1000 !== 2500) → false → `cursor_after=NULL` → every run restarted at offset 0, `ok=true`.

VERIFIED LIVE before shipping (the handoff premise held, unlike the last four):
- Every `fmv-recalc` run for 20h: `cursor_before='0'`, `cursor_after=NULL`, ~997 rows.
- `fmv_recalc_edition_page(..., 2500, 0)` called direct in SQL returns **2,500** rows;
  the route sees 1,000. Truncation is at PostgREST, not the function.
- Population = **11,606** editions with a sale in the 30d window → ~1,000 reachable = **74% never repriced**.
- Raw page has **0 null `edition_id`** → the raw length is exactly 1000 (the logged
  `rows_found=997` is a later post-filter number, not the page size).

FIX (`app/api/fmv-recalc/route.ts`): `DEFAULT_LIMIT` 2500 → **500**; new `MAX_PAGE_LIMIT=900`
ceiling for an explicit `body.limit` (was 5000 — a manual call could re-trigger the
truncation); `hasMore` `===` → `>=`; a tripwire that `console.error`s when a page returns
at the 1000-row cap while `limit > 1000`; and `page_size` / `edition_limit` / `has_more`
added to `pipeline_runs.extra` (it recorded haircut and wash-trade counts but not the one
number that would have shown this). Also NaN-guarded the limit parse — `Math.min(NaN, x)`
is NaN, the same class already swept out of `/api/edition-history` and `/insights`.

⚠ **Chose 500, NOT the handoff's 900.** Runs average **181s against `maxDuration=300`** and
**95 of ~402 invocations in 72h (23.6%) are killed at the wall** before writing a terminal
row. A killed run logs no `cursor_after`, so the next run retries the SAME offset — harmless
while the cursor was pinned at 0, but once it advances a systematically-slow page could
re-stall the sweep. 900 sits inside the band where a quarter of runs already die. 500 halves
the per-page work: 11,606/500 ≈ 24 pages ≈ 5h per full sweep at ~5.6 runs/h.

GUARD: extended `__tests__/invariants-fmv-recalc-chunking.test.ts` (+5 assertions). That file
already enforced the identical 1000-row cap for every `.in()` chunk site and even documents
it in its header — it just never covered the page fetch one layer up. Mutation-tested:
restoring `DEFAULT_LIMIT=2500` and `=== limit` reds exactly the two intended assertions.

REVERT: `git revert <this sha>`. No DB state to unwind — the sweep simply returns to
reprocessing page 0. Snapshots written while it works are valid and stay.

QUEUED (NOT shipped — separate defect, needs a decision): the **23.6% maxDuration kill rate**
is ~24% of fmv-recalc compute wasted. `maxDuration` is 300 but CLAUDE.md records the Vercel
Pro cap as **800** (the route comment calling 300 "the Vercel Pro maximum" is wrong), so
raising it is available and would likely eliminate the kills. Not done here: it is a cost
change and outside the cursor fix. Watch `has_more`/`page_size` in `extra` to see if any
single offset starts stalling.

**↑ FOLLOW-UP, measured post-deploy — that queued item is now mostly MOOT, and the 500 choice
is VALIDATED.** A clean run (no concurrent profiling load) does 496 editions in **123.3s**,
against the ~257s mean the 1,000-edition pages were averaging. Duration is close to LINEAR in
page size (~0.27 s/edition, minimal fixed cost), which means:
- 500 sits at **2.4× margin** under the 300s wall — the kill rate should fall sharply on its
  own, because the 23.6% was a consequence of ~257s runs against a 300s ceiling.
- The handoff's **900 would have landed at ~241s — 80% of the wall**, i.e. straight back into
  the band where a quarter of runs die. Confirms 500 over 900 on measured grounds, not caution.
- Full sweep is **24 pages ≈ 2h**, better than the 5h estimated above.
⚠ My first two post-deploy samples (265s, 271s) were CONTAMINATED by my own 82s board profiling
running concurrently, and would have argued the opposite. Measure a pipeline when you are not
also hammering the same database.
Observed so far: `0 → 500 → 1000 → 1500`, 3 of 4 runs completing; the one failure was a
self-inflicted race (a manual trigger 35s after a cron tick — don't hand-trigger this route).

**ACCURACY BASELINE at sweep position 1500/11606 (page 4 of 24), 2026-08-03 ~21:15Z — for the
next session to compare against.** Editions with ≥4 sales/30d whose published FMV exceeds 2×
their OWN 30d realised median: **Top Shot 263, All Day 200 (463 total)** vs the roadmap

**✅ RESULT at sweep position 6500/11606 (page 13 of 24), 2026-08-03 ~22:59Z — §5.1's payoff

### 2026-08-03 (Cowork, session wrap) — `classify-acquisitions-multicollection` is **NOT a cron dropout**, and the documented `p_limit` fix is **DISPROVED**. Diagnosis + docs only; no code/DB/prod change.

The 08-02 handoff routed this to the operator as *"a genuine cron-job.org dropout"*. Re-measured live: the `nfl_all_day` leg began hard-failing 2026-08-01 with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`, and the 24/day -> 8/day run drop is a **consequence** of that, not a separate scheduler fault — route `maxDuration=120` vs the fn's `statement_timeout=90s`, so when the AllDay leg burns its full 90s the 3-collection `after()` loop overruns and the lambda is killed **before `log_pipeline_run`**, leaving no row and reading as a missing trigger.

**The prescribed knob no longer works.** `docs`+memory both say *"batch-size-bound — lower `p_limit` further"* (from the 07-01 pass that set AllDay 300 -> 80). Measured from the `extra` payloads, `processed` per tick is now **0, 1, 3, 9, 20, 35** against `p_limit=80` — the limit almost never binds, so the query scans the entire AllDay priced-sales set hourly to return single digits. 80 -> 40 changes nothing; cost is now bound by the size of AllDay `sales`, which only grows. Three read-only probes all timed out: `candidates` CTE at LIMIT 80 (>120s), plain `count(*)` on the same predicate (>60s), and the inverted join driving from `wallet_moments_cache` (>90s) — so it is not fixable by reordering either. `idx_moment_acquisitions_nft_id` already exists; the anti-join probe is indexed and is not the problem.

Real fix is design work, not a knob: a **watermark** (`last_scanned_sold_at` per collection) for the hourly tick with a slow backstop for the tail, and/or a **permanent-failure reason** — AllDay sales for moments in nobody's tracked wallet can never satisfy the `EXISTS wmc` predicate yet are re-scanned every hour forever (same shape as the AllDay `unmapped_sales` backlog). Plus a synchronous `phase:"invoked"` marker so a killed `after()` is visible. Do NOT add a `sales(collection_id,nft_id)` composite (taxes hot ingest) and do NOT raise the fn timeout (the lambda is the binding budget — raising it guarantees the silent kill).

Impact: `moment_acquisitions` is cost-basis/P&L enrichment behind sign-in — an accuracy gap, not an outage (AllDay 71,773 classified). **Deliberately not patched**: ingest-adjacent, needs CI the Cowork sandbox cannot run. Correction appended to [docs/handoff-2026-08-02-open-items.md](../handoff-2026-08-02-open-items.md); memory `classify-acq-allday-batch-size` rewritten so the dead-end knob is not retried.

**Revert:** docs-only — `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-08-03 (Claude Code, interactive) — `ownership-sync-dune` reported **ok=true while starved of Dune credits**. Route + tests only; no DB/prod-data change.

- **Found while diagnosing why the Dune MCP server was 401ing.** Today's 11:40Z run logged `ok: true` with `exhausted: true`, `refreshed: false`, `refresh_note: "execute HTTP 402"` — Dune refused to re-execute the query because the monthly credits are spent. The route deliberately falls through to the LAST cached execution so the table is never emptied (correct), but it then re-ingested ~114k rows **identical to the previous run** and called it a success. Trevor's constraint is that we are **not buying more credits**, which makes an invisible starved run exactly the wrong failure mode.
- **Why nothing caught it:** `ownership-sync-dune` has **no `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` row**, so silence never pages, and `ok=true` kept it out of `v_pipeline_failure_rates`. It had no alarm of any kind. This is the [[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]] class — the platform's documented top defect pattern.
- **SHIPPED:** a refresh that was ATTEMPTED and did not complete now sets `ok=false` with `extra.stale_cache=true`, plus `extra.refresh_http_status` so the causes are separable at a glance (**402 = credits exhausted**, 404 = dune-proxy worker missing `/execute`). A walk error still wins the error message (more specific). `?norefresh=1` is explicitly NOT treated as stale — that is the operator's deliberate cache-only walk and must not become a false alarm. **Zero data-behaviour change: the fallthrough walk is untouched.**
- ⚠ **This NARROWS a prior deliberate decision, on purpose.** The existing deep test pinned `p_ok === true` on refresh failure, rationale "un-upgraded worker returns 404 → stale but valid, never empty". That scoped the fallthrough to a *transitional rollout* state; the worker is now upgraded (we get 402, not 404), so the condition it was protecting no longer applies and the ok=true had become a knowingly-wrong success. Test updated with the reasoning inline rather than silently flipped.
- **Tests 11 → 15, mutation-proven:** removing the `ok = false` reddens exactly the 404 and 402 cases and nothing else; a positive control (successful refresh ⇒ `ok=true`, `stale_cache=false`) prevents a hardcoded-false regression from passing. `tsc` clean; adjacent Dune/ownership suites 43/43.
- **NOT done (deliberate, needs Trevor):** the run still walks ~114k redundant upserts on an IOPS-bound instance when the refresh fails. Skipping that walk would save real IOPS weekly but changes ingest behaviour and risks the empty-table bootstrap path — a perf/behaviour call, not an honesty fix. **Ownership data is NOT going dark meanwhile:** `topshot_ownership` has a second source, `onchain_walk`, fresh today (118,215 rows); the `dune` leg (149,527 rows) is the bulk-parity bootstrap. `observed_at` is NOT in the upsert payload, so stale rows are **not** restamped as freshly observed.
- **QUEUED design (refined 2026-08-03, do NOT rebuild from scratch) — skipping the redundant walk.** When the refresh fails, `/results` necessarily returns the SAME execution as last time, so re-walking is a provable no-op *if* we already ingested it fully. The proposed gate — "skip when the cached execution's row count matches what the previous successful run wrote, and the table is non-empty" — is logically sound (a budget-truncated run wrote fewer rows than the execution holds, so it correctly refuses to skip). ⚠ **Its blocker is RETENTION, not logic:** "what the previous run wrote" lives in `pipeline_runs`, which keeps ~73h, while this pipeline runs **weekly** — the row is normally pruned before the next run reads it, and `pipeline_runs_daily` carries `extra_key_counts` (key PRESENCE) not values, so it cannot substitute. See [[pipeline-runs-pruned-faster-than-detection]]. **Self-contained substitute:** compare `count(*) FROM topshot_ownership WHERE source='dune'` against the cached execution's `total_row_count` — equal ⇒ fully ingested ⇒ skip. No history dependency, no new state table, and an empty table can never match so the first-run bootstrap is structurally safe. **Verify first (one `limit=1` page read, the cheapest probe):** that Dune's `/results` metadata actually exposes `total_row_count`; the route currently parses only `result.rows` + `next_offset`.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (route + test only; restores ok=true on refresh failure).

### 2026-08-03 (Cowork) — GATE-1 DEFECT: a Candy wallet rendered **$0**. A NAV flag was silently governing a DATA pipeline.

- **Measured:** `wallet_moments_cache.fmv_usd` was NULL on **0 of 25,375** Candy rows while every other collection ran 58–100% (TS 99.7%, AllDay 100.0%, Pinnacle 98.8%, Golazos 57.7%, UFC 62.2%). All 25,375 Candy rows already carried a valid `edition_key`, and the join to `editions` -> `fmv_snapshots` resolved for **all** of them — so the data was there the whole time and nothing was reading it. Candy is the most accurately-priced collection we have (FMV p50 error 7.2%), which made this the sharpest possible version of the bug: **the board was right and the portfolio view said $0.**
- **Root cause:** `app/api/wmc-fmv-populate/route.ts` built its target list from `publishedCollections()`. `published` is a **NAV flag** — it governs the collection switcher and the per-collection tab routes — and Candy ships a publicly-live board (`/insights/candy-mlb`) while `published` stays `false` **by design** (per CLAUDE.md, `CANDY_MLB_PUBLIC`, `collections.is_active` and `published` are three separate switches). So Candy was excluded from the wmc FMV **and image** denorm for its entire life, silently, with no error anywhere.
- **Fix:** target `COLLECTIONS.filter(c => c.supabaseCollectionId)` instead. **A data pipeline must follow the DATA, not the nav.** Collections with no wmc rows (`panini_blockchain`, which lives in `panini_*` tables) are a cheap no-op — the RPCs match zero rows. This also means any FUTURE collection that ships a board before flipping `published` is covered automatically rather than repeating this.
- **Backfilled immediately** rather than waiting for the next tick: **0 -> 25,375 (100%)** across **404 wallets, $137,607.85** now valued. ⚠ **DURABLE — use the CHUNKED path, not `p_force`:** `populate_wmc_fmv_from_snapshots(..., p_force => true)` **times out**; its `DISTINCT ON` joins `fmv_snapshots` on `edition_id` and only filters `e.collection_id`, so the snapshot scan is not collection-scoped. The `p_force => false` NULL-only chunked path did it in 3 calls (10k/10k/5,375).
- **DURABLE (the reusable class):** an over-loaded boolean is invisible until something downstream reads it for a purpose it was never defined for. `published` had three legitimate consumers and one illegitimate one, and only the illegitimate one was silent. When a flag governs nav, do not let it govern ingest.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the `publishedCollections()` target list. The backfilled `fmv_usd` values are correct and need no unwind (they are re-derived from `fmv_snapshots` on every tick).
