### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — RETIRED the impossible-parallel toil: hourly self-heal shipped; wave 7 cleared (3 -> 0)

- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260720_selfheal_impossible_parallel_circ`.** The same manual circ floor-raise had been applied **seven times** (waves 1-6 = `audit_20260706/10/13/16/18/19_circ_floor_raise_*`, plus wave 7 breaching ~6h after wave 6 cleared). It is mechanical, so it is now automated: `raise_impossible_parallel_circ()` on pg_cron `rpc-selfheal-impossible-parallel-circ` hourly at `:52`.
- **Safety properties, each verified live, not assumed:** **monotonic** — `new_circ > e.circulation_count` guard means it can only ever RAISE, never lower, never invent supply, never touch an edition without an offending sale; **provable** — the new value is `max(observed sold serial)`, the minimum the chain already proves (the real per-parallel backfill stays free to raise further); **scoped** to TS `::` parallels with `circulation_count > 0`; **audited** into permanent `impossible_parallel_circ_raises` (RLS on) with old values, so every raise is individually revertible; **idempotent** (no-op returning 0 when clean); grants `postgres`/`service_role` only, `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` [].
- **First run cleared wave 7: metric 3 -> 0, `status: ok`, trust breaches now [].** The three raises are more informative than wave 6's — all were seeded at **circ 99** against real sold serials of **652 / 1,680 / 2,824** (`218:8780::16`, `218:8787::16`, `258:8687::16`). **CORRECTION (measured same session — my 'fixed default' reading was WRONG, do not chase it).** TS `::` parallel circulation clusters on a legitimate ROUND print-run tier ladder: 1 (133), 5 (188), 10 (421), 25 (503), 50 (352), **99 (749)**, 500 (258), 1000 (216), 2500 (215), 4000 (216) of 3,610 parallels. 99 is a real Top Shot print run, not a placeholder — **748 of the 749 editions at circ 99 carry sales and only 3 ever exceeded it**. So there is NO bad-default to fix at the cataloging path; the class is a small number of editions whose assigned tier does not match their true run. **The self-heal IS the correct terminal answer here, not a workaround** — do not spend a session hunting a cataloging bug that the distribution says is not there.
- **Cost note for wave-N+1:** it runs instantly because it reuses the trust metric's OWN selective predicate. Two earlier attempts using a broad `LATERAL` over every `::` edition timed out under write load. Reuse the metric's predicate.
- **Process note:** the first verification appeared to show "raised 3 but audit_rows 0, metric unchanged" — a false alarm. The function call and the verification subqueries were in ONE statement, so every subquery read the same pre-write snapshot. Re-reading in a separate statement showed it had worked. This is the recorded run -> read -> write discipline; a same-block verify can make a working fix look broken and get it reverted.
- **REVERT:** `SELECT cron.unschedule('rpc-selfheal-impossible-parallel-circ'); DROP FUNCTION public.raise_impossible_parallel_circ(); UPDATE public.editions e SET circulation_count = a.old_circ FROM public.impossible_parallel_circ_raises a WHERE e.id = a.edition_id; DROP TABLE public.impossible_parallel_circ_raises;`

- **SHIPPED (code comment only).** `lock-check-batch`'s `MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7` read as a guarantee; measurement says a 7-day re-check across ~1.6M TS wmc rows needs **~226,000 checks/day** while the batch delivers **~19,200/day** (200 x 48, all succeeding since the 120s timeout fix) — ~12x short, with 1.4M rows never checked. Median pull value under $2."* **Fetched live, it rendered its entire KPI row as em-dashes** (Rips 60d `—`, Delivered $0 `—`, Mean `—`, Median `—`, Over $100 `—`, Over $1k `—`) with "Model vs reality" and the +EV ranker stuck on "Loading…". A page confidently claiming numbers in its own social preview while showing none.
- **Same root cause, worse magnitude: `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev` measured 58,234 ms against the 30s service_role timeout — 194% of budget**, so it could never succeed. (AllDay's was 26.3s / 88%: intermittent. This one: certain.)
- **The entire cost was one CTE.** `FROM topshot_pack_rip_attribution a JOIN pack_rips pr ON pr.id = a.rip_id` planned as **37,116 nested-loop index scans on `pack_rips_pkey` at ~1.554 ms each = 57.8s of the 58.2s** — cold-cache PK lookups into the 1.7 GB `pack_rips` heap. Every downstream expression (the four percentiles, the winsorized mean, the calibration weight) totalled **under 100 ms**. So the fix is narrow: materialize ONLY that join.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260720_mv_topshot_pack_rip_values` + `audit_20260720_topshot_realized_ev_use_mv_plus_refresh_cron`.** `mv_topshot_pack_rip_values` (**37,116 rows — exactly the planner's count — 340 dists, 4 MB**) with a unique index on `rip_id` for CONCURRENT refresh and a `dist_id` index for the group-by. The view's first CTE now reads it; **every other expression is copied verbatim**, so output columns, types and order are unchanged.
- **MEASURED: 58,234 ms -> 2,782 ms (~21x); from 194% of the timeout budget to 9%.** Returns 184 rows. **Downstream consumer verified**: `v_topshot_pack_ev_calibrated` still returns 798 rows.
- **Refresh `refresh_topshot_pack_rip_values()`** — SECDEF, service_role only, `statement_timeout=600s` in proconfig, pg_cron `rpc-refresh-topshot-pack-rip-values` at `5 */6 * * *` — deliberately offset from the AllDay refresh at `:35` so the two heavy refreshes never overlap. Ran once manually, clean.
- **Residual (not urgent, noted):** the remaining 2.5s is almost entirely `pack_ev_latest` inside the `ev_one` CTE — an index scan over `pack_ev_history` with a correlated SubPlan per row (33,352 loops). Worth materializing if that board ever needs to be faster, but at 9% of budget it is not a risk.
- **Health after both waves:** `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]` · RLS-off `[]` · `detect_stalled_pipelines()` `[]` · pg_cron failures none · **invalid indexes 0** · anon AND authenticated revoked on both new MVs.
- **THE GENERAL LESSON, now twice-confirmed: a plausible empty state is the perfect disguise for a failing query.** Both boards had polished copy for "no data" — one designed ("Still gathering opens…"), one implicit (em-dashes) — and both were actually timing out with hundreds of qualifying rows behind them. **Neither Sentry, nor the pipeline health checks, nor `detect_stalled_pipelines()` caught either**, because a page-level query failure isn't a pipeline and returns HTTP 200. Detection recipe: for every board with an empty/degraded state, count the rows in its backing view; if that count is nonzero, EXPLAIN the exact query against the 30s service_role budget.
- **REVERT:** `SELECT cron.unschedule('rpc-refresh-topshot-pack-rip-values'); DROP FUNCTION public.refresh_topshot_pack_rip_values();` then recreate the prior CTE body from migration history, then `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW public.mv_topshot_pack_rip_values;`

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — ROOT CAUSE, and it was NOT my regression: `/insights/allday-pack-reality` has been silently empty because its view exceeds the 30s service_role timeout. Materialized it: **26,284 ms -> 11.5 ms**, board returns 302

Chasing my own suspected regression found a pre-existing silent failure that is worse than the bug I was chasing.

- **My two-page hypothesis was WRONG.** After shipping the one-page fix, the board STILL read "0 qualifying dists". So the cause was never the page count.
- **ROOT CAUSE: `service_role` carries `statement_timeout = 30s` (verified in `pg_db_role_setting`), and `v_allday_pack_realized_ev` measures ~26.3s.** Its inline `realized` CTE GroupAggregates **2,815,039** AllDay `pack_rips` rows (900,336 shared hits + 109,442 reads) and computes a `percentile_cont` median per dist. That sits inside a 14% margin of the timeout, so the read fails under any contention — **proven directly: the query timed out in my own MCP session.** The page then falls to its empty state, whose copy ("Still gathering opens. NFL All Day primary pack sales have ended…") reads as a legitimate product state. **A silent failure wearing a designed empty state — the exact class CLAUDE.md warns about.** 302 rows genuinely qualified the whole time.
- **This predates tonight.** My clamp change did not cause it and could not have fixed it; it only turned an intermittent failure into a certain one for a few hours. Corrects the prior entry's "regression I introduced" framing: the regression was real but was masking a bigger standing bug.
- **CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is NOT reachable from this tooling — recorded so nobody re-derives it.** A covering index on `pack_rips (collection_id, dist_id) INCLUDE (pull_value_usd)` was the first fix attempted. A bare statement hits the ~30s timeout mid-build; combining it with `SET statement_timeout` fails with **`25001: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block`**, because MCP multi-statement calls are transaction-wrapped (independently confirmed earlier: a `set_config(...,true)` persisted across statements in one call). The invalid index the failed build left behind was dropped and verified clean (**0 invalid indexes; `pack_rips` back to its original 9**).
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260720_mv_allday_pack_realized` + `audit_20260720_allday_realized_ev_use_mv_plus_refresh_cron`.** New MV `mv_allday_pack_realized` holds the per-dist realized aggregate (**3,120 rows, 360 kB**, byte-verified against the live CTE's 3,120 groups), with a unique index on `dist_id` so refresh runs CONCURRENTLY and never blocks readers. `v_allday_pack_realized_ev` now joins it instead of computing the CTE — **column names, types and order identical**, `security_invoker` preserved. This mirrors the shape already in place: the other half of that view was ALREADY materialized (`mv_allday_pack_ev_corrected`); this was the missing half.
- **MEASURED: 26,284 ms -> 11.5 ms (~2,280x), buffers 1,012,296 -> 110.** Board returns exactly **302** rows, matching the DB. Comfortably inside the 30s budget with ~2,600x headroom instead of 14%.
- **Refresh: `refresh_allday_pack_realized()`** — SECDEF, service_role only (anon/authenticated explicitly revoked), `statement_timeout=600s` in **proconfig** (not inline: pg_cron sends its command as one simple-query batch, so an inline SET arms too late — the documented trap here). pg_cron `rpc-refresh-allday-pack-realized`, `35 */6 * * *`, active. Ran once manually: clean, 3,120 rows.
- **MV grants:** anon + authenticated revoked (Supabase's default per-role grant, the trap hit twice already this session). Safe because both readers — the page and `/api/public/insights/allday-pack-reality` — import `supabaseAdmin` (the route aliases it `supabaseAdmin as supabase`, which is what made it look like an anon client on first read).
- **Health after: `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]` · RLS-off `[]` · `detect_stalled_pipelines()` `[]` · pg_cron failures none · invalid indexes 0.**
- **REVERT:** `SELECT cron.unschedule('rpc-refresh-allday-pack-realized'); DROP FUNCTION public.refresh_allday_pack_realized();` then recreate the CTE-based view body from migration history, then `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW public.mv_allday_pack_realized;`
- **QUEUED — audit the other boards for the same silent-timeout class.** Any surface whose empty state is plausible can hide a failing query. The tell is a designed empty state plus a nonzero row count in the backing view. `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev` reads the same `pack_rips` table and is worth measuring next.

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — BOTH Dune pipelines hit the account DATAPOINT cap (HTTP 402); window_days 7 -> 2 as a hedge; free Flow-REST worker is the sustainable path

- **THE FAILURE.** `sync-sales-ingest-dune` last succeeded 3:11pm PT (9 windows, 865 inserted / 34,064 filled), then 402 at 5:11 / 7:11 / 9:11pm. `sync-sales-seller-recovery-dune` has 402'd every tick since 6:47pm, parked at `2026-01-15..2026-01-22`. Error body: *"This api request would exceed your configured datapoint limit per billing cycle."*
- **THE LESSON — the binding Dune constraint is DATAPOINTS, not CREDITS.** Budget was being tracked as credits (~900/2,500, comfortable) while the cap that actually bit is a **separate per-billing-cycle datapoint limit**. These full-history queries return 100k+ rows per 7-day window, so datapoints burn far faster than credits. **Track datapoints, not credits, when costing any Dune-backed backfill.**
- **Only visible because of `8928041e`.** That commit made the route log Dune's response body instead of a bare status. Without it this was three identical `execute HTTP 402` lines with no cause — the same swallow-the-error shape that cost hours earlier in this thread.
- **Failing SAFELY.** Every failed tick reports `windows_done: 0`, nothing partial written, cursors parked (`sales_ingest_state` 2025-09-03, `sales_seller_recovery_state` 2026-01-22). Both resume from exactly where they stopped whenever the cap lifts; no cleanup and no dedup risk.
- **SHIPPED (DB-only, reversible) — `window_days` 7 -> 2 on both state tables.** A hedge, not a fix: total datapoints for a full drain are fixed by row count, so this does NOT reduce the overall bill. It only lets a smaller request fit if any cycle headroom remains. If ticks keep 402'ing, the cycle is genuinely exhausted and the honest state is "paused until reset". **Revert:** set `window_days = 7` on both.
- **Trevor's call: NOT upgrading the Dune plan.** So the Dune lane is capped by design and the **free Flow-REST counterparty worker is the sustainable path** — it has no Dune dependency, runs on Cloudflare's free tier, and is unaffected (`sales_counterparty_recovered` 203,336 and climbing; ~34.5k rows/day at 120/tick every 5 min). It will keep draining the null-seller backlog regardless.
- **Watch item:** the 402 ticks log `ok=false`, so both pipelines will appear in failure sweeps until the cycle resets. That is honest reporting, but if it masks a real failure, consider suppressing via `pipeline_alert_suppression` rather than disabling the crons (disabled crons are the documented silent-kill class).

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — POST-SHIP CATCH: my own clamp fix REGRESSED `/insights/allday-pack-reality` (paging doubled a 26s view). Fixed forward by pushing the filter into SQL; Top Shot board verified GOOD at 1,233

Post-ship verification of `1f71a9b` found the fix worked on three boards and broke the fourth. Recording the miss in full because the lesson is general.

- **VERIFIED GOOD — `/insights/topshot-pack-market` now reads "1233 qualifying dists"** live, exactly the DB count, up from the silently-clamped 1,000. The discount/premium/most-traded rankings are now computed over the complete qualifying set. This was the headline defect and it is fixed.
- **REGRESSION I INTRODUCED — `/insights/allday-pack-reality` rendered "0 qualifying dists".** Cause: `v_allday_pack_realized_ev` costs **26.3s** per read (measured: it GroupAggregates **2.8M `pack_rips` rows**; 902,747 shared hits + 109,549 reads). At 1,559 qualifying rows my `fetchAllPaged` issued **TWO** such reads instead of one — ~52s — and the build-time prerender took the error path and rendered the empty state.
- **The comparison that isolates it:** `v_topshot_pack_market` costs **837ms**, so its two pages (1,233 rows) total ~1.7s and rendered fine. Same code change, 30x different view cost, opposite outcome. **Paging is not free — it multiplies the cost of the underlying query by the page count. Measure the view before paginating it.**
- **FIXED FORWARD, not reverted** — pushed the page's own `priced` predicate into SQL (`.gt("pack_price", 0)` + `.not("modeled_gross_ev","is",null)`). That cuts **1,559 -> 302 rows**, which fits in ONE page, halving the work back to the pre-change cost while still eliminating truncation. The JS `priced` filter is byte-identical, so the rendered buckets and `qualifying` count are unchanged by construction — this is strictly better than both the old truncating `.limit(1000)` and my two-page version. Applied to the page AND `/api/public/insights/allday-pack-reality` so they cannot disagree.
- **Durable rule to carry: before converting a `.limit()` to paging, EXPLAIN the source.** If it is an expensive aggregate view, either push filters down so it stays one page, or leave the limit and disclose the truncation — do not silently double a 26s query. A cheap-view assumption is what made this a regression rather than a clean fix.
- **Honest note on blast radius:** I could not establish whether that page showed data *before* my change — only 302 of 1,559 rows have `pack_price > 0`, and the old query had no `.order()`, so PostgREST's arbitrary 1,000 may well have contained few or no priced rows. So the pre-existing state may also have been ~0. Either way the current fix is correct and the post-deploy render is the check that matters.
- **VERIFIED:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; allday-pack-reality suite 3/3 and `fetchAllPaged` 6/6 green (fixture builders gained `.not()`).
- **REVERT:** `git revert <sha>` restores the two-page read (do not — it re-breaks the board); reverting the whole clamp fix is `git revert 1f71a9b`.

Bug report: Moments→Sold shows 0 for a wallet with 39 sales; suspected the client filter `e.collection_slug === dbSlug`.

- **INVESTIGATED FIRST (no blind change).** Called `get_wallet_transaction_history('0xbd94cade097e50ac',200,0,'sells')` live: `total_count` 39, events carry `collection_slug` = **`nba_top_shot`** (underscore, len 12, no hidden chars) — 38 `nba_top_shot` + 1 `nfl_all_day`. `toDbSlug('nba-top-shot')` = `nba_top_shot`, so on a TS board the ORIGINAL filter would keep 38, not 0. **The reported "0" is not reproducible from clean data + a correct board**, so the failure is a runtime `dbSlug`/`collection`-prop value the server data can't reveal — exactly why the report said "log dbSlug and one e.collection_slug side by side before changing anything."
- **SHIPPED (code) — `components/collection/WalletSoldMomentsView.tsx`.** (1) Resolve `dbSlug` defensively: `toDbSlug(collection) ?? (fromDbSlug(collection) ? collection : null)` — accepts `collection` passed as EITHER the URL slug (`nba-top-shot`) or the DB slug (`nba_top_shot`), so a mis-passed form can't zero the board. (2) Filter accepts EITHER identifier and TRIMs the event value: `new Set([dbSlug, collection])` membership on `(e.collection_slug ?? '').trim()` — mirrors the proven sibling `WalletPacksView` (`=== dbSlug || === collection`), defends stray whitespace/form drift. **Kept the filter, per the report — both accepted values are THIS collection's own identifiers, so no other collection's sales can leak onto the board.** The `!dbSlug` → show-all fallback (documented) is preserved for a genuinely unresolvable collection. (3) Added a guarded `console.warn` that fires ONLY when events>0 but rows==0, logging `dbSlug` + raw `collection` + a sample of event slugs side-by-side — the report's requested diagnostic, so if it still zeroes the real values surface in the browser console instead of a silent empty board. `tsc` clean on the file.
- **CONFIRMED (2nd report concern) — the 200-row single-page cap CAN hide TS rows behind other collections for a heavy seller, but it is DISCLOSED, not silent.** The component fetches ONE page (limit 200, offset 0); the RPC returns all collections newest-first, so a wallet with >200 non-TS sells newer than its TS sells could show 0 TS despite having TS sales. The existing `truncated` banner ("Showing the 200 most recent sales across all collections; this wallet has N total") surfaces it. A true fix needs a collection param on the RPC (or paginate-until-N) — out of scope, not the 39-sale case (39<200). Left as-is with the disclosure.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — LIVE public boards were serving TRUNCATED data: two `/insights` surfaces silently dropped 233 and 559 rows before ranking. Fixed at 8 call sites behind one shared helper (`lib/supabase-paginate.ts`), +7 tests

Swept the PostgREST 1,000-row clamp class that produced the Panini `.limit(3000)` bug earlier today. It was not a one-off — it is live and wrong on public surfaces right now.

- **`/insights/topshot-pack-market` — ACTIVELY WRONG. 1,233 rows qualify (`n_sales >= 5`); `.limit(1000)` served 1,000.** ~233 dropped.
- **`/insights/allday-pack-reality` — ACTIVELY WRONG, worst of the set. 1,559 qualify; ~559 dropped.**
- **The severity is the ranking, not the row count.** Neither query carried an `.order()`, so PostgREST returned an ARBITRARY 1,000 — and both pages then compute "biggest discount / biggest premium / most traded" (and over/under/on-model) top-15 lists **in JS over that truncated set**. So a genuine top-15 discount pack could be absent from a public deal-finding board, nondeterministically. That is a credibility defect, not a cosmetic one.
- **`/insights/allday-pack-market` — 796 qualify, ~20% headroom.** Not truncating yet, same unordered shape, fixed alongside.
- **`/insights/market` (The RPC Index) — `.limit(2000)`, silently 1,000.** 686 rows today against a ~847 ceiling (121 days x <=7 tiers) so it is NOT truncating — but it sorts `d ASCENDING`, so the first overflow would drop **the NEWEST days off a market-index chart** while keeping stale history. Worst-possible failure mode for that surface; fixed pre-emptively.
- **The JSON APIs had the identical bug** — `/api/public/insights/{topshot-pack-market,allday-pack-market,allday-pack-reality,market}` all repeated it, so page and API would have disagreed after a page-only fix. **8 call sites fixed total** (4 server pages + 4 routes).
- **SHIPPED — `lib/supabase-paginate.ts` / `fetchAllPaged()`.** This class has now caused live wrong numbers **five separate times** (lock-roi, market, sets-db, market-pulse's 4x undercount, Panini squeeze), so the workaround now lives in one reviewed place instead of being re-derived per call site. Pages `.range()`, caps `pageSize` at 1,000 (a larger request would be clamped and then read as a false short-page = silent truncation *inside* the fix), terminates only on a short page, and returns an explicit **`truncated`** flag for maxPages/page-error so a partial set can never be mistaken for a complete one. Two rules documented in the header: the query MUST carry a deterministic `.order()` (Postgres gives no stable order without one, so paging an unordered query can duplicate rows on one page and drop them from another), and callers must check `truncated`.
- **Added `.order("dist_id")` to the three pack boards** — previously absent, which is what made the truncation nondeterministic *and* would have made naive pagination unsafe.
- **VERIFIED:** `tsc --noEmit` clean (it caught a real defect mid-change — `fetchAllPaged` narrows `error` to `string`, but four call sites still did `error.message`); **23/23 green** across the five public-insights route suites plus **6 new tests** for the helper (over-cap paging, short-page stop, exact-multiple probe page, pageSize clamp, page-error keeps partial rows + flags truncated, maxPages flags truncated). Fixture builders gained `.order()`/`.range()`.
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** `/api/public/insights/pack-reality`'s `.limit(1000)` — measured 184 rows, genuinely under the cap; and the many `.limit(100..200)` "top N" limits on other insights pages, which are intentional.
- **KNOWN REMAINING (not fixed, flagged): ingest/admin routes carry clamped limits too** — `offers-sweep .limit(10000)` (x2), `badge-sync .limit(10000)`, `pinnacle-metadata-backfill .limit(5000/8000/10000)`, `flowty-analytics .limit(100000)`. These are **throughput** bugs, not correctness ones (each tick processes 1,000 instead of the intended N, so sweeps drain ~10x slower than designed) and they touch ingest paths, so they want a deliberate owner session rather than a blind sweep. QUEUED: CLAMPED-LIMITS-INGEST-THROUGHPUT.
- **REVERT:** `git revert <code sha>` — restores the prior `.limit()` calls; `lib/supabase-paginate.ts` and its test are additive and can stay.

### 2026-07-19 (Claude Code, interactive) — LOCK FRESHNESS, Trevor's call = "fix on-demand refresh": the TS on-view refresh now converges the VIEWED wallet (stalest-first + stamps lock_checked_at); the `<500` guard that hid overstated whales is gone

Trevor picked the on-demand-refresh path over batch throughput / display-caveat / stop (the batch is ~24× short of a 7-day promise, so trustworthiness has to come from the wallet a user actually views, not from grinding 1.6M rows). Two real bugs found and fixed in the existing `cache-refresh?refreshLocked=1` path.

- **BUG 1 (the one that perpetuated the overstatement) — the trigger's `<500` guard was backwards.** `collection/page.tsx` fired the on-view lock refresh only `if (lockedCount < 500)` — i.e. it SKIPPED exactly the wallets already showing many (stale) locks. So an overstated whale (the ref wallet's ~13k months-old `is_locked=true`) never self-corrected on view. **Fixed:** fire on every Top Shot collection view; the server early-outs cheaply when nothing is stale (below), so this is safe.
- **BUG 2 (why it couldn't converge) — the backfill re-checked the same first-500 forever and never stamped freshness.** The old body took `allCachedIds.slice(0,500)` in on-chain order (so a whale's moments 501+ were never refreshed) and wrote **only `is_locked`, never `lock_checked_at`**. **Fixed (`app/api/cache-refresh/route.ts` step 7):** one query pulls the **stalest** held moments (`lock_checked_at` ASC NULLS FIRST, 7-day cutoff, cap 500) + the exact stale count; refreshes those via GQL `isLocked`; **stamps `lock_checked_at=now()` alongside `is_locked`** so it's a real freshness check and the batch stops re-selecting it. Each view advances the wallet's freshness frontier ⇒ a normal wallet is fully fresh in one view, a whale converges over a few. A fresh wallet costs **one indexed count query, no GQL** (early-out when `staleTotal=0`). GQL miss → row left stale + unstamped so a later view retries (never stamps an unverified value). Service-role client, so the `lock_checked_at` write is permitted.
- **Net effect:** the lock count on the wallet a user is looking at becomes trustworthy without any caveat and without the impossible 7-day batch chase; the batch (now reliable after the 120s-timeout fix in the entry two above) stays background best-effort for un-viewed wallets. Tests: `__tests__/api-cache-refresh-deep.test.ts` updated — stalest-first refresh now asserts BOTH `is_locked` + a `lock_checked_at` stamp, plus a new fresh-wallet early-out case (no GQL, no write); **7/7 green**, `tsc` clean on the changed files (only pre-existing `.next/types` phantom errors for already-deleted routes). **Revert:** `git revert <code sha>`.
- **SCOPE CAVEAT (verified live) — on-demand refresh fires for SIGNED-IN viewers only.** Deploy `d01e9343` READY on prod (www alias). Driving `/api/cache-refresh?wallet=<ref>&refreshLocked=1` **unauthenticated** returns the login shell — the route is `proxy.ts`-gated (it's a wmc WRITE path), so the client trigger only reaches it when the browser carries an auth cookie. This is a PRE-EXISTING posture (the feature was always signed-in-only; my change didn't alter it) and it's the right audience — a signed-in owner viewing their own portfolio is exactly the complaint's context (the ref wallet: 14,948 TS rows, all stale >7d, oldest 2026-04-13). **Anon viewers do NOT trigger it and rely on the batch.** Extending it to anon would mean adding a write route to the anon allowlist in `proxy.ts` (off-limits auth/lockdown file) — deliberately NOT done; flagged for Trevor if anon-viewer lock freshness is wanted. End-to-end authed prod drive not run here (no secret in-session); logic proven by the 7/7 tests + the READY deploy, DB timeout fix separately verified live (00:38Z tick ok=true).
- **STILL open (Trevor, not this fix):** the batch's 7-day promise remains structurally unmeetable — `MAX_AGE_DAYS=7` stays a background target, not a guarantee. On-demand now covers the display-trust need, so a "locks as of <date>" caveat is unnecessary for viewed wallets. Steps 2 (BATCH_LIMIT raise — unsafe until the selection read is made cheap) and 3 (denser cron string — actively harmful now, would add :08/:38-style collisions → more 60s selection-read timeouts) remain **not recommended** and were NOT shipped.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — CORRECTION to the bridge entry below: "go-live = flip is_active + refresh, no further DDL" is TOO STRONG. It is true for the set DIRECTORY, false for the set EDITION GRID.

Self-caught within the hour by tracing what actually consumes `editions_unified`, instead of trusting that a bridge into the shared plane implies shared surfaces light up. **No shipped code is wrong; the claim about what it buys was.**

  2. The **edition grid is a per-collection IF branch inside each RPC.** Pinnacle has an explicit `IF p_collection_id = v_pinnacle_uuid THEN ... FROM pinnacle_catalog`; every other collection falls through to `FROM editions e WHERE e.collection_id = p_collection_id`. **The bridge does NOT deliver this layer.**
- **Consequence at go-live as it stands:** flipping `is_active` + `refresh_sets_summary()` makes 54 Panini sets appear in `sets_summary` and gives `get_set_detail` a header — but `get_set_editions` falls through to the ELSE branch, queries `editions` for a collection that has **0 rows there**, and renders an **EMPTY grid**. A set page that looks broken is worse than one that 404s.
- **Why nothing is at risk today:** the arm is inert, so `sets_summary` has no Panini rows, so `v_variants IS NULL` fires the early return before any branch is reached. The gap is unreachable until `is_active` flips. The set page also `notFound()`s on `lib/collections.ts`, which has no Panini route entry.

Deliberately NOT shipped tonight: it means `CREATE OR REPLACE` on two large live SECDEF RPCs that serve all five published collections' set pages, for a branch that cannot execute until a product decision Trevor has not made. Low knowledge risk (shape fully characterised above), real blast-radius risk. Do it **with** the go-live, not before, and re-verify a TS + a Pinnacle set page after.
- **Corrected go-live sequence for Panini set pages:** (1) resolve the `panini_blockchain` collections row — it still says `chain=ethereum` / "Panini Blockchain", describing the retired OpenSea plane, and `chain_type` has no `sawtooth` value; (2) ship the two RPC branches; (3) add the `lib/collections.ts` entry + route dirs; (4) flip `is_active`; (5) `refresh_sets_summary()`. Steps 1-3 are DDL/code and must land before 4.
- **Durable lesson: a UNION arm on a "unified" view is not automatically a bridge to the surfaces you assume it feeds.** Trace the consumer chain to the RPC body before claiming a surface lights up — `editions_unified` has exactly ONE consumer (`sets_summary`) and zero repo references, which is far narrower than its name suggests.

So the Cowork entry's fix order ("202-wrap THEN raise BATCH_LIMIT to ~800") is **still unsafe at step 2**: the read is O(limit × 480 hot wallets) and measured **5.8s warm @200 → 24.5s warm @800** (single call, quiet window). Under the contention that already kills it at 200/60s, an 800-limit read fails nearly every tick. The "17–25s inside 270s headroom" is the **Cadence leg** (7× headroom, 13–22 wallets/tick) — the *read* is the bottleneck and it is NOT governed by the soft deadline. **Do not raise BATCH_LIMIT until the read is reliable + cheap.**
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260720_get_lock_check_batch_statement_timeout_120s`.** `ALTER FUNCTION public.get_lock_check_batch(text,integer,integer) SET statement_timeout='120s'` (proconfig verified `[search_path…, statement_timeout=120s]`). Stops the 60s premature kill so the after()-context read (270s soft deadline / 300s maxDuration) completes and delivers its 200 rows instead of discarding 60s of IOPS. Fn is non-inlined (has `SET search_path`), so proconfig applies (precedent: `raise_edition_offers_from_chain` 600s). **~2× delivered throughput at the current limit, ZERO increase in peak per-tick load** — the disciplined "one lever, then watch a day" move under the IOPS caution, and the true completion of Step 1 (raising throughput first would have deepened the silent failure). **Revert:** `ALTER FUNCTION public.get_lock_check_batch(text,integer,integer) RESET statement_timeout;` **Target metric:** lock-check-batch ok=false rate ~50% → ~0 over the next day; rows_written>0 on ≥90% of ticks.
- **CONFIRMS the Cowork entry's "Step 4 is unavoidable" honest read, with numbers.** TS wmc: **1,610,949 rows, 1,581,439 stale >7d (98%), 1,425,215 NEVER checked (88%)**, oldest check **2026-04-13**. ### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — LOCK FRESHNESS: the ceiling is cron-job.org's 30s cap, NOT the batch size — fix order is 202-wrap THEN raise

Trevor: "we need lock freshness to not be a concern." Sizing the real fix. Two of my own earlier recommendations are RETRACTED below.

- **RETRACTED — "scope the promise to viewable wallets" is not a lever.** Measured: **1,609,262 of 1,610,949** TS wmc rows already belong to seeded/saved wallets; only **1,687** do not. The whales ARE the seeded wallets (`0x0d744d23` = 149,506 rows, in the viewable set). There is no smaller subset to retreat to, so honest freshness means genuinely refreshing ~1.6M rows on cycle.
- **RETRACTED — "raise BATCH_LIMIT into the time headroom" is unsafe AS-IS.** The headroom is real (runs finish in **17-25s** against `SOFT_DEADLINE_MS` 270s / `maxDuration` 300 = ~10x), but the binding constraint is elsewhere: `lock-check-batch` is triggered from **cron-job.org at `8,38`, which has a hard 30-SECOND client timeout**. `docs/operations/cron-schedule.md` already flags it: "runs 17-33s, brushes the 30s cap (202-wrap pending)". Raising the batch pushes every run past 30s -> cron-job.org marks them failed and may AUTO-DISABLE the entry (the documented silent-kill class). **Raising the batch before the 202-wrap would stop lock checking entirely.**
- **THE FIX, IN THIS ORDER (do not reorder):** (1) convert the route to the **CRON-30S pattern** - return 202 immediately + do the work in `after()`, exactly as `pinnacle-sync` did in `8ceca936`; verify a tick still writes `lock_checked_at` and that cron-job.org stops recording failures. (2) THEN raise `BATCH_LIMIT` (200 -> ~800 as a first step, ~4x, landing ~80s inside the 270s soft deadline) and re-measure. Target arithmetic: a true 7-day promise over 1.6M rows needs **~229,000 checks/day**; current actual is **~3,283/day**; 200x48 = 9,600/day is the present theoretical ceiling. Even 800/run x 48 = 38,400/day is ~6x short, so **the cadence must rise too** (`8,38` -> a denser comma list) once the 202-wrap makes long runs safe.
- **Already fixed upstream (confirmed live):** the scoping to `["nba_top_shot","disney_pinnacle"]` landed - `unsupported_collections` is now `{}` in every recent run, so no batch slots are wasted on All Day/Golazos (which have no on-chain lock primitive).
- **Honest read on the promise:** `MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7` is currently ~70x oversubscribed. Until throughput rises, either the constant should be raised to something the pipeline can actually honour, or the UI must say "locks as of <date>" - because a 7-day claim the system cannot meet is the thing that made lock counts untrustworthy in the first place.
- **NOT SHIPPED** - a botched 202-wrap silently stops lock checking with no error, and this arrived at the end of a long session with no room to watch a tick. Queued as WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS (supersedes WMC-LOCK-CHECK-COVERAGE).

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — PARITY ASSESSMENT: Panini and Candy sit on opposite sides of the shared plane; measured, not assumed

Trevor asked what it takes to reach Top Shot / All Day parity. Answered from live measurement rather than a feature checklist. Doc: [docs/strategy/parity-assessment-panini-candy-2026-07-19.md](../strategy/parity-assessment-panini-candy-2026-07-19.md). **Docs-only — no code, no schema change.**

- **THE STRUCTURAL SPLIT (the finding that reframes everything).** Candy is INSIDE the shared plane — **125 `editions`, 25,375 `wallet_moments_cache`**. Panini is entirely OUTSIDE it — **0 rows in `editions`, `sales`, `wmc` AND `fmv_snapshots`**, with 1,923 editions / 8,201 serials / 2,542 FMV rows living in the parallel `panini_*` plane. So they are not two instances of one problem: Candy inherits shared surfaces once it has data, while every shared RPC, entity page, wallet surface and concierge tool is **structurally blind** to Panini.
- **PROVEN, not theorised — Candy already inherits shared analytics.** `analytics_sets_directory(ARRAY['candy_mlb'],…)` returns a populated row TODAY (`2026 MLB Base Series ICONs`, `edition_count` 125, `set_external_id` candy-mlb-base-icons-2026, series 1). That row exists **because of this morning's metadata backfill** — creating the `sets`/`players` rows and filling tier/set_id/player_id lit up a shared surface with zero code change.
- **LATENT TRAP FOUND (Candy) — the slug-normalization `CASE` silently drops it.** `analytics_liquidity_distribution` / `analytics_packs_summary` / `analytics_sets_summary` / `analytics_fmv_tier_pulse` and others normalize via `CASE c.slug WHEN 'nba_top_shot' THEN 'topshot' WHEN 'nfl_all_day' THEN 'allday' …` with **no arm for `candy_mlb` and no ELSE** ⇒ NULL ⇒ row dropped downstream. Swept it: **28 shared RPCs reference nba_top_shot + nfl_all_day and NOT ONE mentions `candy_mlb` or `panini`.** Invisible today (no Candy FMV to show); the danger is it stays invisible AFTER Candy gets data and reads as an ingest bug. **Deliberately NOT fixed now** — adding arms would surface an `is_active=false` collection with zero rows behind it and could not be verified; queued to ship WITH the FMV work.
- **PANINI HAS MORE THAN EXPECTED, AND TWO HARD CAVEATS.** It carries per-serial **ownership on 8,201/8,201 serials (1,011 distinct owners)**, **2,968 real sales across 1,193 editions**, 1,194 special-serial flags, 7,239 best-offers — enough in principle for wallet, special-serial, offer and sales-history surfaces. But (1) **owners are usernames, not addresses** (`EZGOLF`, `lepwn` — no `0x`), and RPC's entire wallet stack is address-keyed with no way to link the two identity spaces; and (2) **serial coverage is 6.21%** — 8,201 held of **132,080** total supply across discovered editions, on top of an edition list that is itself listing-gated at ~46% trustworthy.
- **RECOMMENDATION — do NOT bridge Panini into the shared plane yet.** A bridge is schema-feasible (every `panini_editions` column maps) and would buy entity pages, analytics, concierge reach and sets surfaces. It would NOT fix wallet surfaces (caveats above), it would first need a decision about the existing `panini_blockchain` collections row (`chain=ethereum`, `is_active=false` — that row describes the OLD OpenSea plane, not the Sawtooth WC Prizm data), and critically **it multiplies the disclosure obligation**: today one gated board carries one honest coverage note; bridging pushes a 46%-complete index into shared surfaces that have nowhere to say so. Panini's data is good enough to be a strong STANDALONE board set and too incomplete to be a trustworthy citizen of the shared plane.
- **Ordered dependency for Candy (only the first is outside our control):** first sale → FMV → `CASE` arms → route dirs → `is_active`. Explicit anti-recommendation: **do not build Candy route dirs before there is data to render** — empty tabs are worse than an absent collection.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — `/insights` hub live stats are DOWN; root cause is the 7-day sales scan, but measurements are contention-contaminated — did NOT ship an index

Chasing a cheap count source for the OG cards led into a live public-page defect. Diagnosed to a component, then deliberately stopped short of a fix because the evidence is not trustworthy right now.

- **LIVE, USER-VISIBLE: the `/insights` hub renders WITHOUT its live stat line.** `get_insights_hub_stats()` fails; the page catches it and degrades, so the hub returns 200 with all its cards but every "N editions ≥50% squeezed"-style stat is missing. Verified by fetching `/insights` (200, `x-vercel-cache: HIT`, 85 KB, cards present, **zero live-stat strings**). The function was specifically rewritten to a single scan on 2026-07-18 (`995055de`, 19.7s → 5.7s); it is now past even a **2-minute** timeout as `postgres`. Role limits: service_role 30s, anon 3s — the hub reads via service role, so 30s is the real ceiling.
- **COMPONENT ISOLATED — it is NOT the board counts.** I assumed the three computed-view counts were the cost and was wrong. Timed individually: `topshot_squeeze_board` **0.29s** (9,274 rows), `topshot_set_squeeze_board` **0.26s** (242), `pinnacle_scarcity_board` **0.06s** (2,272). The cost is the `recent_sales` MATERIALIZED CTE — `sales` over 7 days with `price_usd > 0`, **32,071 rows**, measured at **39.5s**, then **108.6s** on a repeat.
- **NOTE the counter-intuitive detail:** an *unfiltered* `count(*)` on `topshot_squeeze_board` is 0.29s, but `count(*) ... WHERE squeeze_pct >= 50` is **3.3s** — the filter forces evaluation of the computed column and pulls in the badge join + per-row FMV partition probes. Cheap and expensive counts on the same view differ by 11x depending on the predicate. Worth knowing before anyone "just adds a count".
- **DID NOT SHIP AN INDEX — the numbers are contaminated.** The obvious read is a missing `sold_at` index (the plan uses `sales_2026_collection_id_sold_at_idx`, a composite whose leading column the query never constrains, and the near-perfect `idx_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window` is unusable because its predicate also requires `edition_id IS NOT NULL`). But: **Planning Time alone was 4,465 ms**, which is RPC's documented tell for disk-budget exhaustion, and a live check found the instance mid-contention — **32 active queries, all 32 waiting on locks/IO, longest running 309 s**, wait events `IPC:BufferIo` / `IO:DataFileSync` / `IO:WalWrite`, pg_cron failures up 2 → 3. The 39.5s → 108.6s → timeout spread across three runs of the same query IS the contention. Per the project's own rule (*seq-scan ⇒ add an index; index-driven + low cost ⇒ starved*) this plan is index-driven, so the indicated answer is **starved**, not missing-index. Adding an index on this evidence would be guessing, and index builds themselves consume the IOPS that are already short.
- **QUEUED — `INSIGHTS-HUB-STATS-TIMEOUT` (MED, user-visible).** Re-measure `SELECT count(*), sum(price_usd) FROM sales WHERE sold_at >= now() - interval '7 days' AND price_usd > 0` in a QUIET window. Behavior-equivalent for correct-size wallets, correct for large ones. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — the filter fix was only PARTIAL: PostgREST silently clamped `.limit(3000)` to 1000. Paginated with `.range()`.

So the fetch quietly returned 1,000 of 1,833 and the filters were still wrong, just less wrong: **Rookies went 43 → 177, but the true total is 400.**
- **Caught only because I made the scope note honest.** The new note renders *"Showing 300 of N matching editions"*, and it read **"300 of 1,000"** on an unfiltered board that the KPI directly above declares as **1,833 indexed editions**. A round 1,000 against a known 1,833 is a clamp signature. Had I left the note vague ("showing top 300"), the truncation would have stayed invisible — the honesty fix is what surfaced the correctness bug.
- **SHIPPED — `.range()` pagination.** `fetchRows()` now loops `.range(p*1000, p*1000+999)` until a short page returns, with `MAX_PAGES = 10` as a hard stop so a runaway view can never spin the request, and it returns whatever it has on error rather than blanking the board. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Payload measured before/after** (cold ISR render, so load times are worst-case): 300 rows → transfer 24 KB / decoded 229 KB / load 1,820 ms; 1,000 rows → 42 KB / 433 KB / 3,215 ms. Transfer stays small because the row data gzips well; the growth is decoded size and hydration. Will re-measure warm at the full 1,833 and reconsider if it degrades — if it does, the right answer is server-side filtering (re-fetch on filter change), not re-truncating the fetch and silently breaking the filters again.
- **Pattern worth carrying:** this is the third instance today of *"a bounded fetch treated as the whole set"* — KPIs (300-slice as set totals), filters (300-slice as the filter universe), and now the clamp (1000 as 1,833). Each was invisible to typecheck and tests. **Any client-side aggregate or filter over a server-bounded fetch should be treated as a silent-truncation bug until proven otherwise, and the bound should be asserted, not assumed.**

Measured against the full board: **Rookies 43 of 400 shown (11%)** · **≤ /25: 271 of 935 (29%)** · **≤ /10: 209 of 578 (36%)** · **1-of-1s: 90 of 117 (77%)**. Messi read 100% only because all 20 of his cards clear the FMV cut — which is exactly why the defect is easy to miss by spot-check: it is invisible for expensive cards and severe for cheap ones. A collector clicking "ROOKIES" was seeing a ninth of the rookies.
- **FIX.** `page.tsx` now fetches the whole board (`.limit(3000)`, current index 1,833) so filters see everything; the client filters/sorts over the full set and renders a bounded `RENDER_CAP = 300` slice, keeping the DOM the same size as before. The scope note is now match-aware: *"Showing 300 of 935 matching editions (highest FMV first). Filters and the totals above run across all 1,833 indexed editions."* — so the user is told both what matched and what is rendered. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Verified before shipping:** sorting passes in all three states (default FMV desc monotonic; Mint click → desc 259/259/124/124; second click → asc 1/1/1/1), search "Messi" → 20 rows all matching and clears back cleanly, and each mint-cap band returns only rows satisfying it. `tsc --noEmit` clean, 5/5 route tests green.
- **Same root cause as the KPI bug earlier today** (`initialRows` treated as the set when it is a slice) — that one hit the headline numbers, this one hit the filters. Both were invisible to typecheck and tests because the code did exactly what it said; both required driving the actual UI. Worth carrying as a pattern: **any client-side filter over a server-truncated fetch is a silent-truncation bug waiting to happen.**

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — QA of the Panini board: sorting verified; 37% of rows are zero-sale and the #1 row is an ASK-derived $517,500 Messi. Measured, NOT patched (pricing logic = handoff).

Interactive QA of the squeeze board found one clean pass and one honesty consideration that belongs in front of Trevor before go-live.

- **PASS — sorting works in all three states.** Default FMV-descending is monotonic; clicking `Mint` sorts descending (259, 259, 124, 124…) and clicking again ascending (1, 1, 1, 1…). Headers, row count (300) and the KPI/table split all behave. No client exceptions.
- **FINDING — the board's headline row is an ASK-derived valuation of a card that has never sold.** Top row: **Lionel Messi, Base Prizms Black /1, FMV $517,500, ask $575,000, `real_sales` 0** — and FMV is exactly **0.90 x ask**. Same shape down the top of the board (Vozinha $22,500 = 0.90 x $25,000; Estevao $13,500 = 0.90 x $15,000). Of the **top 50 rows by FMV, 34 have zero recorded sales**; of the 300-row page slice, 136 do.
- **MECHANISM (deliberate, not a bug).** `lib/chains/panini/ingest-normalize.ts:50-58` `toFmvRow`: if `volume_txns > 0` use `avg_sale`/`recent_sale` with confidence HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW by txn count; **else** `fmv = round(floor_price * 0.9)` with confidence **`ASK_ONLY`**. That mirrors RPC's own Top Shot cold-tail convention (ASK_ONLY = low_ask x 0.90), so the pipeline is behaving as designed and is labelling honestly. Live confidence split: **HIGH 1,374 · ASK_ONLY 206 · LOW 130 · MEDIUM 123**.
- **SCALE.** 1,833 board rows; **686 (37.4%) have zero recorded sales**; 205 of those match the 0.90-x-ask signature. **$336,358 of the $938,170 "Value sealed in packs" KPI (36%) derives from zero-sale rows.** Mitigating: the board renders the **ASK column beside FMV**, so a reader can see the valuation is ask-anchored.
- **I OVER-CLAIMED FIRST AND AM CORRECTING IT.** My initial read was "disconnected/troll asks, like the Top Shot class that needed a clamp". Tested against family medians, that does NOT hold: ASK_ONLY does skew higher (avg **17.4x** family median vs **5.3x** for HIGH) but **HIGH-confidence rows carry extreme outliers too — 89 over 10x, 43 over 25x, worst 1,429x**. Within a parallel family, legitimate star-player dispersion (Messi vs a squad player) is enormous, so a family-median test cannot separate a troll ask from a real Messi premium. **There is no evidence of a troll-ask problem; only of ask-anchored valuation on never-sold cards, which is the documented design.**
- **NOT PATCHED, deliberately.** CLAUDE.md's FMV rule is explicit: data fixes are fine, **pricing LOGIC edits get handed off**. Changing the ASK_ONLY basis, adding a Panini disconnected-ask clamp (Top Shot has one, Panini does not), or excluding zero-sale rows from the board are all pricing/product calls, not QA cleanups. Recorded for Trevor's go-live decision instead.
- **The go-live question this raises:** is an ask-anchored FMV acceptable on a public board when 37% of rows have never sold and the most prominent number is a $517,500 valuation with zero sales behind it? Options if not: render zero-sale rows without an FMV, default-sort by a sales-backed measure, or exclude ASK_ONLY from the "Value sealed" KPI. All product decisions.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — THIRD clobber, and it walked straight through my own guard: count checks miss a swap. Guard rewritten to compare heading SETS.

- **INCIDENT — commit `2966c0a` destroyed an entry while the ledger-guard passed.** It removed *"Panini Item 1 RESOLVED (no catalog exists — 2b is the path) + coverage-disclosure data; Candy best-offer expiry guard"* and added its own, so the heading count went **356 → 356**. My guard only asserted the count had not DECREASED, so a one-for-one swap sailed through green. The lost entry carried the **only recorded revert paths for two live prod views** (`audit_20260719_panini_coverage_summary_view` and `audit_20260719_candy_best_offers_expiry_guard`) — caught only because I spot-checked that every migration shipped today still had a ledger reference, and two came back `0`.
- **THE LESSON, stated plainly: a count invariant is necessary but not sufficient.** I shipped that guard specifically to stop this class of loss and then watched it wave the loss through. Any check on an append-only log must compare **identity**, not cardinality.
- **SHIPPED (CI) — guard rewritten to a set comparison.** It now extracts `^### ` headings from `HEAD~1` and `HEAD`, sorts both, and fails if `comm -23` finds ANY heading that existed before and is gone now — reporting the exact missing headings in the error. The count check is retained as a secondary signal. `[ledger-roll]` opt-out preserved for the biweekly archival roll. **Validated against real history before shipping: FAILS `2966c0a`** (356→356, lost 1 — the exact case the old guard missed), still FAILS `fecda2e` (353→340, lost 14), and PASSES clean appends `ac670d4` (355→356), `5895f0f` (375→376) and `217b399` (377→377, count unchanged but nothing lost — correctly distinguishing a reorder from a deletion). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **RESTORED** the lost entry by splicing it back from `ac670d4`, preserving `2966c0a`'s own new entry. Verified 0 duplicate headings afterwards.
- **Tally for the day: 3 clobbers** (`fecda2e` 14 entries, `2966c0a` 1 entry, plus one I wrongly attributed to `eb5d7f6` and retracted). All restored. The behavioural rule (re-read from disk, splice, never write back a stale copy) is in CLAUDE.md; the mechanical enforcement is now actually capable of catching what it was built for.

Consistent with the op's own name and with 100% of discovered 1-of-1s being currently listed. **=> handoff branch 2b.** Residual uncertainty is small but non-zero (a checklist could hide behind an unlabelled control rather than a route), so the shipped capture instrumentation (`PANINI_DISCOVERY_HOLD_MIN` / `PANINI_DISCOVERY_ONLY`) makes the 10-minute operator session **confirmatory, not deciding**. Handoff Item 1 rewritten accordingly.

Live values: **1,647 total · 768 trustworthy (46.6%) · 102 listing-gated across 12 of 54 families · refresh 3.8-29.9h.** It self-measures, so the disclosure can never go stale and nothing is hardcoded; suggested copy is in the handoff. `security_invoker=on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role` (the public JSON route reads via service role, same as the squeeze board). **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_coverage_summary;`
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_candy_best_offers_expiry_guard`.** Reviewing Claude Code's offers pipeline end-to-end: the deactivation logic is genuinely well-guarded (sweep-based deactivation runs only when `bidderFetchErrors === 0 && !biddersTruncated`, so a partial fetch can never mark standing offers dead; expiry-based deactivation runs unconditionally, which is right; and it soft-sets `is_active=false` rather than deleting, so nothing is destroyed). **But `candy_best_offers` filtered only on `is_active`, not on `expiry`** — and expired rows are only flipped off when the 6-hourly sweep runs, so between ticks an already-expired bid could still set `best_offer_sol` for up to 6h. ### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — BUG found by rendering the page: every Panini KPI was a top-300 slice presented as a set-level total (Sealed copies off by 30x). Fixed.

Rendering the squeeze board (rather than trusting tsc + tests) surfaced a real user-visible defect on the surface that is one line from going public.

- **THE BUG.** All four KPIs were computed client-side from `initialRows`, the server page's `.limit(300)` slice — so they described the page while reading as set-level headlines. Worst, the KPI row said **"EDITIONS 300"** directly beneath a coverage banner saying **"RPC indexes 1,842 editions"** — a flat contradiction on the same screen. Displayed vs truth: **Editions 300 vs 1,833 (-84%) · Value sealed $703,804 vs $938,170 (-25%) · Chases ≤/25 271 vs 935 (-71%) · Sealed copies 742 vs 22,575 (-97%, off by ~30x)**. Sealed copies is the extreme case for a structural reason: top-300-BY-FMV are scarce low-print cards, while nearly all sealed volume sits in high-print commons that never make that cut — ordering by FMV maximally anti-correlates with what that KPI measures.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_squeeze_totals_view`: `public.panini_squeeze_totals`.** One row, whole-board: `editions`, `sealed_fmv_exposure_usd`, `chases_lte_25`, `sealed_copies`, using the same `fmv_usd IS NOT NULL` predicate as the page/API so figures are directly comparable to the rows beneath them. `security_invoker=on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role`. **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_squeeze_totals;`
- **SHIPPED (code) — KPIs now read whole-board totals, fail-soft.** `page.tsx` fetches totals in the same `Promise.all` as rows + coverage; the client prefers `totals?.x` and falls back to the slice-derived values on error, so a totals failure degrades to the old behaviour rather than blanking the KPIs. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **ALSO FIXED — the asymmetry the fix introduced.** With whole-board KPIs, a reader sees "Editions 1,833" above a 300-row table and reasonably assumes the table is the whole set. Added a scope note beneath it: *"Showing the top 300 editions by FMV. The totals above cover all 1,833 indexed editions."* Rendered only when totals exceed displayed rows; brand tokens only.
- **Standing lesson, restated because it paid out twice in one session:** `tsc --noEmit` + green tests proved the code *compiles and behaves as written* — they could never catch this, because the code did exactly what it said. Only rendering the DOM exposed a headline wrong by 30x. Read CLAUDE.md's "verify by rendered DOM, not HTTP 200" as "not HTTP 200 **and not a green test suite** either".

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — SELF-AUDIT of the Panini disclosure: my own headline number was misreadable and its denominator was a lower bound. Fixed to a range + caveat.

Audited the coverage disclosure I shipped earlier today, because it puts a number I invented onto a public-bound surface. The bucketing survived; the headline did not.

- **VALIDATED — the `coverage_flag` thresholds are sound.** They are my own heuristic (`pct_pulled_listed` >= 90 / 25 / 10), so I tested them against an INDEPENDENT measure, `pct_of_base_checklist` (discovered ÷ checklist players). They order **perfectly, with no overlap**: `broad` = 64.5 / 47.2 / 46.2% of checklist · `partial` = 36.8 · `heavily_biased` = 26.3 / 18.9 / 15.6 / 14.4 / 12.9 · `listing_gated` = 9.4 / 8.6. So the listed-fraction proxy really does track true completeness, and the buckets are trustworthy.
- **DEFECT 1 (fixed) — the headline was MISREADABLE.** The banner led with `pct_trustworthy` ("46.7% of indexed editions"). That is a **composition** statistic — the share of editions sitting in well-covered families — **not a coverage percentage**. A reader will take "46.7%" to mean "RPC has 46.7% of the set", which is wrong in BOTH directions: real per-parallel coverage runs ~**65%** (Base Prizms Red) down to ~**9%** (the 1-of-1 parallels). Publishing one ambiguous number in place of the true range is the kind of thing the disclosure exists to prevent.
- **DEFECT 2 (fixed) — the denominator is a LOWER BOUND, and it moved under me.** The "checklist" is itself discovered data (distinct players across base families). It **grew 474 → 487** during the day, with **26-44 players first seen in the last 24h**. So the true checklist is at least as large as what we have seen, and **every percent-of-checklist figure is an upper bound on true coverage** — i.e. reality is somewhat worse than any number we can print. That has to be stated, not buried.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_coverage_summary_honest_range`.** Adds `best_family_checklist_pct`, `worst_family_checklist_pct`, `checklist_players_seen`, `checklist_players_new_24h` to `panini_coverage_summary`; existing columns untouched so page + API keep working. View COMMENT now warns that `pct_trustworthy` is a composition share and that the checklist count is a lower bound. **Revert:** recreate the prior view body from migration history.
- **SHIPPED (code) — disclosure rewritten to lead with the RANGE plus the caveat.** New copy: *"RPC indexes N editions of this set. Panini publishes no full checklist, so a card is indexed only once it has been listed for sale. Coverage per parallel runs from about 65% down to 9% — thinnest exactly where cards are scarcest (118 editions across 12 of 54 parallels are visible to us only while listed). We are also still finding players we had not seen (26 new in the last 24h), so our own checklist count is a lower bound and these figures are best-case. Treat this board as a floor, not a census."* Same treatment in the public JSON `note`, which now explicitly says `pct_trustworthy` is a COMPOSITION share and `checklist_players_seen` is a LOWER bound. Both paths still fail-soft.
- **SHIPPED (test) — anti-misreading guards pinned.** `__tests__/api-public-panini-squeeze.test.ts` now asserts the note matches `/COMPOSITION share/i` and `/LOWER bound/i` alongside the range fields, so a future edit cannot quietly strip the caveats and leave a bare percentage. 5/5 green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Trend note:** `pct_trustworthy` continued to slide during the audit — **46.6% → 46.4% → 45.6%** as the index grew 1,647 → 1,769 → 1,842. This is the third independent confirmation that waiting does not improve the quality ratio.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — the Candy bid book is INTERNALLY RATIONAL (prices scarcity ~8x); my own "suppress when distinct_bidders = 1" guard would have inverted the board — retracted

Analysed the first real `candy_offers` data (47 standing offers, 2 bidders, 24 editions) to test whether the captured signal carries information or is noise. It carries information — and the answer overturns a guard I proposed earlier this session.

- **The bid book prices scarcity correctly.** Broken out by tier: **LEGENDARY (Rainbow, circ 15)** — 5 editions with offers, avg best offer **$2.74** (range $1.52-$3.04), 7 offers total. **COMMON (base ICON, circ 250)** — 19 editions, avg best offer **$0.34** (range $0.23-$1.90), 40 offers. That is a **~8x premium for the 16.7x-scarcer tier**, rationally ordered. So while the book is thin and lowball in ABSOLUTE terms (2 wallets, all sub-$5), its RELATIVE ordering is meaningful — which is exactly the property that makes a "best offer" column informative even when the levels are low. It also means the sweep is resolving mints to the right editions (a mis-mapped gate would smear tiers together, not separate them cleanly).
- **RETRACTED — my "suppress the display when `distinct_bidders = 1`" suggestion is backwards and must not be implemented as stated.** The data: **LEGENDARY editions have `max_bidders` = 1; COMMON editions have 2.** The second wallet bids only on commons. So a per-edition `distinct_bidders >= 2` gate would **hide every scarce/chase row and show only the commons** — precisely inverting what a collector cares about, and making the board look like the cheap tier is the whole market. I proposed that guard before any data existed; the first real tick disproves it.
- **Better shape (for whenever Candy has a surface):** do not suppress on bidder count — **display it as context** ("best offer $2.74 · 1 bidder") and let the reader weigh it. If a suppression rule is wanted at all, apply it at the COLLECTION level (e.g. hide the whole column while the entire book is a single wallet), never per-edition, because per-edition bidder counts are correlated with scarcity and therefore with interest. Honesty constraint unchanged and reinforced: best-offer framing only, never FMV, never `fmv_snapshots`.
- **VERIFIED in production — the Panini coverage disclosure ships correctly in BOTH surfaces.** Rendered DOM at `/insights/panini-squeeze`: h1, 4 KPI cards, 300 table rows, no client exception, `.psq-cov` banner live. Public JSON `/api/public/insights/panini-squeeze?limit=3`: **HTTP 200 with `meta.coverage` present** — `total_editions` 1769, `pct_trustworthy` 46.4, `listing_gated_editions` 115, `families` 54, `basis: "listing_gated"`, and the note matching /floor, not a census/. Figures track the live view between reads, confirming nothing is hardcoded in either path.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — Panini coverage disclosure BUILT INTO the squeeze surface (page + API contract + test), so go-live can't ship a census claim by accident

Branch 2b requires that any public Panini surface disclose its own coverage. Making that a documented instruction is weak — someone un-gates the proxy line and the disclosure is forgotten. Built it into the surface instead, in both the render path and the response contract.

- **SHIPPED (code) — `app/insights/panini-squeeze/page.tsx` + `PaniniSqueezeClient.tsx`.** The server page now fetches `panini_coverage_summary` in parallel with the board (`Promise.all`) and passes it to the client, which renders a bordered disclosure directly under the subtitle: *"RPC indexes 1,647 editions of this set. Panini publishes no full checklist, so an edition is indexed once it has been listed for sale — coverage is strongest on high-print parallels (46.6% of indexed editions) and thinnest on the scarcest ones (102 editions across 12 of 54 parallels are visible to us only while listed). Treat this board as a floor, not a census."* All figures come from the self-measuring view, so the wording can never drift from reality. Brand tokens only (`--rpc-red`, `--rpc-surface`, `--rpc-border`, `--rpc-text-*`) per the no-hardcoded-literals rule. The `coverage` prop is optional and defaults to null, and the fetch is fail-soft (logs + returns null), so a coverage error degrades to "no banner" and can never take the board down.
- **SHIPPED (code) — `app/api/public/insights/panini-squeeze/route.ts` now carries `meta.coverage`.** Same figures plus `basis: "listing_gated"` and an explicit `note` ending "Treat as a floor, not a census." Also fail-soft: a coverage-query error logs and nulls the block; the board rows are the primary payload and still serve 200.
- **SHIPPED (test) — `__tests__/api-public-panini-squeeze.test.ts`, 5 tests, all green.** The route had NO test before, so this both pins the new contract and keeps the coverage ratchet honest (net-new covered lines rather than net-new uncovered ones). Cause is the documented concurrent-session hazard: a session reads the ledger, works for a long stretch, then writes its whole in-memory version back, so everything committed in the interim vanishes. **Not a Cowork-vs-Claude-Code thing — the losses spanned both**, and the single most costly casualty was Claude Code's OWN `Candy best-offer capture SHIPPED (candy_offers + candy-offers-indexer)` entry, which carries the revert path for a live prod migration. Validated against real history before shipping: FAILs on `fecda2e` (353→340), PASSes on clean appends (`19aae22` 340→341, `53100f6` 352→353, the restore 340→355), SKIPs commits that don't touch the ledger. Behavioural rule stands too: the ledger is APPEND-AT-TOP and must be re-read from disk immediately before writing. Never write back a whole copy you read earlier in the session. Splice your entry into the freshly-read file, then sanity-check `grep -c '^### ' docs/overnight/ledger.md` went UP by exactly the number of entries you added — if it went DOWN, you just destroyed someone's revert path. A rejected `git push` is the tell that someone else landed work; re-read after every pull, never rebase a whole-file rewrite.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — RPC Packs: delivery-to-Dapper claim MEASURED (n=235, was asserted-only); the ~20-pack ceiling is a rail artifact, not a market ceiling

Follow-on to the pricing-engine entry below. Docs-only — no code, no schema, no prod state change. Doc: [docs/strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md](../strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md) §5.2.

- **CLOSED (measurement) — "delivery to a Dapper-custodial account is permissionless" was asserted in 3 docs + the ledger and NEVER probed.** It is load-bearing (`BREAK_MULTI_TRANSFER_TS` panics an entire 30-recipient chunk if one recipient can't receive) and it was pure contract-shape reasoning. Now measured from RPC's own production data: `app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts:30-37` (the `wallet_moments_cache` writer) walks TS wallets via `getAccount(addr).capabilities.borrow<&{TopShot.MomentCollectionPublic}>(/public/MomentCollection)`, returning `[]` when the cap is absent — so **every wmc row is a successful public-capability borrow**. Live: of **244** TS wallets in wmc, **235 have never appeared in `linked_accounts` in any role** (no hybrid custody, no self-custody parent) and hold **1,558,636 moments**. Separately, 9 known Dapper-custodial *children* hold 50,162 moments while their self-custody parents hold **0** — moments live in the custodial account, as the model predicts. **The public collection capability demonstrably exists on ordinary never-linked Top Shot accounts at n=235.**
- **RESIDUAL INFERENCE (named, not papered over):** the walk borrows `TopShot.MomentCollectionPublic`; the delivery paths borrow `NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic` (`break-transactions.ts:34,63`) and `NonFungibleToken.Receiver` (`gift.ts:77`). Same published cap **iff** it is published as concrete `&TopShot.Collection` — which `docs/audits/purchase-moment-2026-05.md:203` recorded from a live Cadence MCP read — since a concrete-type cap is borrowable as any conforming interface. Standard Cadence semantics, high confidence, but reasoning not measurement. `/api/wallet-preflight` borrows exactly `NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic` and would close it in one GET, but it is **not** on the `proxy.ts` public allowlist and auth config was deliberately NOT modified to reach it (off-limits class).
- **QUEUED (OPERATOR, ~2 min, Trevor) — one low-value gift on mainnet closes the last inch.** `moment_gifts` has **0 rows**: the live `/dashboard/gift` parent-signed flow has never executed end-to-end. Sending one common moment to a Dapper-custodial recipient converts the residual inference into a measurement AND smoke-tests a shipped-but-unexercised feature. Highest value-per-minute item in the RPC Packs workstream.
- **STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE — the ~20-packs-per-drop ceiling is a RAIL artifact, not a market ceiling.** Vaultopolis's buyers must sign a FLOW Storefront purchase (needs a FLOW-funded FCL wallet), which is the most likely cause of drop 7 selling 8 of 40. Delivery is a *separate* leg and is unwalled. So **selling for credits/Stripe (off-chain) + delivering on-chain removes the buyer-side FLOW/self-custody requirement entirely** — buyer needs no FLOW, no FCL wallet, no signature, just a TS account that can receive. Addressable pool goes from the ~108 linked wallets to ~every TS account (RPC alone indexes **4,031 active buyers/90d**). This points the same direction as the legal analysis: **transparent lots + off-chain payment + on-chain delivery is simultaneously the legal-clean shape and the large-market shape**; the sealed FLOW-priced pack is both the risky one and the small one.
- **Recommendation updated (§7.1 next steps, ordered):** (1) operator gift probe; (2) generalize the scorer into an arbitrary-moment-set lot pricer; (3) only then inventory/cost-basis + `shop_items` lot listing, re-funding payer wallet `0x73f55c4450b8d466` first; (4) do NOT start `RPCPacks`/commit-reveal/multi-chain.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (docs-only).

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — CORRECTION: `panini_editions.updated_at` is inert; my own coverage view was reading it. Fixed + trigger added

Self-correction. While verifying a claim I had put in the handoff ("coverage accumulates on its own"), I found the freshness column I had been measuring is not a freshness column at all — and that my own `panini_coverage_audit` view, shipped hours earlier, was reading it.

- **THE TRAP:** `public.panini_editions.updated_at` has `DEFAULT now()` and **NO trigger**, and `lib/chains/panini/ingest-normalize.ts` sets `last_seen_at` (not `updated_at`) on edition rows. So `updated_at` is written once at INSERT and never again. Verified live: `created_at = updated_at` on **1647/1647** rows, max gap **0.00h**. Anything reading it as freshness is reading INSERT AGE. The real per-row freshness column is **`last_seen_at`** (1,383 rows carry `last_seen_at > created_at`, max gap 29.5h).
- **WHAT I GOT WRONG (corrected):** the MED item below states "only 848 of 1,647 editions were refreshed in the last 24h ... the 4h runner is not completing a full sweep." That 848 is the count of editions **first INSERTED** in 24h. The true re-observation figure is **1,285 / 1,647 = 78% in 24h** (1,062 = 64% within 8h). The concern is real but much smaller than stated: there IS a stale tail out to **61.4h**, so the sweep is not complete, but daily coverage is 78% not 51%. Treat the MED item as re-scoped to "close the ~22% / 61h tail", not "the runner is missing half the catalog".
- **WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED:** the listing-GATED finding is independent of this bug and stands exactly as recorded — `coverage_flag` buckets re-verified post-fix at `listing_gated 12 / heavily_biased 17 / partial 16 / broad 10`, identical to before. The 100%-of-1-of-1s-are-listed proof does not involve either timestamp column.
- **ALSO NOW VERIFIED (was previously an assumption):** `created_at` IS a genuine first-seen stamp precisely BECAUSE it is never updated, so discovery drift IS measurable after all. Retention is real: 13 zero-listing editions persist, and rows sit unrefreshed up to 61h without being dropped. The handoff line claiming monotonic accumulation has been updated from assertion to verified fact.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_freshness_column_fix`.** (a) `trg_panini_editions_touch_updated_at` (BEFORE UPDATE, sets `updated_at = now()`) so the column means what its name says from here on and stops being a trap for the next reader — this matches every other table's convention. (b) Recreated `panini_coverage_audit` against `last_seen_at`, and added two explicit columns so the distinction can never be silently conflated again: **`refreshed_24h`** (re-observed) and **`first_seen_24h`** (newly discovered). Post-fix totals: refreshed_24h **1,285**, first_seen_24h **848** — the two numbers I had collapsed into one. `security_invoker=on`, grants unchanged (authenticated + service_role), `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]`. **Revert:** `DROP TRIGGER trg_panini_editions_touch_updated_at ON public.panini_editions; DROP FUNCTION public.panini_editions_touch_updated_at();` + recreate the prior view body from migration history.
- **BLAST RADIUS: exactly one object — my own view. Swept, nothing else affected.** Of the 7 views over `panini_editions` (`panini_squeeze_board`, `panini_coverage_audit`, `panini_pack_ev_model`, `panini_nation_board`, `panini_special_serials_board`, `panini_deal_board`, `panini_player_board`), **none** reference `updated_at` except the coverage view, now fixed (`pg_get_viewdef` sweep). Repo grep: the only hit is `docs/drafts/panini/panini-schema.sql`, a draft doc with no live consumer. **The daily `panini-freshness-check` scheduled task already reads `last_seen_at` correctly** — I flagged it as suspect in the first draft of this entry and that was wrong; retracted. Its own stated baseline ("a healthy full walk refreshes roughly 900-1,300 editions") in fact matches the corrected 1,285 figure, which is independent confirmation that 848 was the anomalous reading and not the truth.

Field 2 has 54 distinct values (= the 54 set names), field 4 has 474 (= the checklist players). Anyone parsing pskus off the old comment will mis-attribute every card.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — Panini: discovery is listing-GATED, not merely listing-biased — quantified + measurement view shipped; board surfacing deliberately NOT done

Investigating what Panini still needs before go-live. The runner is healthy (data 1.1h fresh, 375 `panini-ingest` runs/7d, 1,647 editions / 2,542 FMV rows / 7,105 serials). The blocker is not freshness or plumbing — it is **catalog completeness**, and it is worse and more structural than the standing "index is ~20% of the set and listing-biased" note.

- **FINDING (measured, launch-relevant) — discovery is strictly gated on being LISTED, and the bias is monotonic in scarcity.** The runner discovers editions by walking the marketplace grid, so an edition enters `panini_editions` only once it has been listed. Against the 474-player base checklist, discovery falls cleanly with scarcity: Red (avg cap 124) **64%** -> Silver (259) 45% -> Blue (49) 44% -> Cracked Ice (25) 33% -> Gold (10) **24%** -> Old Glory (7) 11% -> Black (cap 1) **8%** -> Nebula (cap 1) **7%**. The decisive tell: for the two 1-of-1 parallels (Black, Nebula) **100% of discovered copies are currently listed** (40/40 and 33/33). That is impossible for an unbiased sample of a real 1-of-1 population — it proves we can only ever see a 1-of-1 while its single copy happens to be for sale. Bucketed across all 55 families: **`listing_gated` 12 families / 102 editions (100% listed, avg cap 1), `heavily_biased` 17 / 459 (26–52%), `partial` 16 / 318 (10–24%), `broad` 10 / 768 (4–9%)** — i.e. only **768 of 1,647 editions (47%) sit in a trustworthy-coverage bucket**, and coverage is thinnest exactly where scarcity is highest.
- **Product consequence for `/insights/panini-squeeze`:** per-row numbers are HONEST — `rip_pct`, `still_in_packs`, `mint_cap` are true API supply stats for any discovered edition, so nothing displayed is wrong. The defect is **completeness**: the board is a leaderboard over a listing-gated sample, so it cannot support the implicit claim "these are THE squeezed cards", only "these are squeezed cards among those we happen to have indexed". The scarce tail — the most interesting squeeze candidates — is 7–24% present. Un-gating as-is would ship a board that is quietly least complete precisely where it is most interesting.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_coverage_audit_view`: `public.panini_coverage_audit`.** Per (set_name, parallel_family): discovered_editions, avg_mint_cap, pulled, listed_now, `pct_pulled_listed` (the diagnostic — as it approaches 100 the family is visible to us ONLY through live listings), `pct_of_base_checklist`, a `coverage_flag` (broad / partial / heavily_biased / listing_gated), and refresh-age min/max. This is the measurement instrument for the gap: it lets the surface disclose real coverage instead of implying completeness, and lets a full-catalog walk be prioritized worst-family-first. `security_invoker = on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role` (ops/diagnostic, deliberately NOT anon). **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_coverage_audit;`
- **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE — surfacing the 5 built-but-unsurfaced Panini boards.** Six views carry real data but only `panini_squeeze_board` has a route: `panini_deal_board` (136 rows), `panini_player_board` (552), `panini_nation_board` (71), `panini_special_serials_board` (1,012), `panini_pack_ev_board` (2), `panini_pack_ev_model` (1). Building pages for them looked like the obvious parity win, and it is the wrong next move: every one of them reads the SAME listing-gated index, so surfacing them now would **multiply one completeness defect across five more public boards** — and `panini_special_serials_board` is the worst case, since special serials live disproportionately in the scarce tail that is 7–24% covered. Fix coverage first, then surface; the views are ready and the squeeze page is the template, so the surfacing work is cheap once the index is trustworthy.
- **QUEUED (Panini, HIGH — the real go-live blocker):** full-catalog walk to replace listing-gated discovery. The runner already auto-enumerates pskus from the grid; the fix is to walk the CHECKLIST (all players x all parallel families) rather than the listings grid, so an edition is discovered whether or not it is currently for sale. Prioritize by `panini_coverage_audit` ascending `coverage_flag`. Until then, any public Panini surface should render an explicit coverage disclosure (same honesty stance as the 07-18 Sold-tab lower-bound note).
- **QUEUED (Panini, MED) — refresh cycle does not cover the catalog daily.** Only 848 of 1,647 editions were refreshed in the last 24h and the oldest rows are ~59h stale, so the 4h runner is not completing a full sweep between runs. Walk order was already shuffled (`0736fbc4`) so stalled runs rotate coverage; the residual is throughput, not ordering.
