Trevor asked what it would take to launch RPC Packs (RPC re-packs real moments, users open them on RPC), ideally multi-collection and eventually multi-chain. The June spec ([docs/strategy/repack-drops-feature-scope-2026-06-19.md](../strategy/repack-drops-feature-scope-2026-06-19.md)) already reverse-engineered the Vaultopolis contract and specced `RPCPacks`; this addendum covers only what it doesn't. **Docs-only — no code, no schema, no prod state change.**

- **SHIPPED (docs) — [docs/strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md](../strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md).** Covers: (1) month deltas — the base doc's one measured weakness (parallel FMV undervaluing the chase) is **CLOSED**, live 3,597 `::` parallels cataloged / 3,574 priced in 7d = 99.4%; pack-EV gained the pool-completeness guard + Actual-vs-Typical (mean-vs-median = the honest-pricing edge); TAM re-measured (linked wallets ~66 → **108 children / 114 parents / 117 links**, wmc 261 → 296, TS buyers 90d 3,655 → 4,031) — binding constraint unchanged, the pack market is the self-custody+FLOW slice ≈100–300 wallets. (2) **Multi-collection** — contract side is EASY and `RPCTradeEscrow` is the wrong reference (it commits one `Type` per side at `:135-136`, a design choice not a Cadence limit; a `Pack` escrowing `@[{NonFungibleToken.NFT}]` is heterogeneous natively). Real costs are the **per-collection receiver** (init-on-open, else partial-open failures) and **FMV comparability** (TS ~3,349 + AllDay ~826 H+M are honestly priceable; Golazos 4 / UFC 15 are not; Pinnacle is a separate render-keyed grain). (3) **Multi-chain** — no honest single-pack-across-chains without a bridge or custodial IOU; recommend per-chain packs with a unified UI; every write path today is Flow/Cadence (Solana is read-only DAS), so it's a second write stack + treasury + key surface + audit, i.e. a separate program. (4) **Legal, sharpened** — NY AG sued Valve Feb 2026 on a gambling theory whose hinge is **transferability**, the maximal case for NFT packs; the RPC-specific aggravator is that **RPC publishes FMV**, i.e. RPC's own appraisal engine is evidence for the "prize has real-world value" prong that's normally contested; also contradicts the deliberate NO-chance rule already set for the rewards program. Reframe offered: **transparent lots** (exact contents + FMV + price) delete the chance prong entirely and are more on-brand than sealed randomized packs.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — All Day lock freshness was UNKNOWABLE: `allday-lock-refresh` wrote `is_locked` without ever stamping `lock_checked_at`

Found while auditing the lock pipeline per-collection. Small, bounded, and it unblocks the queued WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS work.

- **THE ANOMALY.** Per-collection wmc lock state: `nfl_all_day` has **333,115 rows, 3,682 flagged `is_locked`, and 0 rows with any `lock_checked_at`** (`max(lock_checked_at)` NULL). Top Shot 179,750/1,608,798 checked, Pinnacle 44,350/44,368 (99.96%) — both stamped and current.
- **NOT phantom data — a missing timestamp.** `app/api/allday-lock-refresh/route.ts` legitimately recomputes All Day locks by diffing the on-chain unlocked-id set against wmc, so the 3,682 values are real. But it wrote **only** `is_locked` and never `lock_checked_at`. Consequences: (a) All Day lock freshness is unknowable, and since locks EXPIRE a stale `true` is a lie the UI cannot detect; (b) any staleness-based display-honesty fix would treat All Day as "never checked" and be unable to distinguish real-but-undated data from genuinely-missing data; (c) `lock-check-batch` reports All Day under `unsupported_collections` every run, implying nothing maintains its locks, when this route does.
- **SHIPPED (code).** Stamp `lock_checked_at` alongside both `is_locked` writes, **plus a third pass over every examined row**. That third pass is the load-bearing part: the two existing loops only touch rows whose lock state FLIPPED, so in the steady state (nothing changed) no row would ever be stamped and freshness would never advance — which is precisely the failure being fixed. The third pass writes only the timestamp, never `is_locked`: it asserts "verified at", not a value.
- **Test-safe (checked, not assumed):** `__tests__/api-allday-lock-refresh.test.ts` uses a chainable Supabase stub (`update: () => sb`) and asserts only on response-body counts (`total_cached`, `marked_locked`, `marked_unlocked`) — none of which changed. The added loop just calls the stub once more. Verified by reading the test; vitest cannot run from the Cowork sandbox (Windows-native `node_modules`), so **CI is the gate** — this is the same class as the 07-18 wave that left CI red 24h, and the new `ci-status` monitor job now watches for exactly that.
- **REVERT:** `git revert <sha>` (single route file, no schema change — `lock_checked_at` already existed).
- **⚠ CORRECTION (same session, ~1h later) — the fix is INERT and the All Day picture is WORSE than written above.** I claimed "`lock-check-batch` reports All Day as unsupported … when in fact this route does [maintain its locks]". **It does not.** `/api/allday-lock-refresh` has **ZERO rows in `pipeline_runs`** — the only lock pipeline that runs at all is `lock-check-batch` (153 runs, newest 2026-07-19 05:08). Nothing schedules the All Day route: not cron-job.org (no pipeline_runs telemetry would exist if it fired), not vercel.json, not GHA, not pg_cron. So the 3,682 All Day `is_locked` flags are **undated AND unmaintained** — frozen at whatever past manual invocation set them, with no refresh path. **My stamping fix is correct but dormant: it changes nothing until something calls the route.** Making All Day locks trustworthy therefore needs a scheduling decision (add a cron + a watchlist row, mirroring `lock-check-batch`) or an explicit decision to stop displaying All Day locks at all. Folded into WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS. This is the same enumerate-the-callers failure the 07-18 seed-wallet gate produced — I should have checked `pipeline_runs` for the route before asserting it was live.

  | era | mkt acquisitions | sale row in ±2d | any sale row ever | coverage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | pre-2026 | 6,733 | 1,217 | 1,851 | **18–27%** |
  | 2026 | 539 | 329 | 400 | **61–74%** |

- **CONCLUSION — the gap is REAL but neither figure was right.** Not ~8% (that was the ungated-withdrawals framing) and not ~0%. Historical sale ingest captured roughly a quarter of known marketplace purchases; current ingest captures two-thirds to three-quarters. The reference wallet reads worst-case (~8%) because its sales span 2024-03 → 2026-05, i.e. mostly the under-ingested era.
- **Corroborating shape:** TS sales/quarter run 104k–248k across 2023–2025 but **309k / 311k in 2026 Q1/Q2**, with 2026 Q3 tracking current daily volume (62,125 over 19 days ≈ 3,270/day). The market did not double in 2026 — the live indexer got complete while history stayed partial. Some of that is date drift on backfilled rows rather than true absence, so ~27% is the fairer historical coverage figure and any gap-filling job must dedup on `(tx_hash, nft_id)` rather than on date proximity or it will double-insert.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — WMC-LOCK-CHECK-COVERAGE re-diagnosed: it is a FRESHNESS failure that OVERSTATES locks, not a coverage gap that understates them

Investigated Trevor's "lock number doesn't seem accurate". The earlier framing (88.9% of TS wmc rows never lock-checked ⇒ "systematic lower bound") is **directionally wrong for real users**, and the fix it implies would be the wrong fix.

- **The 88.9% is real but concentrated in whales, not spread across users.** TS wmc has only **244 distinct wallets**, and **240 of them (98.4%) have been lock-checked**. The 1,430,158 unchecked ROWS sit in a handful of mega-wallets — the top 5 hold **357,150** of them (largest: 146,097 unchecked of 149,506 rows). So "88.9% unchecked" describes wallets nobody views; it does not describe a typical user's board.
- **The real defect is FRESHNESS, and it inverts the sign.** Reference wallet (`0xbd94…50ac`, 14,945 rows): **95.2% checked** — coverage is fine — but newest check **2026-07-12**, oldest 2026-04-13, and **14,203 rows last verified >30 days ago**. Of its 13,207 rows flagged `is_locked`, **13,183 were last verified >30d ago** and only **0** within 24h. **Top Shot locks EXPIRE**, so a months-old `is_locked=true` is very likely already released ⇒ the UI **OVERSTATES** locks for exactly the wallets users actually look at. An "understating" fix (chase raw coverage) would make this worse by spending scarce budget on whale rows instead of refreshing viewed ones.
- **The freshness promise is ~70× oversubscribed.** `app/api/cron/lock-check-batch/route.ts` declares `MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7` with `BATCH_LIMIT = 200`, scheduled every 30 min (48 runs/day ⇒ 9,600 rows/day ceiling). Honouring a 7-day refresh over 1.6M TS rows needs **~229,000 rows/day**. Measured actual: **22,985 rows in 7 days ≈ 3,283/day**, i.e. a full pass takes **~435 days** against a 7-day target. The route also burns batch slots on collections it cannot check (`unsupported_collections: {nfl_all_day: 200, laliga_golazos: 44}` every run — AllDay/Golazos/UFC have no on-chain lock primitive).
- **Implication for the fix (do NOT just raise throughput).** The Cadence leg is the bound, so 70× is not reachable by tuning. The correct shapes are (a) **scope the promise to what's viewable** — prioritise seeded/saved/verified wallets and refresh them on a real 7-day cycle (244 wallets, and the non-whale ones are small), letting whale rows go deliberately stale; (b) **stop pulling unsupported collections** into the batch entirely; (c) **display honesty** — surface "locks as of <date>" (or suppress the lock figure past a staleness threshold) so a months-old snapshot never reads as current; (d) optionally **on-demand re-check** when a user opens their own wallet view.
- **NOT shipped** — this changes what the fix should be, and the route is an ingest-adjacent hot path that was itself rewritten 2026-07-16 (`get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite). Wants a deliberate owner session with the above shape, not a throughput bump. **Queued as WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS (supersedes WMC-LOCK-CHECK-COVERAGE).**

FROM PUBLIC` did NOT strip Supabase's default **anon/authenticated EXECUTE** grants on two SECDEF fns, one of which writes to `sales` — caught on post-flight grant check, fixed by explicit per-role REVOKE (grants now postgres + service_role only). This is the documented SECDEF anon-grant regression; `REVOKE FROM PUBLIC` is not sufficient. (2) the cursor was set unconditionally to the batch min, so replaying a newer batch **rewound the watermark** and would re-walk covered ground — caught by the idempotency test, fixed with `LEAST(...)`.

Nothing broke; the safety net did.
- **ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS (process, worth keeping).** I reasoned about the gate against the 4 cron-job.org cohort entries and never grepped for **other callers of the route**. One `grep -rn "seed-wallet-refresh" --include=*.yml` would have surfaced it before the push. **Rule: before gating/short-circuiting any route, enumerate every caller — cron-job.org, GHA workflows, vercel.json, pg_cron, in-repo fetches — not just the one you had in mind.**
- **SHIPPED — `?force=1` bypass.** The route now honours `force=1|true` alongside the `SEED_WALLET_REFRESH_EVERY_WAVE` env hatch, and the backstop workflow URL gains `&force=1` with a LOAD-BEARING comment so a future reader can't drop it. Safe to expose as a query param: the route is already Bearer-auth-gated above the check.

The only true per-wallet skip is `LOW_PRIORITY_INTERVAL_HOURS` (24h) and it applies to low-priority rows only. Checked empirically instead: over 3 days the backstop hours produced **0 runs at 02/08/20 and 14 runs at 14 (~5/day)** vs ~1,213/day for the gated waves — the backstop only does real work when a primary cohort actually failed. **Bypass cost ≈ 5 runs/day. The cost lever is intact.**

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — Phase 3: `v_moments_needing_hydration` #3-disk-reader FIXED (237 MB → 1.5 MB/call, 4,326 ms → 165 ms) — and the standing "trigger-queue" premise DISPROVEN

The carried Phase 3 item (`V-MOMENTS-NEEDING-HYDRATION`, deferred since 07-17 as "structural fix only — trigger-maintained incremental queue"). Measured it properly first; the premise was wrong and the real fix was far smaller and safer.

- **PREMISE DISPROVEN — it was never a selectivity problem.** The standing note said "its seq-scan predicate matches ~89.6% of `moment_acquisitions`, so no index helps," implying only a trigger-maintained queue could work. The predicate figure is right (636,495 of 711,625 rows are `pack_pull`+`verified`) but it was not the cost driver. Proof: `SELECT * FROM v_moments_needing_hydration LIMIT 300` already ran in **431 ms / 12 MB** — Postgres pipelines the CTE and stops pulling once the limit is met. So the limited read was never the hog.
- **ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE — an optimizer fence, found in `pg_stat_statements`.** The real consumer is the `topshot-moments-hydrator` worker via PostgREST: `... WHERE collection_id=$1 **ORDER BY acquired_date DESC** LIMIT 300 OFFSET $3` — **300 calls, 70 GB total, 237 MB + 4,326 ms each**. The view body wrapped its candidates in `WITH cand AS MATERIALIZED (...)`. Under an outer `ORDER BY`, that fence forces all ~636k candidates to materialize and hash-anti-join a **full seq scan of `moments` (540k rows)** before the top-N sort, so the `LIMIT` can never short-circuit. The ordering, not the predicate, was the problem.
- **SHIPPED (index, concurrent) — `idx_ma_hydration_queue_desc`** on `moment_acquisitions (collection_id, acquired_date DESC) INCLUDE (nft_id, wallet, source_pack_rip_id) WHERE acquisition_method='pack_pull' AND acquisition_confidence='verified'`. 58 MB, built `CONCURRENTLY` via standalone `execute_sql` (never inside `apply_migration` — that wraps in a txn). `INCLUDE` carries every column the anti-join and output need, so the candidate side is a true Index Only Scan. Sized against a measurement, not a guess: a `DESC` walk needs only **14,203 of 636,495 candidates (2.2%)** to collect 300 unhydrated, because the backlog reaches right up to the newest rows (newest unhydrated was 2 min old; oldest 2026-04-10). **REVERT:** `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY public.idx_ma_hydration_queue_desc;`
- **SHIPPED (view) — `audit_20260718_moments_needing_hydration_unfence_cte`.** Dropped the `AS MATERIALIZED` fence, rewriting the body as a direct `NOT EXISTS`. Removing a fence only ADDS plan choices — the planner still picks the hash anti-join for unlimited/count-shaped calls — so this cannot regress the other call shapes. **REVERT:** restore the prior `AS MATERIALIZED` body from migration history.
- **MEASURED, worker query shape, before → after:** execution **4,326 ms → 165 ms (~26×)**; disk blocks read **~29,000 → 186 (~1.5 MB, ~160×)**; candidate rows walked **636,571 → 14,102**; plan Hash Anti Join + full `moments` seq scan → **Nested Loop Anti Join with early stop** off the new index. At the observed ~300 calls/window that is ~70 GB → ~0.5 GB.
- **POST-FLIGHT ALL GREEN:** `view_rows_now` 172,017 == independent recompute 172,017 (parity exact; +5 vs pre-change = normal ingest drift); columns/order/types unchanged; grants preserved (**postgres + service_role only, anon NOT granted**); `reloptions` unchanged (null); `check_public_security_invariants()` []; `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` []; `tables_without_rls` 0; no invalid indexes DB-wide.
- **NOT DONE deliberately — no trigger, no queue table.** The trigger-maintained queue would have added write-path amplification to TWO active ingest tables (`moment_acquisitions` + `moments`) and new correctness surface, to solve a problem that turned out to be a one-line fence plus an index. **Recommend removing "build a trigger-maintained hydration queue" from the standing queue.**
- **RESIDUAL (optional, low):** the remaining 165 ms is dominated by `Heap Fetches: 14,012` on the `moments` index-only probe — stale visibility map on an actively-written table. A `VACUUM (ANALYZE) public.moments` would convert most of those to true index-only reads, but it is I/O on an IOPS-constrained instance; left for a deliberate quiet-window call, not bundled here.

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — Phase 2 cost lever: seed-wallet-refresh effective cadence 6h → 12h (in-route gate; ~56 lambda-hours/day)

Roadmap Phase 2's named "single highest-leverage lever." Measured it before pulling it.

- **MEASURED FIRST.** Over 7d the 7 `wallet-backfill*` pipelines burn **≈113 lambda-hours/day**: multicollection-complete 680 runs × 262s ≈ **49.4h**, wallet-backfill 645 × 92s ≈ 16.6h, allday 676 × 85s ≈ 16.0h, pinnacle 672 × 78s ≈ 14.6h, ufc 665 × 57s ≈ 10.6h, golazos 580 × 27s ≈ 4.4h, dispatch 680 × 6s ≈ 1.2h. Every one of those lambdas lands on the same 60-conn Supabase pool → it is simultaneously the #1 Vercel Fluid-memory driver AND the #1 DB-IOPS driver behind the recurring contention/statement-timeout class. The roadmap's claim is confirmed, not assumed.
- **SHIPPED (code) — 12h cadence gate in `/api/seed-wallet-refresh`.** Executes only the `utcHour % 12 < 2` waves (hours 0/1 and 12/13 — covers every cohort's slot without knowing which cohort calls) and no-ops the 6/7 and 18/19 waves in <1s with `{status:"skipped",reason:"12h_cadence_gate"}`. Cost of a skipped wave is freshness only (orchestrators are idempotent) — ~2× wallet-data staleness, strongly favourable at current traction (31 sessions/7d). Escape hatch `SEED_WALLET_REFRESH_EVERY_WAVE=1` disables the gate with no deploy.

### 2026-07-18 (Claude Code, interactive) — post-ship page fixes: logged-in Market fetch un-gated (P1) + AllDay thumb size (P2) + edition Activity contention-resilience (P3)

Follow-up to the edition-level Market ship below; all three are client-side page fixes from the `09`/post-ship handoff. Commit `12a9fab9`.

- **P1 (SEV-HIGH) — logged-in `/market` no longer strands on the loading skeleton.** The fetch effect hard-gated on `supabaseCollectionId`, which — unlike `collectionId` — has **no fallback** in `buildContext` (`collection?.supabaseCollectionId ?? null`). During the logged-in first-commit window (extra auth/profile/wallet fetches race `useParams()` resolution) it was momentarily null, so the page committed its filter UI but never issued `/api/market` (no error, logged-in only, intermittent — anon resolves params synchronously and never hits the window). Fix: derive `resolvedCollectionUuid = supabaseCollectionId ?? getCollectionUuid(collectionId)` (collectionId is always a valid published slug → always a non-null UUID) and gate/fetch on that. **Corrects the handoff's root-cause premise** — the stuck "Loading market…" is the outer Suspense fallback and the fetch was gated, not an async context race in the hook (the hook is a pure synchronous `useMemo`).
- **P2 — AllDay Market table thumbnails 32→52px** (Trevor-flagged "too small"). Grid-view card image was already full-size (`width:100%` aspect-1/1), untouched.
- **P3 — edition Activity section survives DB contention.** `EditionBottomSections` fetched via one `Promise.all` whose members only handled the supabase-js `{ error }` shape; a statement/gateway timeout that **rejects** the promise bypassed `if (error)`, rejected the whole `Promise.all`, and dropped the entire bottom section incl. the `<Section title="Activity">` heading → recurring `/nfl-all-day/edition/446` smoke false-fail during morning heavy-cron windows. Fix: per-fetch `.catch(() => <empty fallback>)` so each leg degrades to its titled empty-state and the section always renders.
- **Scope:** two client `.tsx` files only (`market/page.tsx`, `edition/[slug]/page.tsx`); tsc clean on both; market + edition route tests pass (the 6 full-suite failures are pre-existing 5s timeouts in worker-pack-events-ingest / ingest-backfill / pinnacle-sync, untouched here).

### 2026-07-18 (Claude Code, interactive) — P2 latency pass: get_insights_hub_stats single-scan rewrite SHIPPED (19.7s→5.7s); entity-detail premise DISPROVEN; moments-hydration deferred

Handoff `08` P2-latency. Measured each candidate before touching prod (IOPS-sensitive DB); shipped the one clean win, disproved one premise, deferred the structural one.

- **SHIPPED (DB migration) — `get_insights_hub_stats()` single-scan rewrite (`audit_20260718_insights_hub_stats_single_scan`).** The /insights cold-miss driver (~19.7s mean). Its market block ran FOUR separate scans of the `sales` `sold_at` window (24h count/sum + 7d count/sum), each ~5.4s over the `(collection_id, sold_at)` composite index (no collection_id predicate → full index scan). Since 24h ⊂ 7d, read the 7d window ONCE into a `MATERIALIZED` CTE and derive all four. Insights block byte-identical. **Measured 19.7s → 5.7s (~3.5×)**, parity confirmed (market numbers match within normal sales drift; insights block identical). No new index (IOPS-neutral). **REVERT:** restore the prior 4-scan body from migration history. Residual ~5s is the single 7d sales scan — a dedicated `(sold_at) WHERE price_usd>0` index would cut it further but adds write churn on the hot sales table (IOPS tradeoff) → left for the deliberate read-diet pass.
- **NO ACTION — entity-detail "60 GB / 5.3s" premise DISPROVEN (misattribution).** The actual top reader matching `p_slug` is `count_insider_detector_candidates(p_slug, p_detector)` — called by the **`run-insider-detectors` CRON**, NOT a user-facing entity page (and its rewrite is already disproven per [[insider-detector-rewrite-disproven]]; it carries a 60s timeout + per-collection split). The genuine entity-page detail RPCs are all healthy for cache-miss: `get_edition_market_bundle` 440ms, `get_edition_offers` 653ms, `get_edition_high_offer` 345ms, `get_moment_detail` 341ms, `get_edition_special_serials` 554ms, `get_pack_detail_bundle` 1.8s — none near 5s. So there is no entity-page query to optimize.
- **DEFERRED (unchanged) — `v_moments_needing_hydration`.** Structural fix only (trigger-maintained incremental queue); its seq-scan predicate matches ~89.6% of `moment_acquisitions` so no index helps. Explicitly a deliberate-owner-session item (07-17 ledger), not an autonomous ship.
- **NOTED read-diet candidate (deliberate pass, not shipped) — `backfill_wmc_metadata_from_editions`** (19.8 GB / 5.3s / 2,293 calls, background). Cadence-throttle candidate like the 07-17 read-diet levers, but needs measurement of its freshness necessity before throttling — not a blind ship.

Migrations `audit_20260718_split_weekly_db_maintenance` + `audit_20260718_prune_stale_wmc_statement_timeout_600s`. Ran both once live: log-purges ok=true (reclaimed 52 smoke rows); wmc-prune ok=true 7.1s / **0 rows** deleted.

### 2026-07-17 (Claude Code, interactive) — PERF/read-diet lever #1 SHIPPED (DB-only): throttled the #1 IOPS backfill 6× (verified live)

Measured attack on the first-paint latency (P2). `pg_stat_statements` (by `shared_blks_read`) showed the top ~15 IO consumers are ALL background cron/backfills — the public first-paint queries (collection-stats/market/pack-reality) aren't even in the top 15, confirming the finding's thesis: **cheap user queries running slow under IOPS saturation from heavy background jobs**, not slow queries themselves. So the lever is the read-diet, not query optimization.

- **SHIPPED (DB-only, prod-state) — throttled `backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev` (pg_cron jobid 71, owner `cron_heavy`).** The #1 total-exec-time consumer (2.77h total / 222 calls / 1.64M block reads). It re-scanned ALL TS `pack_distributions` with expensive per-dist correlated subqueries (`count(DISTINCT drop_weight)`, `NOT EXISTS pack_ev_history`, `sec_ask`) **every 10 min** to find ≤10 dists lacking a fresh (<12h) EV row — but ~146 of the ~157 candidates can never insert (pool_incomplete `ok:false` / no live ask post the 07-16 guard), so it **spun** on them, burning ~7.4K blocks/scan × 6/hr during the contention windows. Freshness invariant is 12h → 10-min cadence was ~6× overkill. Changed to **hourly** (`13 * * * *`) + `p_limit` 10→15 so 12 runs × 15 = 180/12h still refreshes the full 157-dist backlog inside 12h. **~6× fewer candidate scans; no logic/output change.** Verified live: jobid 71 `13 * * * *`, `...(15)`, owner still `cron_heavy`, active. (`alter_job` was blocked — postgres has EXECUTE but not ownership; cron_heavy owns it but lacks EXECUTE — so updated in place via `cron.schedule` upsert-by-name AS cron_heavy.) **REVERT:** `SET ROLE cron_heavy; SELECT cron.schedule('rpc-backfill-historical-pack-ev','3,13,23,33,43,53 * * * *','SELECT public.backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev(10)'); RESET ROLE;`
- **SHIPPED 3 more measured throttles (DB-only, all owner `cron_heavy`, all proven-spinning by direct measurement, cadence-only/reversible):**
  - **`backfill_null_serial_sales_from_moments` (jobid 76): every-15-min → hourly (`5 * * * *`, ~4× cut).** Scans 1,505 null-serial sales (45d window) every run to find only **2 resolvable now** — ~99.9% spinning on unresolvable rows; historical-sale serials tolerate hourly latency (new sales resolve as their moments hydrate). **REVERT:** `SET ROLE cron_heavy; SELECT cron.schedule('rpc-recover-null-serial-sales','5,20,35,50 * * * *','SELECT public.backfill_null_serial_sales_from_moments()'); RESET ROLE;`
  - **`rollup_allday_rip_pull_value` (jobid 72): every-30-min → hourly (`14 * * * *`, ~2× cut).** Full 173K-row `allday_pack_pull` GROUP BY every run but only **9 changed writes/6h** (22 AllDay rips/24h — AllDay ended primary packs). **REVERT:** `... cron.schedule('rpc-allday-rollup-rip-value','14,44 * * * *','SELECT public.rollup_allday_rip_pull_value()'); ...`
  - **`sync_allday_pack_dist_totals` (jobid 75): every-30-min → hourly (`24 * * * *`, ~2× cut).** Full `v_allday_pack_info` scan every run but **0 of 3,052 AllDay dists updated in 24h** (`total_minted` frozen post-primary-end) — pure spinning. **REVERT:** `... cron.schedule('rpc-sync-allday-pack-dist-totals','12,42 * * * *','SELECT public.sync_allday_pack_dist_totals()'); ...`
- **Intentionally LEFT ALONE (throttling = real user-facing-freshness tradeoff, not free):** `refresh_mv_pack_ev_latest` (10-min, keeps core pack-EV boards fresh), `roll_pack_ask_hourly_low` (15-min, each run captures the intra-hour ask MINIMUM via `LEAST` → extra runs add real 24h/7d low-ask accuracy), `refresh_allday_badge_low_ask` (30-min, real badge-ask work), `dedup_allday_cross_source_sales` (already hourly). These do incremental real work at their cadence — not throttled blind.
- **Seed-wallet-refresh read-diet (handoff `03`-I / cost-runbook #3): FINDING — already comprehensively implemented in code (2026-06-14 `VERCEL-FLUID-RIGHTSIZE`):** dispatch pacing (`DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE=6`, `TARGET_SPREAD_MS=9min`, ~18× lower peak child-arrival), a low-priority interval gate (skip priority-≥4 discovered-cohort wallets walked <24h ago, env-tunable `SEED_REFRESH_LOWPRI_INTERVAL_HOURS`), AND a cohort-split mechanism (`?cohort=K&of=N`). The remaining levers there — widening the env interval or activating staggered cohort cron entries — are **operator/config actions** (Vercel env / cron-job.org), NOT new code. Deliberately did not invent a marginal staleness-risking code change.
- **NET:** 4 measured throttles on the top IOPS-spinning offenders (6× + 4× + 2× + 2×), each proven-spinning and reversible → cuts background IOPS during the contention windows that were the root cause of the 8–16s public first-paint. Validate the aggregate IOPS/latency impact over the next cycle; further cuts need the operator config levers or user-facing-freshness tradeoffs.

### 2026-07-17 (Cowork, interactive, round 5) — SELF-CORRECTION: rwfd v2 was a regression (read the fmv_current VIEW = full-history scan); v3 reads fmv_snapshots directly (818k buffers -> 130)

Caught my own regression by EXPLAIN-ing what I'd shipped this morning instead of trusting a warm-cache timing (the exact "measure the loop, don't trust a warm sample" lesson).

- **The regression:** round-2 rwfd v2 sourced the changed-set + values from the **`fmv_current` VIEW**, which I'd assumed was a cheap maintained table. It is a **VIEW** = `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ... FROM fmv_snapshots ORDER BY edition_id, computed_at DESC` — a FULL scan of the 876k-row fmv_snapshots_2026 partition (**818,583 buffers / 1.09s**), and v2 read it TWICE per call. That was WORSE than the v1 it replaced (315 MB/call). My v2 "1s" number was warm-cache-lucky.
- **SHIPPED — rwfd v3** (migration `audit_20260717_rwfd_delta_v3_direct_snapshots`): reads the delta straight from `fmv_snapshots` with the `computed_at > watermark` predicate on `idx_fmv_snapshots_2026_computed_at_desc` — a snapshot newer than the watermark IS by definition that edition's latest, so `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ... WHERE computed_at > cutoff` returns exactly the changed editions with current FMV. **EXPLAIN: 130 buffers / 3ms** (index range scan — structurally cheap, NOT cache-dependent this time; ~6,000× fewer reads than v2). Measured 1.8s backlog / 0.015s steady-state; invariants []. Semantics identical to v1/v2; watermark unchanged. **Revert:** restore the v2 (fmv_current) def from migration history.
- **Lesson reinforced (memory updated):** before claiming a rewrite is cheaper, EXPLAIN(BUFFERS) the actual inner read — a warm-cache wall-clock sample hid a 6,000× regression. And: check `relkind` before assuming a name is a table (fmv_current is a view; my earlier "fmv_current has no PK, add one" flag was moot).

Owned the double-close route bug the wave-8 coverage sweep documented and explicitly left for a follow-up owner (its test deliberately skipped the two crashing paths). **SHIPPED `24874f1b` (code + test):** `app/api/bulk-classify/route.ts` — the background SSE streamer's two early-return paths (`requestedOffset >= total`, and the mid-run wall-clock TIMEOUT) each called `await writer.close()` then `return`, but `return` inside the `try` still runs the `finally`, which closed the writer AGAIN → `ERR_INVALID_STATE` unhandled promise rejection from the fire-and-forget IIFE. These are the classifier's two most common terminal paths (a caught-up wallet; any backlog exceeding one 55s call), so the rejection fired routinely in prod. Fix: made the `finally` the single close point (dropped the two explicit closes) + guarded the finally close and the error-path `send` with `.catch(()=>{})` so a client-aborted SSE (already-errored writer) also can't throw. Added 2 regression tests (offset>=total → done/processed:0; timeout branch via a `Date.now` spy → timeout/nextOffset:0) — a clean stream read is the assertion the writer closes once; **7/7 green, tsc clean** (both paths previously crashed the test process with exit 1). **Revert:** `git revert 24874f1b`.

### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive) — pack-dist smoke false-fail root-caused DEEPER than round 6: swallowed streamed-body timeout → hard "200, needle=false"; fixed in `checkHtmlContains`

The "pack dist 5048: 200, Sales History=false" hard-fail (fired 07-16 during the live 60s-statement-timeout contention window — `analytics-smoke` cancelled 18:43–21:43Z, `rpc_sales_summary_topshot_30d` 16–25s) is the SAME class round 6 mitigated by retargeting 7800→5048, but the actual bug is in the smoke harness, not the probe target. Every RPC the pack page's streamed bottom block runs is <200ms in isolation (get_pack_sales_history 177ms, get_pack_contents 109ms, exhausted-count 0.16ms, top-pulls pool sub-second) — so dist 5048 is not a module regression. Root cause: the pack "Sales History" (and edition "Activity") sections flush from a `<Suspense>` boundary AFTER the 200 shell headers; `fetch()` resolves on headers, so the retry/inconclusive guard was already past when the streamed-body `res.text()` read ran under the SAME AbortSignal budget. Under contention the flush blew the budget, `res.text()` rejected mid-stream, and the old `.catch(() => "")` swallowed the abort to `""` → `needle`-absent read out as a HARD "HTTP 200, <needle>=false" — bypassing the whole soft-inconclusive machinery built for exactly this.

- **SHIPPED (code) — `checkHtmlContains` now reads the streamed body INSIDE the retry/inconclusive handling** (`app/api/smoke-test/route.ts`). A timeout in the fetch OR the streamed-body read is now transient (retry once → SOFT inconclusive, never Sentry); a body that fully reads but genuinely lacks the needle still HARD-fails as a real module regression. Fixes both HTTP-contains probes (pack Sales History + edition Activity). Complementary to the round-6 retarget (which reduced frequency but not the swallow). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. **Target metric:** the hourly "pack dist … Sales History=false" hard page stops firing during contention windows (reclassifies to soft inconclusive); a real missing-module regression still pages.

### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive, afternoon) — night-queue Item 1 SHIPPED: `get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite kills the #1 disk reader (1,522 MB/193s → 8.4 MB/119ms)

Worked the 07-16 night handoff ([docs/handoff-2026-07-16-evening-queue.md](../handoff-2026-07-16-evening-queue.md)) top item — the post-wmc-fix #1 pg_stat_statements reader. Shipped **1** (DB-only, 1 index + 1 fn rewrite), reverted 0. Pure DB; no code deploy. Ledger is the record.

- **SHIPPED — `get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite** (migrations `audit_20260716_wmc_lockcheck_order_index` + `audit_20260716_get_lock_check_batch_index_driven_rewrite`). The old body window-ranked the ENTIRE stale `wallet_moments_cache` set (~2.0M rows) per call with a per-row `EXISTS(hot_wallets)` subplan in both the SELECT and the window `ORDER BY`, then `LIMIT p_limit` — measured **1,522 MB read / 193s in a single call** (historic 1,286 GB / 1,460 calls). It was the driver of the hourly IOPS-saturation windows (page-view 30s statement-timeouts + smoke pages). New body: index `idx_wmc_lockcheck_order (collection_id, lock_checked_at ASC NULLS FIRST)` (14 MB) + two index-driven arms per collection off that index — (a) fill = the p_limit stalest rows in the collection, (b) priority = the p_limit stalest rows owned by a hot wallet (472 hot addrs, materialized once) — `UNION ALL`, dedup (`bool_or` reconstructs `is_priority` with **no** per-row EXISTS), then rank priority-first/stalest-first per collection and round-robin via `ORDER BY rn, collection_id`. **Identical batch semantics** to the old body (validated pre-swap: golazos scoped old-vs-new = 44/44 rows, 0 set diff, 0 priority-flag mismatch; + composition proof — each arm capped at p_limit is sufficient because the final batch is ≤ p_limit total). **EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS)** unscoped/limit200: `Index Scan using idx_wmc_lockcheck_order` on both arms, **shared hit=690 read=383 (~8.4 MB) / Execution 119 ms** (was 1,522 MB / 193,000 ms → ~180× fewer reads, ~1,600× faster). Live fn verified: 200 rows / 5 collections / 0 null keys / priority-first (matches old ranking); SECDEF + ACL `postgres`+`service_role` only (no anon/authenticated). Route unchanged (still reads the same 4 out_ cols).
  - **Build note (reusable):** MCP `execute_sql` wraps multi-statement calls in a txn (→ `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` 25001); a lone-statement CONCURRENTLY avoids the txn but is still 2min-capped and one full 785 MB wmc scan already exceeds 2 min under contention → canceled → invalid 0-byte index. Built instead via `apply_migration` plain `CREATE INDEX` in a verified-idle window (active=0) guarded by `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='4s'` + `maintenance_work_mem='128MB'`; completed <2 min, `indisvalid=true`. See [[route-db-calls-inherit-8s-statement-timeout]].
  - **Revert:** `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.idx_wmc_lockcheck_order;` + recreate the prior `get_lock_check_batch` body from migration history (the `WITH hot_wallets … ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY collection_id ORDER BY EXISTS(...) DESC, lock_checked_at NULLS FIRST)` window version).
  - **Target metric:** `get_lock_check_batch` drops out of the top of `pg_stat_statements` by shared_blks_read/call (≈0.9 GB/call → <0.02 GB/call); the hourly page-view statement-timeout bursts + smoke saturation windows stop; `lock-check-batch` pipeline stays ok=true.

Trevor: "get local main to stop falling behind and continuously stay synced across all mains." **Diagnosis:** the alarming "50 ahead / 50 behind" on local `main` was a **shallow-clone illusion** — web sessions clone this repo shallow (~50 deep) and start on a fresh `claude/*` branch, so the true merge-base sits below the fetch horizon and git falsely reports divergence. After `git fetch --unshallow`, local `main` was **0 ahead / 110 behind** = pure ancestor, just stale, no lost work, no conflicts. One-time fix applied live (`git branch -f main origin/main`).

- **SHIPPED (infra) — `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` + `.claude/settings.json` (`e01575ab`).** SessionStart hook (web-only, synchronous, idempotent) runs every session: unshallows the clone so relationships compute truthfully → fast-forwards local `main` to `origin/main` with `--ff-only` (**never** clobbers genuine unpushed commits — leaves them with a notice) → checks out `main` on a clean tree (per CLAUDE.md "always work on main"). `.gitignore` narrowed from `.claude/` to un-ignore ONLY those two shared files; local `.claude/` state stays ignored. Validated: caught a live `origin/main` advance (`d2b0eab2`→`a7421ee7`) and ff'd automatically; claude/*→main checkout path + non-remote guard both pass. **NOTE for nightly pass / monitor:** `.claude/hooks/` + `.claude/settings.json` are now TRACKED files — expected, not drift. **Revert:** `git rm -r .claude/hooks .claude/settings.json` + restore `.gitignore` line 52 to `.claude/`, or `git revert e01575ab`.

Picked up `docs/handoff-2026-07-12-*` (the overnight cron-failure investigation). Shipped the one blocked code item, then verified the DB-side fixes — and found the primary one never worked.

- **SHIPPED (code) — buyer-backfill forward lane bound to 2025+ (`44d741e`, prod `dpl_CEZHf4k6...` READY).** Added `.gte("sold_at", '2025-01-01')` to the forward null-buyer select in `app/api/admin/backfill-topshot-buyers/route.ts` (uses existing `HIST_WINDOW_END`) + `app/api/admin/backfill-allday-buyers/route.ts` (new `FORWARD_WINDOW_START` const). - **FINDING — the 2026-07-12 pg_cron `statement_timeout` fix (`audit_20260712_pgcron_stmt_timeout_and_stagger`) was INERT.** Heavy jobs were STILL dying at exactly 120s as recently as 14:03Z today (`cross-source-dedup`, `fmv-clamp`, `thin-fmv-guard`, `remap-misattrib`, `ccm-step1`, etc.) — **plus 4 the handoff never listed** (`backfill-historical-pack-ev` 43, `allday-rollup-rip-value` 23, `refresh-mv-pack-ev-latest` 35, `allday-badge-low-ask-refresh` 31). Root cause: pg_cron sends its command as one **simple-query batch**, so `statement_timeout` is armed once at batch start from the SESSION default (120s cluster default). The inline `SET statement_timeout='600s'; SELECT fn()` prefix (and the 06-30 proconfig) never re-arms the already-running batch. Yesterday's "live validation" passed only because it ran through a normal client session (separate `SET` message), which is NOT how pg_cron executes.

### 2026-07-11 ~10:25 PT (Claude Code, interactive) — 3 failing pipelines fixed: pack-opens backfill lock-timeout (DB fix LIVE) + hydrator whole-chunk-discard (committed, needs deploy)

Trevor flagged 3 pipelines with 3 consecutive failures each. Diagnosed from live `pipeline_runs` (ground truth differed from the report: topshot backfill already `done`, allday failing with **lock** timeout not statement timeout). Commit `c1ba51e` (local `main`, **NOT pushed**). DB migration `audit_20260711_upsert_pack_rips_lock_timeout` **applied to remote (live now)**.

- **`pack-opens-api-backfill-{topshot,allday}` — "canceling statement due to lock timeout" ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (DB fix live).** Not a missing index (`idx_pack_rips_tx_hash` unique exists) and not statement timeout (RPC already `statement_timeout=60s`). Real cause: the edge fn calls `upsert_pack_rips_from_api` (SECDEF, service_role) but the PostgREST session connects via `authenticator`, whose session-preloaded **`lock_timeout=8s` survives `SET ROLE`** and applies inside the RPC (which only overrode statement_timeout). Overlapping backfill invocations walk the SAME `after_cursor` and upsert the SAME `pack_nft_id` rows → the second contends on `pack_rips` locks and dies at 8s (each real page-upsert is sub-second). **Fix 1 (DB, LIVE):** migration adds `lock_timeout=25s` to the RPC so a brief overlap waits it out instead of failing (grants unchanged: postgres+service_role, no anon). **Fix 2 (edge, needs deploy):** per-collection `claim/release_pipeline_lock` guard in `backfill-pack-opens-api` so overlapping runs cleanly no-op (fail-open, 300s stale). **Verified:** since the migration, 5 consecutive allday ticks `ok=true`, `rips_total` 1,141,298→1,221,269 (~20k/tick), **0 lock-timeout failures** — incl. a 17:20:20Z tick where topshot+allday fired the same second and both passed. **Revert:** `ALTER FUNCTION public.upsert_pack_rips_from_api(jsonb) RESET lock_timeout;` + `git revert c1ba51e`.
- **`topshot-moments-hydrator` — "gql errors: Error with GetMintedMoment" ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (needs CF worker deploy).** Client bug, NOT TopShot's API down (50 moments/run resolve fine). `fetchChunk` discarded the **entire 50-id aliased chunk** whenever `json.errors` was non-empty — but GraphQL returns **partial data**: one burned/retired moment nulls only its own alias while the other 49 succeed. One poison id wasted 49 good lookups and let the permanent tail of unresolvable ids at the queue head (`v_moments_needing_hydration`) starve throughput → the observed alternating ok=false / `fetched_from_graphql:0` runs. **Fix:** parse `json.data` even when `errors` present; unresolved aliases fall through as `graphql_failures` (now counted, previously vanished). Separate hard chunk failures (HTTP/network/parse — no data) from normal per-id upstream errors; only hard failures (or a 0-row write with resolvable rows) flip `ok=false`. Adds `hard_chunk_failures` telemetry. Worker typecheck passes. **Revert:** `git revert c1ba51e`.
- **DEPLOY NEEDED (noted, not done — no push/deploy per constraint):** (1) Supabase edge fn `backfill-pack-opens-api` (concurrency guard — belt-and-suspenders; the DB lock_timeout fix already stopped the failures). (2) CF worker `topshot-moments-hydrator` (`wrangler deploy` — this is what activates the #3 fix; until deployed the hydrator keeps discarding poisoned chunks). Commit `c1ba51e` is on local `main`, unpushed.
- **Left untouched:** the 2 pre-existing unstaged edits (`edition/[slug]/page.tsx`, `moment/[id]/page.tsx`) from concurrent work. No FMV-calc code touched.

`fmv-recalc` was logging intermittent `edition_page_fetch: canceling statement due to statement timeout` (3 consecutive fails at report time; scattered pairs across the day, clustering at higher OFFSET 2500/5000/7500). **Root cause:** Step-1a's edition-page query (`SELECT edition_id FROM sales WHERE sold_at >= now()-30d AND price_usd>0 AND collection_id<>pinnacle AND edition_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY edition_id ORDER BY MAX(sold_at) DESC LIMIT/OFFSET`) ran through the generic `query_sql` RPC, which inherits the **service_role 30s statement_timeout**. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` = **31.2s cold vs 0.18s warm** — the 30-day window now spans ~110K sales rows / ~11,953 distinct editions, and with no `sold_at`-leading index the planner does a full scan of `sales_2026_collection_id_sold_at_idx` (collection_id leading, unusable for a sold_at-only range) + ~110K heap fetches (~18.5K cold blocks). Not a code regression — organic sales-volume growth pushed the cold scan just past 30s; warm runs (most) passed, cold/contended runs failed. Confirmed via `pipeline_runs` (ok=true runs interleaved with the timeouts).

- **SHIPPED (DB) — `fmv_recalc_edition_page(timestamptz, uuid, int, int)`** (`audit_20260711_fmv_recalc_edition_page_fn_120s_timeout` + `_revoke_anon`). Dedicated SECURITY DEFINER fn, `SET statement_timeout=120s` + `search_path=public` in proconfig (mirrors `query_sql`'s RLS-bypass so behavior is identical), **service_role-only** (REVOKE anon+authenticated — Supabase default-privs re-grant them on new public fns; `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` []). Output verified byte-identical to the inline query (2500/2500 rows, full INTERSECT overlap). Gives the page fetch deterministic headroom regardless of planner/cache state (120s ≫ 31s cold worst case). Revert: `DROP FUNCTION public.fmv_recalc_edition_page(timestamptz, uuid, integer, integer);`
- **SHIPPED (DB) — covering index `idx_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window`** (`audit_20260711_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window_covering_index`) `ON sales_2026 (sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (edition_id, collection_id) WHERE price_usd>0 AND edition_id IS NOT NULL`. Once autovacuum lifts `sales_2026` visibility (currently 74% all-visible; the query targets the newest, least-visible pages), the planner switches to a fast index-only scan and the cold path drops from ~31s to ~sub-second — the 120s ceiling becomes a safety floor, never the steady state. Non-concurrent build (MCP wraps DDL in a txn so `CONCURRENTLY` is unavailable; 492MB partition built in <1s under a brief ShareLock, harmless to cursor-based sales ingest). Revert: `DROP INDEX public.idx_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window;`
- **SHIPPED (code `e2f3922`, deploy `dpl_9kd98rsU2UiKTZZC3LtqVdyTkovf`)** — route Step-1a now calls `fmv_recalc_edition_page` instead of the inline `query_sql`. Additive, single call-site swap; response shape unchanged (`{edition_id}[]`). Revert: `git revert e2f3922`.
- Relation to the standing **FMV-RECALC-EDITION-FETCH-TIMEOUT-CREEP** ledger watch (DB-growth contention) — this is that creep crossing the hard 30s wall; now fixed deterministically.

This is a pack-EV pricing change → build + verify against `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev.calibrated_ev` (realized pulls) before wiring as the display EV. **Cheaper interim alternative worth measuring first:** for depleted dists that HAVE a `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev` row, surface `calibrated_ev` (realized-pull-anchored) as the headline instead of the pool EV — no new model. NOT shipped this pass (larger, FMV/pricing-sensitive, and the handoff flags it non-autonomous). **Do NOT attempt the proxy re-weight — it can't recover missing tiers, and bulk-driving topshot-proxy trips Cloudflare 1015.**

Traced it: the DB + API are correct (`v_collection_marketplace_status` golazos = healthy/buy_ctas_enabled=true; live `GET /api/marketplace-status?collection=laliga-golazos` with `no-store` returns **healthy**), but the client hook `components/marketplace-status/useMarketplaceStatus.ts` fetched with `cache:"force-cache"` — which returns the browser's HTTP-cache copy **fresh OR stale**, ignoring the route's `s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60`. A live `force-cache` fetch returned the stale pre-fix **unknown/buy_ctas=false**. So any visitor who loaded Golazos before 07-03 kept seeing the old banner + suppressed buy CTAs indefinitely (until browser eviction), never reaching the intended 5-min refresh; symmetrically it would keep buy CTAs live after a collection went UNhealthy. The stated reason for `force-cache` (one call per slug per session) is already met by the module-level `memoryCache`/`inflight` dedup, so `force-cache` only added staleness. Switched to `cache:"no-cache"` (revalidate; the CDN `s-maxage=300` still absorbs load). Affects the banner + every client marketplace-status consumer (sniper/market/collection/overview rows). tsc clean (changed file). No FMV/pricing. **Revert:** `git revert` (cache mode back to `force-cache`).

- **Item 1 (topshot-sales-history-backfill 429 storm).** The pipeline was hard rate-limited on ~every TS GQL call — ticks completed in ~0s draining nothing while ~5.6K editions sat pending. Fix spans two files:
  - `lib/chains/flow/topshot.ts` — `topshotGraphql` gained an **opt-in** 3rd arg `TopshotGraphqlOptions { retryOn429, maxRetries, maxBackoffMs }`. When `retryOn429` is set, a 429 is retried honoring the server `Retry-After` header (delta-seconds OR HTTP-date), falling back to exponential backoff (2s·2^n) + jitter, each sleep capped by `maxBackoffMs`. **Default OFF → every existing caller (sniper-feed, badge-sync, …) is byte-identical; zero blast radius.**
  - `app/api/cron/topshot-sales-history-backfill/route.ts` — opts in via `GQL_OPTS { retryOn429, maxRetries:2, maxBackoffMs:8000 }` on both GQL call sites; adds a `GQL_THROTTLE_MS=250` sleep before every set-map/tx page fetch; adds an `INTER_EDITION_DELAY_MS=350` sleep between editions; drops `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` 120→15 (small batch — hundreds/tick just re-trips the limiter); and adds attempt-counter integrity — an edition that exhausts `MAX_EDITION_ATTEMPTS` on a retryable (gql/setmap) error is now counted (`editions_maxed_out`, surfaced in the `pipeline_runs.extra` + a `console.log`) instead of silently freezing in `error` status. Bounded: worst-case retry adds ~16s to one call, well inside `maxDuration=300` with the between-edition budget break. **Verify:** watch `pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline='topshot-sales-history-backfill'` — runs should show `sales_inserted>0` / declining `pending_remaining` once the queue clears. **Revert:** `git revert` the two-file commit (DB untouched; the opt-in param is inert for all other callers).
  - Note: the route calls `public-api.nbatopshot.com` directly (via `topshotGraphql`), not the proxy — 429 (not 403) confirms the requests reach the API; the fix is rate-pacing, not a routing change.
  - **Follow-up (same day, `921f5fc`): `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` 15→40.** A post-deploy `workflow_dispatch` tick verified the fix live — 15 editions ran with only **2 `gql_errors`** (~13% vs the ~83% pre-fix; 13/15 drained, 0 maxed_out, budget NOT hit). Since the batch cap (not the limiter) was bounding throughput on the finite ~5.6K queue, raised to 40 so the 240s `ELAPSED_BUDGET_MS` is the limiter again (throttle + inter-edition delay govern API pressure per call regardless of batch), draining ~2x faster at the same low error rate. Deliberately exceeds the prompt's "5-10/run" (that was a proxy for "don't burst," now enforced by the throttle). **Revert:** set `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` back to 15 (or `git revert 921f5fc`).
- **Item 2 (Bug 13 — restore moment-page LISTED field).** The earlier 07-03 entry HID the field because its only source (`ts_listings`) is dead. This restores it from `cached_listings_v2` — the live on-chain listing feed (currently 21,999 active AllDay listings / 20,900 flow_ids; Golazos 0 right now; no TS rows yet). `app/moment/[id]/page.tsx`: new `fetchActiveListingAsk(nftId)` does `DISTINCT ON`-equivalent (`.eq(flow_id) .is(completed_at,null) .order(price_usd asc) .limit(1)`) → cheapest active ask; wired into the serial-block `Promise.all` (kind='moment' only, keyed on `ss.nft_id`); renders a single `Listed` StatCell (`fmtUsd`, dash when unlisted). Collection-agnostic: TS moments have no rows → honest `—` (not a wrong value off a dead feed); AllDay moments light up (verified `/moment/10658549` → flow_id 10658549 has an active $99 ask). Read-only against `cached_listings_v2`. **Revert:** `git revert` the moment-page commit.

### 2026-07-02 (daytime, Claude Code) — P8 WRITER GUARD SHIPPED: found + fixed the 5th moments-writer (the hydrator's ambiguous (set,play)→edition map); leak stopped, drain now durable

The updated handoff flagged that P8's corrupt-moments set is NOT finite — ~325/24h are actively created by an unidentified 5th moments-writer, so firing the `?p8=1` drain once just re-accumulates. Found the writer, root-caused it, and guarded the write chokepoint. 1 commit (`1cd46de`) + 1 migration (applied via MCP `audit_20260702_replace_topshot_moments_batch_parallel_guard`, repo-synced `supabase/migrations/20260702150000_*`); `check_public_security_invariants()` **[]**; verified live end-to-end.

- **The 5th writer = `topshot-moments-hydrator`** (worker, every 10 min, ~265 moments/run). Its `resolveEditions()` (workers/topshot-moments-hydrator/index.ts L289-298) selects editions by `(set_id_onchain, play_id_onchain)` and builds a `${set}:${play}`→edition uuid map — but the **2026-06-20 subedition catalog cloned those on-chain ids onto every `::` parallel**, so that pair is non-unique (base + all parallels share it) and the map is **overwritten by whichever row PostgREST returns last**. A small-circ `::` parallel can win → a Standard moment lands on it (serial > parallel circ = impossible). NOT the `/api/ingest` `buildEditionKey` (that's submap-gated + 97% of corrupt nfts aren't in the submap), NOT a circulation backfill.
- **Evidence (re-measured live):** 464 corrupt; **328 moment-side inserts/24h, edition-side untouched (0)**, `created_at==updated_at` (fresh inserts of new nfts); the SALES for these nfts sit on **base** (`sale_on_same_parallel=0` all sources) = moment-only mis-key; **452/464 not in `topshot_moment_subeditions`**; **114/114 corrupt `::`editions share (set,play) with a base sibling**; hydrator runs time-correlate to the newest corrupt insert (21:02Z).
- **Fix (root-cause, at the write chokepoint) — `replace_topshot_moments_batch(jsonb)`.** This SECDEF RPC is where every moments writer actually lands rows, so the guard lives here (mirrors the sales-indexer Step-4e + offer_fill base-redirect). A `redirected` CTE, applied **before** the `(edition_id,serial_number)` dedupe (so post-redirect collisions collapse instead of tripping `ON CONFLICT ... cannot affect row a second time`), rewrites any incoming moment on a `::`parallel with `serial > that parallel's circulation` to the **base** `setID:playID` edition; genuine subedition moments (serial ≤ circ) pass through untouched. Catches the hydrator AND any future caller.
- **Deliberately did NOT force base in the hydrator worker.** The hydrator can't place genuine parallels (no submap); forcing all (set,play) resolutions to base would re-collide genuine parallel serials with base serials — the exact conflation the `::`-split solved. The DB guard only touches the unambiguously-impossible case (serial > parallel circ), leaving genuine-parallel placement to the existing submap-driven `remap_topshot_base_keyed_parallel_sales()`.
- **Verified live (MCP):** (1) end-to-end RPC probe — `replace_topshot_moments_batch` with a Standard serial 11 keyed onto `222:7443::20` (circ 10) → **landed on base `222:7443`** (test row cleaned up, no real moment touched); (2) negative replay — **0/500** existing genuine parallels would be redirected; (3) **two** post-guard hydrator cycles (**21:12Z + 21:22Z**, ~268 moments each) → **0 new corrupt** (newest corrupt still 21:02Z, the last pre-guard run; vs the pre-guard ~2–3/run); (4) `check_public_security_invariants()` **[]**.
- **Consequence: `?p8=1` (24fec11) is now a durable one-shot.** New impossible mis-keys are blocked, so the existing 464 are a finite set the drain cleans on firing (operator/deployed, proxy creds). The 175 colliders still need on-chain truth (the drain's `remap_topshot_from_onchain_map()` free-slot leg handles them); the 281 non-colliders could alternatively be bulk-redirected to base via the same guard logic if the operator prefers not to fire the drain. **Revert:** restore the prior function body from `supabase/migrations/20260517131500_replace_topshot_moments_batch_on_conflict_do_update.sql` (+ `git revert 1cd46de`).

Tightened reliability β<1.0 → only COMMON+ALL-pooled reliable (sub-linear); RARE/LEG/FANDOM→pooled. v2: base<$150 (96% of volume) calibrated 0.88–0.94 / APE ~0.50; grails conservative (≈base above ~$450). vs LT v2 is below LT on grails BUT sales back v2 → LT over-prices illiquid grails (don't chase). Net: jersey is sales-validated/wireable for the bulk with a high-FMV low-confidence flag; grail tail unmodelable (thin data). Still INERT. Revert: re-create the fit fn with β<1.25 + recompute.
- **Deep multi-factor serial analysis (2026-06-30, read-only).** Tested "value from many property factors" with 5-fold CV (held-out $APE) across #1/perfect/jersey (n=679/242/186, FMV-anchored). Only FMV+tier+circ generalize for #1 (testR² 0.66 / APE 44%); perfect=FMV (0.54/46%); jersey=FMV (0.34/52%). `series`, `play_category`, AND `player-stardom` all OVERFIT (raise train fit, not held-out; player-star redundant with edition FMV). Noise floor ~44–52% APE is irreducible (special-serial prices high-variance). A many-factor model = fitting noise; the parsimonious FMV+tier+circ model is the honest ceiling, and the existing power-law models are near-optimal (one validated gain: explicit circ for #1). Detail in handoff "Deep multi-factor analysis".
- **Serial factors — rookie/TS-Debut badges + player career scarcity also REJECTED (2026-06-30).** CV-tested Trevor's intuitive factors on #1 (n=336) from `badge_editions` (Top Shot Debut, Rookie Year/Premiere/RoY, badge_score) + per-player Σcirc (Wemby-scarcity): base FMV+tier+circ R² 0.536 → +each ~flat (0.533–0.536), +ALL four 0.528 (overfit); coeffs ~0/wrong-signed conditional on FMV. WHY: edition FMV is a near-sufficient statistic — the market already prices rookie/debut/scarcity INTO base FMV, so they're redundant in the serial-premium layer (they belong in the base FMV model). Confirms: serial premium = f(FMV,tier,circ) by type; nothing else generalizes.
- **Special-serial trends + PARALLELS swept (2026-06-30, descriptive).** #1 multiple is monotone-inverse to circ (mass-common 35× / $25 → grail 3.8×) + tier (COMMON 18× / LEG 2.5×); vintage abs-premium (S1/S2 $1k–9k, thin); set high-mult = cheap-common sets (Extra Spice 42×); player superstar cheap-common #1s 28–50× (Luka 50/Steph 49/Wemby 28/LeBron 15) vs pumped-rookie low-mult. PARALLELS: 137 #1+126 perfect/yr; multiple tracks parallel scarcity EXACTLY (Club Collection circ99 7.8× → Galactic circ5 1.4×); base-#1 cheaper when parallels exist (9.6× vs 5.9×, no parallel-exists discount). Parallels need NO separate model — each `::` is its own edition with own FMV+circ, so FMV+tier+circ prices them right; only lever = per-parallel circ/FMV accuracy (~22% of `::` still floor-circ). Detail: handoff trends+parallels section.
- **Base edition-FMV factor test — badges/series/rookie DO predict base value (2026-06-30, the thin-edition lever).** Mirror of the serial finding: predicting ln(edition FMV) from FEATURES ONLY (no own sales), 5-fold CV n=700: tier+circ R² 0.643/51% → +series 0.681/47% → +badges(TS-Debut/rookie/badge_score) **0.732/43%**. Coeffs: LEG +2.57, ln(circ) −0.556, newer-series negative (vintage premium real), rookie +0.137, badge_score +0.136/pt; player-career-circ weak (−0.025). So property factors are redundant for the serial PREMIUM (already in FMV) but PREDICTIVE for BASE value — usable as a feature PRIOR for NO_DATA/thin-LOW editions (~213 NO_DATA + LOW tail) where sales-recalc has no signal. Review-gated base-FMV pricing change (LT gate + Trevor). Detail: handoff base-FMV section.
- **Feature-prior stress-test + CORRECTION (2026-06-30).** Built `v_topshot_fmv_feature_prior` (read-only/INERT, cohort median FMV tier×series×circ_band×rookie; 39% APE/98% cov held-out). CORRECTION: the cohort prior is PLAYER-BLIND → its over_3x divergence is dominated by LEGIT STARS (Flagg Rookie-Debut $1,876 vs prior $6, LeBron $819, Jokić $8,999), NOT mispricing — so the earlier "323 stale-chase pool editions" read was WRONG. Player-aware prior is worse (80% APE, sparse — most players <3 priced editions). Bottom line: no feature-only substitute for sales on the star tail; cohort prior helps only the NON-STAR thin tail (~31/188 NO_DATA). REINFORCES: edition FMV (sales-derived, stardom-aware) is the near-sufficient statistic; thin-tail lever = more sales density, not a feature prior. View kept as honest cohort reference (comment fixed). Revert: DROP VIEW v_topshot_fmv_feature_prior.

TO authenticated` next to its RLS policy — a forgotten grant is a LOUD permission-denied, not silent data loss. Post-change: invariant **0**, anon SELECT on public boards preserved (deals board still readable). **Revert:** `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE,TRUNCATE ON TABLES TO authenticated;` (+ re-grant on the swept views if any path actually needed it — none should).

- **OFFER-SANITY-RAISE · 2026-06-09 (data-quality sweep, recommend) · [LOW-MED · CC — edition_offers writer, off-limits to the passes] schedule the durable GREATEST-based `edition_offers.highest_offer` raise.** `v_offer_sanity_flags` = 174 (was 132 on 06-07); composition stable + structural: 138 (79%) are `chain_exceeds_gql`+sub_serial (GQL collapses subedition/serial offers; max gap $658), 21 `gql_blank_chain_has` (the 12 non-subedition ones carry the headline gaps — SGA Kingmaker $5,222, LeBron Supernova $5,000, Wilt $1,501). Growth tracks on-chain offer accrual, not a fault. Durable fix (per `rpc-offers-data-model` memory): raise `edition_offers.highest_offer` via `GREATEST(existing, chain_open_max)` — never clobber down — keyed off the on-chain `offers` open-max, in a CC-owned job; recurring raise (slowly grows), not a one-time backfill. Optional companion: add `offer_sanity_max_gap` to `v_rpc_trust_health` scoped to edition-grain gaps (CREATE OR REPLACE on the live monitoring view — CC, not a watchlist row). Sweep did NOT write edition_offers (task-forbidden). **CLASSIFICATION LOCKED 2026-06-09 (Trevor):** `offers.offer_type` is 3 nested grains, each displays at its OWN grain — **edition** (universal across the edition), **subedition** (that subedition only), **serial** (that one serial only). The edition "Best offer" cell may be raised ONLY by `offer_type='edition'` (a serial/subedition bid is not the edition floor). Open volumes: edition 5,284 / subedition 1,541 / serial 535. Validated raise scope = `GREATEST(existing, max(offers WHERE offer_type='edition' AND status='open'))`: the REAL edition-cell gap is just **14 editions** (`gql_blank_chain_has`, ~$17.2k total, max $5,222 SGA Kingmaker / $5,000 LeBron Supernova / $1,501 Wilt); the other 13 edition-grain flags are penny noise ($14 total) and the 147 sub/serial flags are correctly out-of-scope. Small + safe. Subedition offers → a subedition-grain surface; serial offers → that serial's moment view. Detail: `docs/data-quality-sweep-2026-06-09.md`.
  **CC investigation 2026-06-12 (did NOT ship — two reasons, both needing a call above CC):** (1) **The raise must be edition-level, NOT a blind `GREATEST(existing, chain_open_max)`.** `v_offer_sanity_flags.chain_max_offer` is `max(offer_amount_usd)` over ALL open offers incl. `offer_type IN ('subedition','serial')`, and `has_sub_serial` is `bool_or` across the edition — so 79% of flags are serial-locked offers (a bid for serial #1 only). Raising an *edition*-level "Best offer" display to a serial-locked offer would misrepresent the price. The correct raise filters to `offer_type NOT IN ('subedition','serial')`: measured live = **30 editions** have a genuine edition-level on-chain offer above `edition_offers.highest_offer` (max gap still $5,222 — SGA Kingmaker), the real actionable set. That's a pricing-display semantics + recurring-cron decision = Trevor's product call + operator wiring, not auto-shippable. (2) **The `offer_sanity_max_gap` monitor must land WITH the raise, not before it.** Adding it to `v_rpc_trust_health` now would BREACH immediately on the $5,222 gap and stay breached until the (unbuilt) raise job closes it = chronic paging noise — the opposite of `fmv_sanity_flags` (which breaches at 1 because those are fixable now). Ship the edition-level raise first; add the monitor as its companion so it sits ok and catches regressions. CC left both unshipped deliberately.

- **Q8 · 2026-05-31 (PM, Claude Code) · [MED] badge-sync upsert poisons ~40% of batches → coverage barely grows.**
  SHIPPED (CC, commit `bd8f663`, deploy `dpl_5J9aTFbz4vG85LusJP4J7a5Pe7TS` READY): the badge-sync sweep was capped at MAX_PAGES(20)×100 = 2,000 editions/badge; raised to 80 (+`maxDuration=300`, PAGE_DELAY 400→250). Verified the cap is genuinely lifted — Top Shot Debut sweep now returns 2,018 (>old 2,000) and Rookie Year 1,138→1,596 distinct. BUT a full sweep grew the table only +23 (3,012→3,035 TS rows): the `POST /api/badge-sync` run logged `upserted:2006, upsertErrors:28` — ~1,400 collected rows dropped. ROOT CAUSE: the upsert uses `onConflict:"id"` but the table also has `badge_editions_ext_coll_unique UNIQUE(external_id,collection_id)`; parallels of the same play share an `external_id` but differ in `id`, so a parallel with a new id takes INSERT → violates the unique constraint → fails the WHOLE 50-row supabase-js batch. The lifted cap surfaces MORE parallels → more poisoned batches. Existing rows are a mix (2,819 parallel_id=0 + ~216 non-zero) so the table's row-grain is itself ambiguous (PK embeds parallel; unique key collapses to one-per-play). FIX (needs a row-grain decision + Trevor review — not rushed): decide one-row-per-play vs per-parallel, align `onConflict` + the unique constraint, and dedup the sweep by `external_id` in code to avoid "ON CONFLICT … cannot affect row a second time". NOT auto-shippable (touches the badge write path + a constraint). Memory: badge-editions-key-format-and-upsert-poison.

## 2026-07-16 (Cowork, interactive, continuation) — Pack EV ROOT CAUSES fixed: pool-insert PK collision (v22), TS remaining-basis, frozen realized layer revalued (35,812 rips), guard + calibration hardened

Trevor: "keep going on all of this — no cutting corners on data integrity." Every queued root cause from the morning session executed. Edge fn + 6 migrations + 1 chunked data remediation, all verified live.

### compute-topshot-pack-ev v22 (edge fn, deployed via MCP; repo copy committed this push)
- **ROOT CAUSE of the 306 "$0 EV on live packs" (incl. 2026 Finals/WNBA/Playoffs flagships): pool-insert PK collision.** Probe (temp edge fn `tmp-pack-pool-probe`, now 410-stubbed) proved `packEditionsV3` returns one node PER SLOT — the same edition appears in >=2 nodes on multi-slot packs (8520: 10 dupes of 29 editions; 8548: 6; 8564: 2). `pack_drop_pool`'s PK is `(collection_id, dist_id, edition_id, slot_name)` with `slot_name='default'` hard-coded -> the entire insert chunk failed 23505 AFTER the pool delete had run -> pool left EMPTY every tick -> `no_varied_remaining_pool` -> $0 sentinel, deterministically, forever (8514 never had a real EV since 05-22; the API had full real data the whole time — probe showed 8548 with 1,407 unopened + real per-edition remaining). **v22 merges duplicate editions (sum count + remaining) before insert.**
- **Pagination truncation:** the editions walk was 8 pages x default-10 = max 80 chase-sorted nodes. v22 passes `first: 50` (probe-verified accepted; typical pool now fits in 1 page).
- **Ask fallback:** `fetchSecondaryAskMap` now fills missing entries from `pack_ask_state` (canonical) — writer-side dual price no longer misses live asks (secondary_asks_count 1,950/tick, was Studio-only).
- **verify_jwt GOTCHA (memory updated):** MCP `deploy_edge_function` RESET `verify_jwt` false->true on redeploy, which would have 401'd the cron trigger (non-JWT Bearer). Caught immediately; toggled back OFF via the dashboard (Chrome). **Any future MCP redeploy of a cron-triggered fn must re-check verify_jwt.**
- Verified live: v22 ticks ok=true, pool_rows_written 42-158/tick, no auth gap.

### audit_20260716_pack_ev_guard_allow_single_edition_pools + audit_20260716_pack_ev_topshot_remaining_basis
- Guard refinement: `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` now blocks only MULTI-row uniform pools; honest single-edition packs (1762 Vintage Vibes - Dwyane Wade, genuinely 1 edition, 61,388 remaining) become priceable.
- **Basis correction per the 2026-07-07 Fix-A directive:** TS EV is now computed over the REMAINING pool (what a sealed-pack buyer actually draws from), not the original mint distribution (the 06-09 "Item 4" preference — a workaround for chase-truncated pools that v22 obsoletes). Non-TS callers unchanged. Same signature both times -> grants preserved; `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]`.

- `pack_rips.pull_value_usd` is only recomputed by the hourly backfill whose `ORDER BY metadata_updated_at NULLS FIRST` is permanently starved by **3.28M never-valued historical rips** -> already-valued rips NEVER re-refreshed. **35,812 of 39,930 dist-attributed rips (90% of the calibration ground truth) carried pre-07-02-disconnected-FMV-fix values.** Example: dist 3873 showed 3 "pulls" at ~$2,930 each whose moments' CURRENT FMVs sum to ~$12 -> realized_mean $844 on a $5 pack.

Verified: 0 stale remain; 3873 realized_mean $844.11 -> **$41.34**. Revert: `UPDATE pack_rips pr SET pull_value_usd=a.old_value FROM audit_20260716_rip_pull_value_revalue a WHERE pr.id=a.rip_id`.
- **Durable:** `audit_20260716_rip_backfill_split_budget_rotation` — `backfill_pack_rip_metadata` budget now splits 40% stale-already-valued (oldest first) / 60% newest-NULL drain, so the realized layer stays fresh and new rips still value quickly.

## 2026-07-16 (Cowork, interactive, continuation 4) — THE core Pack-EV inaccuracy found + guarded: chase-biased public-API pools

Accuracy validation pass on the now-repriced board surfaced the real reason "the numbers still don't seem accurate" on CURRENT packs. The 2026 Finals Standard (8548) showed $37 gross vs $18 ask (2x). Root cause: **packEditionsV3 returns a CHASE-BIASED edition list** — 8548's own remaining_by_tier says 4,564 commons / 958 rares / 4 legendaries still sealed, but the pool the API gave us had only 1 common edition + 4 legendaries. The per-slot RPC normalizes over that survivor set, so a handful of $772/$248 legendaries (2 copies left each) drag the mean to $37 while the TYPICAL pull is a $6 common. Same on 8520 WNBA ($45, driven by one genuinely-$48 Olivia Miles rookie common that was 79% of a pool holding only 149 of 8,695 real remaining moments).

**Rigorous completeness guard (audit_20260716_pack_ev_pool_completeness_guard, supersedes the same-day tier-fraction guard):** a COMPLETE per-slot remaining pool must have `sum(drop_weight) = sum(remaining)/total_unopened >= moments_per_pack >= 1`. Observed: complete pools (Atlas harvests, chance-hit packs) sum to 0.89-1.0; chase-biased packEditionsV3 pools sum to <0.08 (8548 0.038, 8520 0.075, 8601 0.009) — a clean 10x+ gap needing no tier/slot data. `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` now returns ok:false 'pool_incomplete' when TS sum(drop_weight)<0.5 → no writer emits chase-inflated EV; single-edition packs (sum_dw>=1) and Atlas pools pass. (The earlier tier-fraction guard caught 8548 but missed 8520, whose few captured commons happened to include the $48 rookie — the fraction looked fine while absolute coverage was 1.7%.)

**Routed to Atlas + flipped live:** `v_topshot_atlas_pool_targets` now also includes chase-incomplete gql pools (sum_dw<0.5) + adds 'atlas_refresh' for restaleing atlas pools — 174 targets (146 incomplete_pool). Wrote qualifying sentinels for the 97 currently-inflated incomplete dists (pack_price=ask so they supersede in pack_ev_latest's price>0 filter) → they now show honest "no EV" immediately. Verified live on pack_table_rows: 8548/8520/8564/8601 → NULL EV (honest); Grail Seeker $0.75, Birthday Party $3.23, Courtside $3.87 (Atlas-complete) → real EV. security 0/0/0/0.

**NET honest state:** Pack EV shows a real number ONLY where the pool is complete (Atlas-harvested or genuinely complete); chase-incomplete packs show "no EV" instead of a fabricated one. Re-running the Atlas harvest (`scripts/atlas-pool-harvest.ps1`, now 174 targets) gives the current flagship packs (Finals/WNBA/Playoffs) real complete-pool EVs — the differentiator. **Reverts:** restore prior compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted + v_topshot_atlas_pool_targets defs from migration history; the 97 sentinel rows age out as real EV rows land. **Deferred (Trevor decision):** the median/typical-pull display signal — even a complete-pool mean EV overstates the typical outcome for lottery-shaped packs; a "typical pull $X / jackpot $Y" UI split would be more honest than a single mean, but that's a frontend change (handoff), not shipped.
